feature.name: Authorizations and Authentications
feature.description: The feature defines the complete requirements for human Authorizations and Authentications that use '{env}.chathealthy.ai' and chathealthy.ai. The scope of this excludes how users in the Dev Ops pipelines and processes manage their entitlements and identities.

story.name: GUID â€” stable per-session auth credential
story.description: The stable 32-char session identifier carried inside the security token. Manufactured once per page session and preserved across every cross-service hop.

requirement.requirement: The session token MUST use a stable GUID that identifies the session for its lifetime. The GUID MUST NOT change between calls within the same session.
requirement.name: GUID is stable across all inter-service calls in a session

requirement.requirement: The GUID MUST be 16 bytes (128 bits) generated by the UUID version 4 algorithm (RFC 4122), rendered as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters with no separators.
requirement.name: GUID is 16 bytes

depends_on.reason: RFC 4122

story.name: NONCE â€” fresh-per-hop replay defense
story.description: The 17-char timestamp stamped freshly by every server on receive. Defends against replay per NIST 800-53 SC-23. Distinct from the GUID; only the nonce changes per hop.

requirement.requirement: The nonce (timestamps) MUST be regenerated fresh on every hop a token traverses: (1) the browser->SharedServices /gate hop on inbound traffic, and (2) every server-to-server inter-service call thereafter. The nonce MUST NOT be reused across hops. Every ChatHealthy component (SharedServices, FindCare, EvaluateCare) that receives a token MUST update the last_used timestamp in the nonce to prove it processed the token at that time. Reusing a nonce is a replay attack vector and fails NIST 800-53 SC-23 (Session Authenticity).
requirement.name: Nonce regenerated fresh on every hop - browser->/gate plus every server-to-server hop thereafter

requirement.requirement: The NONCE value displayed in the session-verification panel MUST reflect the most recent stamping done on behalf of the currently-owning service. Ownership belongs to the service whose UI the user is interacting with: FindCare drives the Left Panel; EvaluateCare or SharedServices drives the Right Panel. The contacted server for all browser traffic is always SharedServices /gate per EPIC-002-F-004-S-001; the displayed-owner is independent of the contacted gateway and is determined by which iframe holds the active view.
requirement.name: Displayed-service ownership determines which panel shows the most recent nonce stamp

requirement.requirement: The nonce field MUST be 35 bytes in the exact TimeByteOrder YYYYMMDDHHMMSSmmmXYYYYMMDDHHMMSSmmm - two UTC wall-clock timestamps in YYYYMMDDHHMMSSmmm format (17 bytes each: year 4, month 2, day 2, hour 2, minute 2, second 2, millisecond 3 bytes; ASCII digits, no separators) separated by a single literal uppercase ASCII 'X' pad character at byte position 18. The first 17 bytes are the original mint time; the pad 'X' is byte 18; the next 17 bytes are the most-recent restamp time.
requirement.name: Nonce is 35 bytes

requirement.requirement: Bytes 1-17 of the nonce field hold the original mint timestamp. Bytes 19-35 hold the most-recent restamp timestamp. Both values are identical at mint; the latter advances on each restamp while the former is preserved.
requirement.name: Nonce byte order: original 1-17, latest 19-35

story.name: Security Token â€” signed wire envelope
story.description: The wire object and its content exchanged between services: { origin, token (CH{nonce}{created}{guid}), signature, created_at, signed, server_env }. Binds the GUID and nonce under an RSA PKCS1v15 SHA256 signature by the current stamping origin.

requirement.requirement: Every session token used in a call between ChatHealthy components (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) MUST include an `origin` field whose value is the name of the originating service. The token's signature MUST be produced with that service's own private key. Any service receiving a token MUST verify the signature using the named origin's public certificate and MUST reject the token if the origin field does not match the signing key. Browser-facing token minting is governed exclusively by SharedServices /gate per EPIC-002-F-004-S-001 and is OUT OF SCOPE of this requirement.
requirement.name: Every server-to-server token signs with the sender's key and identifies its origin

requirement.requirement: Any session_token object returned over the wire MUST have its `origin` field set to the name of the service that produced THIS response object - distinct from the cryptographic signer of any embedded credentials. On browser-facing responses (all client traffic flows through SharedServices /gate per EPIC-002-F-004-S-001), the origin field MUST be "SharedServices". On server-to-server responses that include a session_token, the origin field MUST name the responding service. One service MUST NOT assert another's identity in this field.
requirement.name: Any token-bearing response self-identifies its sender in the origin field

requirement.requirement: Session token mutual authentication MUST pass for SharedServices. The same token FindCare created MUST be the same one SharedServices received.
requirement.name: Enforce SharedServices mutual auth using FindCare-created session token

requirement.requirement: Any call from FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices to one another MUST complete a mutual-authentication TLS 1.2+ handshake. A failed or incomplete handshake is a fatal error per EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-B-002.
requirement.name: Mutual-authentication TLS 1.2+ for FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices inter-service calls

requirement.requirement: For non-production environments (local, dev, qa), if session-token verification or mutual-authentication handshake (per EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-T-003) fails to complete or does not return a definitive VERIFIED/FAILED result within 30 seconds, the state is illegal. The UI MUST render a 'Fatal Error' splash in the center panel and display Verified: FAILED in the session verification panel. The UI MUST NOT display 'Pending' for longer than 30 seconds. In production, any runtime security-primitive failure MUST cause the hard process exit defined in EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-T-004.
requirement.name: Render Fatal Error splash if session authentication fails or times out in non-prod

requirement.requirement: On startup every server MUST exercise each security primitive it uses (session-token generation, signature signing and verification, credential redaction, mTLS handshake, key decryption, authentication check). If any exercise fails the process MUST exit with a non-zero code. A server MUST NOT serve any request after a failed startup exercise. Exit codes: 78 (configuration failure â€” missing library, missing cert, missing env var, malformed primitive output), 77 (permission denied on cert or key file), 70 (unexpected internal error). Stderr MUST name the primitive that failed.
requirement.name: Startup must test security primitives; exit on failure with specific codes

requirement.requirement: The session token display MUST separate the nonce from the GUID so a human can visually verify each part. The display MUST show: (1) Signed token (the encrypted signature), (2) Nonce (the two timestamps extracted from the token), (3) GUID (the session identifier extracted from the token). The nonce and GUID MUST be displayed as separate labeled fields. The presentation in the right panel (after EvaluateCare or SharedServices handoff) MUST be identical to the presentation in the left panel. Both panels MUST use the same labels, layout, and format.
requirement.name: Signed-token panel renders signed token, nonce, GUID as separate labeled fields, identical in both panels

requirement.requirement: All traffic MUST be HTTPS with mutual authentication.
requirement.name: All inter-service traffic uses mutual authentication over HTTPS

requirement.requirement: MUST comply with EPIC-002-F-003-S-001-REQ-T-002.
requirement.name: Comply with the GUID specification

requirement.requirement: The session-verification widget MUST display the time in UTC.
requirement.name: Time displayed in UTC
Session token byte assembly: GUID, first timestamp, X, second timestamp
requirement.requirement: The session token MUST be assembled in exactly this byte order: (1) the 32-character GUID per EPIC-002-F-003-S-001-REQ-T-002; (2) immediately followed by the 17-byte first timestamp; (3) immediately followed by a single literal uppercase ASCII 'X' character; (4) immediately followed by the 17-byte second timestamp. The two timestamps and their semantics are defined by EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-T-001, EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-T-002, and EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-B-002.

depends_on.reason: Defines the GUID (16 bytes, 32 hex chars).
Defines the two-timestamp nonce and its byte order.

story.name: Create and login users with OAuth across supported identity providers
story.description: ChatHealthy.ai MUST support the creation and use of identity-provider IDs (Google, Facebook, Apple, and others as introduced) for logins using each identity provider's OAuth capabilities. The firm and its application rely on identity providers as identity sources. This story specifies all the technical and business requirements for this capability.

requirement.name: Business statement (identical to the story)
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy.ai MUST support the creation and use of identity-provider IDs (Google, Facebook, Apple, and others as introduced) for logins using each identity provider's OAuth capabilities. The firm and its application rely on identity providers as identity sources. This story specifies all the technical and business requirements for this capability.

requirement.name: Playwright test of the Login & Registration sequence of screens and messages
requirement.requirement: A Playwright test script MUST execute the full Login & Registration sequence end to end and MUST assert each screen the user sees and each message presented in that sequence.

requirement.name: Login & Registration link in the static-site navigation
requirement.requirement: Every static page on the chathealthy.ai website MUST render a top-level navigation with exactly three links, in this left-to-right order: Home, Login & Registration, Products and Services.

requirement.name: Login click signals login_register intent and identity_provider to /gate
requirement.requirement: On a click of the Login & Registration link, the browser MUST POST to the SharedServices /gate endpoint with the request body carrying intent = "login_register" and an identity_provider field set to the operator-selected identity provider.

requirement.name: AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.run() routes to utterance or to a control use case
requirement.requirement: AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.run() MUST route each request into exactly one of two top-level paths: (a) the utterance path, or (b) the control path. Requests on the control path MUST identify a single control use case (for example, login_register) and MUST invoke the corresponding tool or process. An unrecognized path or an unknown control use case MUST cause a hard error.

requirement.name: login_register intent triggers OAuth at the selected identity provider
requirement.requirement: When AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.run() observes intent = "login_register", it MUST return a Response whose redirect_url field is the SharedServices /auth/<identity_provider>/start endpoint URL for the identity provider carried in the request.

requirement.name: /gate emits redirect event when AuthN returns redirect_url
requirement.requirement: When the AuthN Response carries a non-null redirect_url, the SharedServices /gate route MUST emit, as the terminal NDJSON event, a record of the shape {"type": "redirect", "url": <redirect_url>} and end the response.

requirement.name: Frontend follows redirect events
requirement.requirement: On any /gate NDJSON event of shape {"type": "redirect", "url": <string>}, the frontend consumer MUST call window.location.assign(<url>).

requirement.name: /auth/<identity_provider>/callback exchanges the authorization code
requirement.requirement: The SharedServices /auth/<identity_provider>/callback endpoint MUST receive the identity provider's authorization-code redirect, exchange the code with the identity provider's token endpoint, and obtain the identity provider's stable identifier (hereafter the identity-provider user ID) and the verified email claim.

requirement.name: Users collection stores user_objects, indexed on lookup keys
requirement.requirement: Each document in the users collection IS a UserObject conforming to the canonical schema at https://dev.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyUserStateSchema.json. The collection MUST maintain a unique index on user_id and multi-key indexes on OAuthIdentities.identity_provider_user_id and on OAuthIdentities.email so the OAuth callback can perform constant-time lookups.

requirement.name: Registration creates the users record
requirement.requirement: When no existing users record carries { identity_provider: <identity provider>, identity_provider_user_id: <identity-provider user ID> } in its OAuthIdentities AND no existing OAuthIdentities[].email matches the verified email returned by this callback, the SharedServices /auth/<identity_provider>/callback endpoint MUST create a new users record (a UserObject) with: user_id set to a freshly generated random GUID (RFC 4122 UUIDv4); OAuthIdentities set to exactly one entry { identity_provider: <identity provider>, identity_provider_user_id: <identity-provider user ID>, email: <identity-provider email> }; public_username set to the verified email returned by the identity provider (this default value may be changed by the user via a future story); is_registered = True; user_type = "Prospect".

requirement.name: Persist mirrors user_object to the users collection when is_registered == True
requirement.requirement: AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.persist() MUST, on every invocation, write the current user_object to admin.sessions (keyed by GUID). When the user_object's is_registered == True, persist() MUST ALSO write the same user_object to the users collection (keyed by user_id). The two writes MUST carry the same UserObject value.

requirement.name: On successful login notify the user and welcome new pre-alpha users
requirement.requirement: On a successful login notify the user that they are logged in. If they are new users, welcome them and state that ChatHealthy is glad to have them as pre-alpha users.

requirement.name: Returning OAuth login replaces the guest user_object with the DB user_object
requirement.requirement: On a successful OAuth callback whose OAuthIdentities lookup matches an existing user's { identity_provider, identity_provider_user_id }, the endpoint MUST reuse that record's existing user_id, MUST refresh that entry's email to the email returned by the identity provider on this callback, MUST re-set ChatHealthyRegisteredUserCookie per EPIC-002-F-003-S-006-REQ-T-004, MUST replace the current session's guest user_object with the stored UserObject, and MUST bind that stored UserObject to the current session.

requirement.name: UserObject defines OAuthIdentities, an array of identity-provider identities
requirement.requirement: The UserObject schema MUST define a field named OAuthIdentities of type array. Each array element MUST be an object with exactly three sub-fields: (a) identity_provider - the identity-provider name; the enum is open and includes each supported identity provider (initially "Google", with additional identity providers added as introduced); (b) identity_provider_user_id - the identity provider's stable identifier for the user; (c) email - the verified email returned by the identity provider on its most recent OAuth callback for this user. The array MUST be non-empty whenever is_registered == True.

requirement.name: On failed login explain pre-alpha state and how to request access
requirement.requirement: On a failed login explain that in this 'pre-alpha state' Google demands that ChatHealthy registers them as pre-alpha users, and ask them to email skip@chathealthy.ai, or text him at 01 (646) 408-8999.

requirement.name: Returning user welcome-back message with last-login timestamp
requirement.requirement: If a returning user logs in give them a 'Welcome back' message and tell them when they last logged in.

requirement.name: Returning login appends the guest conversation onto the stored user history
requirement.requirement: On a successful OAuth callback handled by EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-012, before the stored UserObject replaces the current session's guest UserObject, the endpoint MUST append the guest UserObject's session_conversation_history.utterances, session_conversation_history.ux_events, and session_conversation_history.unanswered_questions arrays to the corresponding arrays of the stored UserObject's session_conversation_history. The merged UserObject (stored history first, then the appended guest entries) MUST then be written to the users collection and bound to the current session.

requirement.name: Cross-identity-provider reconciliation via verified email
requirement.requirement: On every successful OAuth callback, the endpoint MUST first attempt to match (identity_provider, identity_provider_user_id) against any user_object.OAuthIdentities entry across the users collection. When that match succeeds, the returning-login path per EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-012 runs. Otherwise, the endpoint MUST attempt to match the verified email returned by this callback against any user_object.OAuthIdentities[].email. When that match succeeds, the endpoint MUST append { identity_provider, identity_provider_user_id, email } to that user's OAuthIdentities, re-set ChatHealthyRegisteredUserCookie per EPIC-002-F-003-S-006-REQ-T-004 with that user's existing user_id, replace the current session's guest user_object with the stored UserObject, and bind that stored UserObject to the current session. Otherwise, the registration path per EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-009 runs.

requirement.name: Pre-alpha authorized-registrant allow-list is hardcoded in application code
requirement.requirement: The pre-alpha allow-list of authorized registrants MUST be 100% hardcoded in the application code. No database collection, no env var, no manifest entry â€” to add or remove an authorized pre-alpha user the operator edits the code and redeploys.

requirement.name: OAuth Login Tool audits every attempted login and its result
requirement.requirement: The OAuth Login Tool must audit each attempted login and each result in the Shared Service application log. The gateway must not own this audit.

requirement.name: Failed authentication keeps user as guest without destroying or disclosing prior identity state
requirement.requirement: On a failed authentication, the system MUST keep the user as a guest, MUST tell the user that the authentication failed, and MUST NOT delete the user_object or the user's ChatHealthyRegisteredUserCookie. The user-facing message MUST NOT disclose that a cookie exists or any aspect of prior identity state.

story.name: User State
story.description: Defines the User State object â€” the in-session and post-session representation of a ChatHealthy user.

requirement.requirement: Every ChatHealthy session - Guest, Prospect, or Owner - MUST instantiate exactly one User State object on session start. For logged-in users this object comes from the admin.users collection but is stored in both the admin.sessions and admin.users collections on each server call.
requirement.name: Every session instantiates exactly one User State object

requirement.requirement: The structure of every User State document MUST conform to the JSON Schema published at https://dev.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyUserStateSchema.json. The schema is the canonical contract; any divergence between schema and implementation is an engineering bug.
requirement.name: Schema governs the User State document's structure
ch_session carries the session token; server surfaces time_remaining; client tracks it and pre-flights
requirement.requirement: Every SharedServices /gate response MUST (a) set a Secure, HttpOnly cookie named ch_session with Max-Age=300 whose value is the session token defined by EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-B-007, and (b) include in the response body a field named time_remaining_seconds whose integer value is the seconds remaining between the moment of response and the most-recent-restamp timestamp (bytes 19-35 of the nonce per EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-B-002) plus the 300-second TTL. The browser MUST store the most-recent time_remaining_seconds together with the local clock value at receipt, and MUST update that stored pair on every subsequent /gate response. Before issuing any SharedServices request the browser MUST compute the remaining time from that stored pair against its local clock and refuse to issue the request when the remaining time has elapsed. All browser-side reads and writes of any ChatHealthy.ai cookie MUST be performed by exactly one shared JavaScript file (served with Content-Type text/javascript) loaded by index.html; no other browser code, including inline scripts within index.html, may read or write any ChatHealthy.ai cookie.

depends_on.reason: Session-token assembly per REQ-B-007.
Most-recent-restamp timestamp per REQ-B-002.

requirement.name: /gate sets the ch_session cookie with the required attributes
requirement.requirement: Every SharedServices /gate response MUST include a Set-Cookie header that sets a cookie named exactly ch_session with attributes Secure, HttpOnly, Max-Age=300, SameSite=None, Domain=chathealthy.ai, Path=/gate.

requirement.name: The ch_session cookie value IS the session token
requirement.requirement: The value of the ch_session cookie set by /gate MUST be the 67-byte session token defined by EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-B-007.

depends_on.reason: REQ-B-007 defines the 67-byte session-token assembly.

requirement.name: /gate response body includes time_remaining_seconds
requirement.requirement: Every SharedServices /gate response body MUST include a top-level field named time_remaining_seconds whose value is a non-negative integer.

requirement.name: time_remaining_seconds value is computed from the nonce restamp
requirement.requirement: time_remaining_seconds MUST equal (most_recent_restamp_timestamp + 300 seconds) - server_response_instant, computed in UTC milliseconds and floored to whole seconds, where most_recent_restamp_timestamp is bytes 19-35 of the nonce per EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-B-002.

depends_on.reason: REQ-B-002 defines the restamp byte position (bytes 19-35).

requirement.name: Browser stores the most recent time_remaining_seconds with its receipt local-clock value
requirement.requirement: On every SharedServices /gate response the browser MUST store, in client-side state, the received time_remaining_seconds value together with the local clock value Date.now() at the moment of receipt, replacing any prior stored pair.

requirement.name: Browser pre-flights every SharedServices request against the stored pair
requirement.requirement: Before issuing any SharedServices request the browser MUST compute remaining = stored_time_remaining_seconds - (Date.now() - stored_receipt_clock) / 1000, and MUST refuse to issue the request when remaining <= 0.

requirement.name: /gate is POSTed on every page load
requirement.requirement: Every page load of any ChatHealthy.ai client surface MUST POST to the SharedServices /gate endpoint with op="boot" as the first network call. The page MUST receive that response and store the (time_remaining_seconds, Date.now()) pair per EPIC-002-F-003-S-005-REQ-T-005 before issuing any subsequent SharedServices request.

requirement.name: /gate error handling
requirement.requirement: When the browser receives an error response from SharedServices /gate (any HTTP 5xx, any HTTP 4xx other than an expected business error, or any malformed body), the browser MUST display the application's hard-fail error page with the text "authentication error from SharedServices". The SharedServices server side MUST log the error with full detail including the originating request, the exception class, and the full server-side stack trace.

requirement.name: Session-expired handling
requirement.requirement: When the browser's pre-flight check per EPIC-002-F-003-S-005-REQ-T-006 determines the session has expired, the browser MUST navigate the user to the home page. The user MUST be given a blank Guest user_object with no history from the just-expired session. In place of the usual splash the home page MUST render a "system timed out" notice. When the user was a registered user during the just-expired session the notice MUST read "system timed out: please log back in"; when the user was not a registered user during the just-expired session the notice MUST read "system timed out: please start again".

Set on a successful OAuth callback; carries only the ChatHealthy-minted user_id (the user_id top-level attribute of the admin.users record per EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-008).

requirement.name: Business statement

It is set on a successful OAuth callback.

feature.name: Universal Navigation
feature.description: The ChatHealthy.ai application guides users to find care, evaluate their choices objectively, and meet with their loved ones, care providers, and AI robots to discuss their options, and potentially get deep research based on their context. Users might be registered, guests, customers, or site administrators. The requirements for One Universal Navigation Mechanism are specified herein. Navigation takes place between an end user typing values into a prompt or using one of ChatHealthy's tools and corresponding UX component to do work such as picking providers, specialties, clinical trials, or tuning the mixing board in EvaluateCare. These requirements when met must, along with other controls, demonstrate ChatHealthy's compliance with NIST 800-53. I.e., they must meet the strictest requirements that any HIPAA audit might uncover.

story.name: Universal entrance: all ChatHealthy.ai client to server calls route through SharedServices /gate
story.description: The single client-facing endpoint for the entire ChatHealthy.ai application is SharedServices /gate. Every browser-initiated HTTP call from any ChatHealthy.ai surface - the wrapper site, embedded FindCare/EvaluateCare iframes, future mobile webviews, future native clients - funnels through this one endpoint. SharedServices performs any cross-component work server-to-server on behalf of the client.

requirement.name: All calls to ChatHealthy.ai MUST go to the ChatHealthy.ai Universal Gate
requirement.requirement: All browser, or other client, calls to ChatHealthy.ai servers MUST POST to {env}.sharedservices.chathealthy.ai/gate. Other calls to other URLs, except for the domain name by itself, MUST result in a 404; i.e., calls to http://chathealthy.ai, https://chathealthy.ai, http://dev.chathealthy.ai, https://dev.chathealthy.ai, http://qa.chathealthy.ai, https://qa.chathealthy.ai MUST all redirect to the universal gate call.

requirement.name: Skip already-completed upstream work on follow-up turns
requirement.requirement: When the Utterance Manager (UM) upgrades target_action on a follow-up turn because a pending_disambiguation just resolved, the Universal Router (UR) does not re-run any upstream tool whose result is already cached on the IntentDocument. UR reads the cached output from the relevant intent entry's arguments and dispatches only the downstream tool that still needs to run. Asking the user a clarification question therefore does not pay the cost of re-classifying or re-fetching upstream work the user has already seen.

depends_on.reason: Depends on UM's pending_disambiguation state per REQ-B-007 and REQ-B-009.

requirement.name: IntentDocument carries upstream tool outputs across turns
requirement.requirement: Each typed intent entry in the IntentDocument carries the outputs of upstream tools as additional arguments. The Universal Router (UR) writes these arguments after the upstream tool runs the first time and reads them on follow-up turns to satisfy REQ-B-002. The schema for each intent entry enumerates the upstream-output arguments it accepts so the contract between the Utterance Manager (UM), UR, and each consuming tool is explicit.

requirement.name: Serial wire order on partial-information turns
requirement.requirement: On a turn that carries both a user_message and a partial-information target_action, the wire order is deterministic. The Utterance Manager (UM) streams its {kind:"prompt"} event and awaits an event-loop tick to flush before returning to the Universal Router (UR). UR then dispatches downstream tools per target_action; each tool streams its own events and flushes before returning. UR emits its terminal {kind:"final"}. UR does not chain to closeConnection200 on a turn that carries a pending disambiguation, because the connection is logically still open across the user's next turn.

depends_on.reason: Depends on UM REQ-B-009 (user_message field) and REQ-B-010 (LLM authors prose).

requirement.name: Universal Router handles authentication by calling OAuthLoginTool directly
requirement.requirement: In order to support testing in the localhost environment, the Universal Router MUST handle the authentication flow by calling OAuthLoginTool directly. The Universal Router MUST NOT route the authentication flow through the UtteranceManager. This is the natural flow in all other environments.

story.name: Implement unique FindCare Universal Router requirements
story.description: This story specifies the Universal Router (UR) behavior that is specific to FindCare's two action types â€” findAProvider and specialtySearch â€” beyond what the general Universal Router story (EPIC-002-F-004-S-001) defines. It covers the SpecialtyFilter output as the cached upstream result carried as nucc_codes on each FindCare intent entry, the UR-side write and re-read of nucc_codes across turns so SpecialtyFilter does not run twice on the same complaint, and the schema sufficiency rule that gates UR dispatch of ProviderSearch so the provider search executes only when geography is fully specified. UR behavior shared with non-FindCare actions is out of scope for this story.

requirement.name: NUCC codes are the cached upstream result
requirement.requirement: For the findAProvider and specialtySearch actions, the SpecialtyFilter output is the cached upstream result that satisfies Universal Router (UR) REQ-B-003. The IntentDocument's IntentSpecialtySearch and IntentFindAProvider entries each carry an nucc_codes argument holding the SpecialtyFilter codes and their scores. UR writes nucc_codes after the first SpecialtyFilter run and reads it on the geography-resolution turn so SpecialtyFilter does not run twice on the same complaint.

depends_on.reason: Instantiates the cached-upstream-output pattern from REQ-B-002 and REQ-B-003.

requirement.name: ProviderSearch fires only when geography is sufficient
requirement.requirement: ProviderSearch executes only when target_action is findAProvider and the geography on the IntentFindAProvider entry passes the schema sufficiency rule â€” zip alone, state alone, state plus city, or state plus county. On any turn where the Utterance Manager (UM) holds target_action at specialtySearch because of pending geography disambiguation, ProviderSearch does not fire; the Universal Router (UR) streams the specialties event and the user_message event and emits its terminal final event without provider results.

feature.name: Utterance Tool
feature.description: This feature defines the requirements for the handling of every user interaction with ChatHealthy.ai's core front-end application that requires LLM-mediated routing or prose. The Utterance Manager (UM) has two responsibilities. (a) Interpret â€” when the user types free-text into the prompt, UM classifies the latest utterance, builds the canonical IntentDocument, and may author a user_message prompt the user back. This is the 'interpret an utterance' path. (b) Manufacture â€” when the user clicks a structured UI control (Apply Filter, future selected-for-evaluation gates, future pagination edges) that requires the system to ask the user something before it can act, the Universal Router (UR) dispatches UM with a synthetic trigger. UM reads the carried IntentDocument's slot state and authors a brief LLM-generated user_message requesting whatever slot is missing. No free-text utterance was typed; UM is manufacturing an utterance the system needs to deliver. Both paths end the same way: UM writes an IntentDocument back to user_object.intent, optionally streams user_message as kind:'prompt', and returns. UR validates and dispatches the resulting target_action. This feature is complete when every user-facing chat prose in the application is either (a) interpreted from a free-text utterance via path (a) or (b) manufactured by UM via path (b) â€” and no tool authors its own chat strings.

story.name: Universal utterance routing
story.description: The single canonical routing path for every user utterance from the input control through to the terminal user_object update. Holds the business rule that all utterances flow through this path and the technical contract for each hop in the path.

requirement.name: All user utterances must flow through the user-prompt tool
requirement.requirement: Every user prompt coming from any component, e.g. user-prompt input, where a user uses natural language to communicate with the app MUST flow through the UniversalNavigationTool to the UtteranceManager.

requirement.name: User object is the tool's input
requirement.requirement: The tool's input MUST be a User State object as canonically defined by EPIC-002-F-003 (Authorizations and Authentications).

depends_on.reason: Defines the canonical User State / User Object

requirement.name: Tool must be tightly coupled with a front end component
requirement.requirement: The tool MUST be tightly coupled with a front-end JS file that: (1) takes the input from the user and sends it to the universal router using the universal router's input pydantic tool as a JSON; if and only if the router determines that it was an utterance shall the router construct the pydantic object and pass it to the tool. The component MUST be capable of both transmitting the user's input and responding in text if further natural language input is required from the user.

depends_on.reason: Universal Navigation feature â€” defines the universal router

requirement.name: UtteranceManager obtains tool metadata from the router and caches it at runtime
requirement.requirement: UtteranceManager MUST obtain downstream-tool metadata from the universal router's metadata API. UtteranceManager MUST cache the retrieved metadata at runtime â€” the API call is for cache population on startup (or on cache invalidation), not a per-utterance lookup. The router's registry is the source of truth; UtteranceManager holds a runtime copy.

requirement.name: Universal utterance tool must be capable of doing multi-thread processing
requirement.requirement: The universal utterance tool must be capable of multi-threaded processing. It might make parallel calls to Mongo, and/or LLMs. Within that multithreaded environment, if required and one thread with precedence returns, the tool must be capable of calling on a tool prior to the other tools completing their activities.

requirement.name: Universal utterance round-trip path
requirement.requirement: Every utterance MUST complete the full round-trip path. Outbound: (1) user input enters at the user-prompt input; (2) front-end JS routes the utterance from client to server; (3) the universal router receives it on the server side; (4) the router constructs the User-object payload and dispatches to UtteranceManager; (5) UtteranceManager classifies and returns a decision: exactly one of two outcomes â€” (a) the name of a downstream registered tool to invoke (the safety tool, FindCare, EvaluateCare, or any other registered tool), or (b) a clarifying-question / feedback-request message to send back to the user; (6) on outcome (a), the universal router invokes the named downstream tool with the User-object payload. Inbound: (7) the resolved response â€” tool data or clarifying message â€” flows back through the universal router; (8) the router routes the response from server to the originating client; (9) the front-end JS receives it and renders to the user, completing the loop. No utterance may bypass UtteranceManager. UtteranceManager MUST NOT invoke downstream tools itself â€” only the universal router does. Every utterance MUST produce a delivered response.

requirement.name: Classifier input is the last N user utterances
requirement.requirement: The Utterance Manager (UM) classifier input is up to the last 10 user utterances drawn from user_object.session_conversation_history.utterances. The cap is a maximum, not a target â€” fewer turns are passed when the session has not accumulated that many. Tool-invocation entries and LLM-clarification bridge entries are excluded from the window so the classifier sees only what the human said.

requirement.name: Ambiguous-but-resolvable third action state
requirement.requirement: The Utterance Manager (UM) classifier distinguishes three states for any required action slot: sufficient, missing, and ambiguous-with-candidate. Ambiguous-with-candidate applies when the slot cannot be filled from the utterance alone but the classifier has a plausible candidate value for it. In this state UM sets target_action to the partial-information action so any work that does not depend on the missing slot can still proceed, records the candidate value as pending_disambiguation on the relevant intent entry, and emits an LLM-authored user_message proposing the candidate to the user.

requirement.name: Pending disambiguation resolved on the next turn
requirement.requirement: When the next utterance is a yes/no answer to the prior pending disambiguation, the Utterance Manager (UM) resolves it. "Yes" fills the candidate value into the appropriate argument on the IntentDocument and upgrades target_action to the now-fully-specified action. "No" keeps target_action at the partial-information action and emits a follow-up LLM-authored user_message requesting the missing slot a different way. Either outcome clears the prior pending_disambiguation.

requirement.name: IntentDocument carries disambiguation state and user-facing prose
requirement.requirement: The canonical IntentDocument has two optional fields beyond its required target_action and intents. The first is pending_disambiguation, attached per-intent on each entry in intents[], an object that captures the disambiguation kind, the candidate value being proposed, and any scaffolding the next-turn resolver needs; it persists across turns until the Utterance Manager (UM) clears it. The second is user_message, attached at the top level of the IntentDocument, a string carrying the LLM's prose intended for the user; when it is non-empty UM streams it as {kind:"prompt", data:{text: user_message}} and flushes before returning to the Universal Router (UR), when it is absent UM streams nothing.

requirement.name: LLM authors all user-facing chat prose
requirement.requirement: The Utterance Manager (UM) classifier's structured output includes a user_message field. The LLM writes every user-facing chat line â€” clarification questions, follow-ups, friendly framing, error explanations â€” and UM streams whatever the LLM produced. No hardcoded clarification or chat string appears in UM, NonsenseTool, CloseConnection200Tool, or any other component on the dispatch path. The LLM owns the prose; the runtime owns the transport.

requirement.name: Classifier prompt corrects significant misspellings or asks when uncertain
requirement.requirement: If a spelling error is significant to understanding an utterance, the Utterance Manager classifier prompt MUST treat user-typed misspellings as a first-class case. For each suspected significant misspelling: if the classifier is at least 75% confident of the intended word, it MUST substitute the corrected form into the output fields (e.g. complaint, geography.city, geography.state, geography.county etc.) and proceed with the normal classification rules. On the same turn the classifier MUST populate BOTH (a) a structured corrections[] list on its output containing one {"original": <user-typed word>, "corrected": <corrected word>} entry per substitution applied, AND (b) user_message set to the user's full corrected utterance with each correction annotated inline in the form <corrected_word> (corrected from '<original>') using straight single quotes. The two outputs MUST be consistent: every corrections[] entry MUST appear in user_message as a (corrected from '...') marker and vice versa. The frontend uses the corrections[] list (not text-parsing of user_message) to identify and render each marker in red font, so the user sees that their spelling was interpreted, not ignored. If confidence is below 75%, the classifier MUST NOT guess; it MUST set target_action="closeConnection200" and emit a brief user_message naming up to three plausible candidates and asking the user to clarify; corrections[] MUST be empty in that case.

requirement.name: User utterances MUST NOT propagate a fatal exception
requirement.requirement: No user utterance â€” regardless of content, length, language, malformedness, ambiguity, or spelling â€” CAN cause the Utterance Manager to propagate a fatal application exception to the user. The classifier MUST always produce a valid IntentDocument with a usable target_action (typically closeConnection200 with a brief friendly clarification when no other action can be derived). No exception within the Utterance Manager tool can throw. Any unhandled exception inside UM MUST be caught within the UM tool and converted to an appropriate user message.

requirement.name: UtteranceManager does not handle the authentication flow
requirement.requirement: The UtteranceManager MUST NOT handle the authentication flow. This is an explicit exception per EPIC-002-F-004-S-001-REQ-B-005.

depends_on.reason: Anchors the explicit exception cited by this requirement.

story.name: Implement unique FindCare Utterance Manager requirements
story.description: This story specifies the Utterance Manager (UM) behavior that is specific to FindCare's two action types â€” findAProvider and specialtySearch â€” beyond what the general Utterance Manager story (EPIC-002-F-010-S-001) defines. It covers the geography slot as the ambiguous-but-resolvable disambiguation slot when the user names a city or county without a state, the UM-side handling of the corresponding pending_disambiguation marker on the IntentDocument's findAProvider intent entry, and the LLM-authored user_message proposing the candidate state to the user. UM behavior shared with non-FindCare actions (nonsense, closeConnection200) is out of scope for this story.

requirement.name: Geography slot is the disambiguation slot for findAProvider
requirement.requirement: For the findAProvider action, the geography slot uses the general ambiguous-but-resolvable pattern defined in Utterance Manager (UM) REQ-B-007. When the SpecialtyFilter has produced NUCC codes but UM has only a city or county without state, the IntentDocument's IntentFindAProvider entry carries the candidate state on pending_disambiguation, target_action remains at specialtySearch so the filter still renders, and UM proposes the candidate via user_message.

depends_on.reason: Instantiates the general ambiguous-but-resolvable pattern from REQ-B-007 and the schema additions from REQ-B-009.

requirement.name: Apply Filter with insufficient geography routes through UM as a manufacture turn
requirement.requirement: When UR receives op='apply_filter' with a payload containing the new nucc_codes set, UR reads the carried IntentDocument's geography from user_object.intent. If geography is sufficient (per the same sufficiency rule findAProvider applies â€” zip, state, state+city, or state+county), UR builds the IntentDocument deterministically with target_action=findAProvider using the new nucc_codes set, and dispatches ProviderSearch without calling UM. If geography is insufficient, UR populates a manufacture_utterance_reason dict with at minimum gesture='apply_filter' and missing_slot='geography', optionally adds session-derived facts (prior complaint, prior partial geography candidate, etc.) it deems useful, and dispatches UM as a manufacture-trigger Request per EPIC-002-F-010-S-003-REQ-T-001. UR does NOT specify the prose; UM authors it per EPIC-002-F-010-S-003-REQ-B-003.

depends_on.reason: Depends on the manufacture-trigger Request schema (REQ-T-001), the always-end-in-closeConnection200 rule (REQ-B-002), and the context-sensitive prose rule (REQ-B-003).

story.name: Manufacture utterances for non-free-text triggers
story.description: Defines UM's manufacture-path responsibility. When UR receives a structured UI gesture instead of a free-text utterance, UR dispatches UM with a synthetic trigger Request carrying a structured manufacture_utterance_reason â€” a set of hardcoded, non-user-facing facts UR has assembled about why a manufactured utterance is needed (e.g., gesture='apply_filter', missing_slot='geography', plus any session-state facts UR thinks relevant). UM uses a distinct, narrower prompt template that takes those facts AND the prior dialogue from session_conversation_history and authors a brief user-facing user_message sensitive to the conversational context â€” NOT a phrase the operator could have hardcoded. UM then morphs the IntentDocument's target_action to closeConnection200 (the user-facing prose is the answer for this turn; the user's next free-text utterance comes back through the interpret path and resolves any pending slot via the normal disambiguation mechanism). The manufacture prompt is distinct from the classifier prompt and is governed by its own output schema constraints.

requirement.name: UM accepts two trigger types
requirement.requirement: UM's Request shape carries a discriminator field trigger_type with values 'utterance' (the free-text classifier path) and 'manufacture' (the manufacture path). When trigger_type='utterance' UM reads the latest person utterance from user_object.session_conversation_history and runs the classifier prompt as today. When trigger_type='manufacture' UM does NOT read free-text; it reads the synthetic trigger context off the Request and runs the manufacture prompt. UM's Response shape is unchanged â€” an IntentDocument written to user_object.intent.

requirement.name: Manufacture path uses a distinct prompt template that always ends in closeConnection200
requirement.requirement: The manufacture prompt is narrower than the classifier prompt: it does not classify intents (the manufacture trigger and reason already name the intent context), it authors a brief user-facing user_message responsive to the supplied manufacture_utterance_reason and the prior dialogue. Hardcoded chat strings remain forbidden everywhere; the LLM authors all manufacture-path user_message text. After authoring the user_message, UM MUST set target_action=closeConnection200 on the emitted IntentDocument â€” the manufactured utterance IS the turn's answer; UR closes the connection and the user's next free-text utterance returns through the interpret path. The IntentDocument's intents[] array may carry forward intent entries (e.g. cached nucc_codes, partial geography, pending_disambiguation markers) so the next-turn interpret path can resolve naturally; only the target_action is constrained.

depends_on.reason: Builds on the LLM-authored-prose rule (REQ-B-010) and the IntentDocument shape (REQ-B-009).

requirement.name: Manufactured user_message must be context-sensitive, not formulaic
requirement.requirement: The manufacture path EXISTS because the user-facing prose is too context-dependent to hardcode. UM's manufacture prompt MUST consult the prior dialogue (recent transcript window) AND the manufacture_utterance_reason facts together when authoring the user_message. The result must read as a natural continuation of the conversation, not as a generic templated phrase. A prose output that ignores prior dialogue and could have been hardcoded in UR is a regression on this REQ â€” the whole reason the path is LLM-mediated is that UR cannot author this prose deterministically.

requirement.name: Synthetic trigger Request schema
requirement.requirement: The synthetic-trigger Request carries: trigger_type='manufacture', manufacture_utterance_reason: dict[str, Any] (UR-populated structured facts; keys are fact names â€” at minimum gesture and missing_slot, plus any additional context UR wants UM to consider; values are JSON-serialisable scalars or lists; none of this dict is user-facing). Future gestures and slots are added by populating new keys; the Request shape is stable. The IntentDocument that UR passes through user_object.intent is the carried session state UM reads alongside the reason dict.

epic.description: This epic defines all of the services that are shared by the ChatHealthy.AI runtime application used by consumers, and site administrators. This includes functional shared services such as universal navigation services, security services, safety services, etc.

epic.name: ChatHealthy FrontEnd libary
epic.description: Shared Python library distributed as the pip package `chathealthy-frontend-lib` (repo root: `FrontEndApplicationLib/`). Owns the code consumed in common by ChatHealthy.ai's front-end-facing services (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) and the wrapper. Scope is FRONT-END application code only â€” devops, data pipelines, and analytics are explicitly out of scope. Operating-model intent: a separate team with its own P&L manages this library; consumers depend on it via versioned releases (`pip install chathealthy-frontend-lib==X.Y.Z`) following standard industry convention for shared libraries, including the boundary that the package mints no auth tokens â€” auth-token MANUFACTURE belongs 100% to SharedServices; only auth-token MANAGEMENT (verification, parsing, nonce advancement) is shared and lives here.

feature.name: Shared front-end UX widget library
feature.description: Distribution mechanism + source-of-truth for the display-only UX widgets currently inlined in Website/index.html and the FindCare React iframe. Includes the chFatalError full-screen overlay, the non-prod env banner, the non-prod security panel (right-side rightSecurity panel), and any future widget shared by more than one front-end consumer. The library carries NO business logic â€” peer selection, mutual-auth pairing, service routing, ownership state, and any other biz-logic concerns are explicitly excluded and live in the backend per the no-biz-logic-on-client rule. Distribution channel TBD (npm package, CDN-hosted versioned bundle, or repo-internal copy at deploy time) â€” to be decided as part of the first story under this feature. Owned by the same EPIC-003 team that owns chathealthy-frontend-lib (Python).

feature.name: Backend orchestration that supports the shared front-end UX widgets
feature.description: Backend endpoints + service-layer code that own all the business logic that today lives inline in Website/index.html and the FindCare React iframe â€” peer selection (which backend's /health to call), mutual-auth pairing (the /session-then-/verify-token sequence currently driven from the wrapper), service-routing/ownership-state (gotoFindCare/gotoEvaluateCare/gotoSharedServices and the underlying ownership transition), and any other biz-logic decision the wrapper is making today. The widgets in EPIC-003-F-001 then become pure display: each widget consumes ONE clean data endpoint per render. This feature exists so that the no-biz-logic-on-client rule can actually be enforced; without it, extracting widgets only relocates the violation, not removes it. Per the auth caveat, token MANUFACTURE belongs 100% to SharedServices and any orchestration here MUST respect that boundary.
realized_by: sharedServices/Code/ (likely host of the orchestration endpoints)

feature.name: Manage Errors
feature.description: This feature defines the requirements to manage errors that the ChatHealthy.ai's application code encounters. It defines a unified deliberate-exception model across the ChatHealthy.ai codebase. Every exception explicitly managed shares an exception class â€” ChatHealthyException. This exception class has a mode discriminator and structured context dict. Catch sites discriminate on mode, not on exception type. External exceptions (httpx, pymongo, etc.) remain as their native types and are converted to ChatHealthyException at well-defined boundaries. The default behavior is and remains, when an exception occurs, fail hard and fast. But that policy is mitigated by the need to handle expected errors from users and external systems gracefully.

story.name: Use only the ChatHealthyException when deliberately throwing exceptions within the code base.
story.description: Establishes the foundational rule and the implementation that realizes it. Defines ChatHealthyException in chathealthy-frontend-lib, specifies the constructor contract (mode discriminator + message for logging + context dict), mandates the substitution at every existing deliberate-raise site in our authored code, and adds a pre-commit gate that rejects new raises of forbidden built-in exception types in our modules. The first mode the substrate uses is llm_unavailable, introduced by the LLM facade with context {provider, call_site, attempts}. Additional modes (compliance violations, geography insufficient, db unreachable, rate limited, etc.) land as the operator approves their definitions; the substrate accepts them without code change at the catch sites.

requirement.name: ChatHealthyException class definition
requirement.requirement: The chathealthy-frontend-lib package MUST define a class ChatHealthyException that inherits from the standard library Exception. The constructor signature is (mode: str, message: str, **context). Message is used for logging, and not for end user communications. Context is a dict; its keys vary by mode. The instance exposes attributes mode (str), message (str), context (dict), and exception (Exception â€” the original wrapped exception, when ChatHealthyException is being raised as a boundary conversion of an external library exception; None when this is an originating raise from our own code). The class lives at a stable import path within the package so every consumer service can import it.

requirement.name: Exhaustive use rule for deliberate raises in our authored code
requirement.requirement: Every deliberate raise of an exception authored in ChatHealthy.ai repository code MUST use ChatHealthyException with an appropriate mode discriminator. Use of built-in Python exception types (ValueError, RuntimeError, AssertionError, TypeError, KeyError) in deliberate raises authored by our code is forbidden. Re-raises of external exceptions (e.g. httpx.RemoteProtocolError, pymongo.errors.*) preserve the original type and the call stack of the original exception, so that logging of the exception becomes the duty of the exception class and not the code that creates the exception.

requirement.name: Boundary conversion rule for external-library exceptions
requirement.requirement: External-library exceptions MAY be converted to ChatHealthyException at defined system boundaries. The LLM facade (EPIC-003-F-003-S-001-REQ-B-007 below) is one such boundary. When such a conversion happens, the exception object MUST log the original exception with full traceback for operator forensic value before raising the new ChatHealthyException, so the original failure is not lost.

requirement.name: Catch-side discrimination on mode
requirement.requirement: Code that catches ChatHealthyException SHOULD discriminate on the mode attribute, not on isinstance against new exception subclasses (there are no subclasses). The mode taxonomy is the design surface for discriminating failure shapes. Catch sites that need to handle several modes use an explicit conditional on exc.mode.

requirement.name: Mode taxonomy lives in the feature's design doc
requirement.requirement: The set of valid modes is documented in the feature's architecture design doc under FrontEndApplicationLib/architectureAndDesign/. Adding a new mode is a design-doc edit that the operator approves, not a code-only change. Code that raises with an undocumented mode MAY be rejected by a future enforcement gate (out of scope for this story).

requirement.name: Pre-commit gate forbids new deliberate raises of built-in types
requirement.requirement: A new engineering rule (Rule-NNN, operator picks the number) MUST gate pre-commit. The worker scans every staged Python file under ChatHealthy.ai's authored directories (sharedServices/, FindCare/, evaluateCare/, Code/, FrontEndApplicationLib/, architecture/) and rejects any line matching a deliberate raise of ValueError, RuntimeError, AssertionError, KeyError, TypeError. Exempted: re-raises with no expression, test files asserting expected behavior, and external-library calls that we do not author. Forbidden raises in existing code at the moment the rule lands are tracked as orphan-fix items; the rule rejects only NEW commits that introduce additional violations until the historical backlog is migrated.

requirement.name: LLM facade boundary defines the first concrete mode llm_unavailable
requirement.requirement: The LLM call facade in chathealthy-frontend-lib catches transient HTTP errors (httpx.RemoteProtocolError, httpx.ConnectError, httpx.ReadTimeout, httpx.WriteTimeout, httpx.PoolTimeout) from the underlying pydantic-ai Agent.run call and, after the retry policy is exhausted, raises ChatHealthyException(mode='llm_unavailable', provider=<str>, call_site=<str>, attempts=<int>). UR catches this exception in _handle_utterance and re-dispatches to UM as a manufacture-trigger Request whose manufacture_utterance_reason carries the same context, so UM authors a user-facing message via the existing manufacture pattern. If the manufacture call itself raises ChatHealthyException, that exception propagates to UR's outermost catch and the existing fatal path fires; the operator sees the failure via telemetry and the user sees chFatalError. This three-rung ladder (transient blip covered by retry, sustained-recoverable covered by manufacture dialogue, truly-down covered by fatal) is the substrate.

requirement.name: Exception Management Modes
requirement.requirement: Every catch site that catches a ChatHealthyException MUST classify the caught exception into exactly one of three modes and act accordingly. Mode 1 â€” expected and easily handled (retry, fallback, alternate path): catcher logs at INFO with the if_debug flag set so the record is emitted only when in debug; caller continues via the recovery mechanism; user sees nothing. Mode 2 â€” expected and probably attributable to user error OR to a resource temporarily unavailable: catcher logs at ERROR (always emitted, no debug gate), surfaces an appropriate user-facing message describing the problem, and does NOT return HTTP 503. Mode 3 â€” unhandled, NOT expected (a bug): the safety-net @app.exception_handler returns HTTP 503 to the user and logs the unhandled exception so we can track it down and fix it; Mode 3 is the ONLY case where the user sees an HTTP 503; the architectural goal is for Mode 3 occurrences to be RARE â€” every observed Mode 3 instance MUST become a local catch with Mode 1 or Mode 2 handling. Throw-side rule: when a catch site converts a library exception (httpx, pymongo, etc.) into a ChatHealthyException, that site MUST clean up the underlying resource (close the connection / cursor / file handle, abort the request, release the pool slot, etc.) before raising the ChatHealthyException, so a leaked resource does not produce a delayed second failure (e.g., a 100-second-later timeout from a connection that was never closed).

feature.name: Manage Database Connections
feature.description: All database client instantiation from any ChatHealthy.ai service routes through a single shared library utility that owns connection lifecycle, service identity (appname), timeout policy, and connection-related logging.

story.name: Manage MongoDB Connections
story.description: ChatHealthyMongoUtilities (lives at FrontEndApplicationLib/src/chathealthy_frontend_lib/mongo_utilities.py) is the canonical entry point for obtaining a MongoClient. Every live service path uses it. Direct MongoClient(...) instantiation outside the utility itself is forbidden and enforced at pre-commit via Rule-004.

requirement.name: Canonical Mongo client provider exists
requirement.requirement: A class named ChatHealthyMongoUtilities MUST exist at FrontEndApplicationLib/src/chathealthy_frontend_lib/mongo_utilities.py and serve as the canonical Mongo client provider for every ChatHealthy.ai service.

requirement.name: Zero-parameter constructor, environment-sourced configuration
requirement.requirement: The constructor takes zero parameters. The utility sources connection coordinates and service identity from runtime environment configuration without caller input.

requirement.name: Process-wide singleton client
requirement.requirement: The utility maintains a process-wide singleton MongoClient. Repeated instantiation of ChatHealthyMongoUtilities returns the same underlying client and connection pool.

requirement.name: getConnection() is the single public method
requirement.requirement: getConnection() is the single public method. It returns the MongoClient. Callers select their own database and collection from the returned client.

requirement.name: Default operation timeout
requirement.requirement: The utility sets timeoutMS on the MongoClient per the CSOT (Client-Side Operation Timeout) policy, with default value 15000ms.

requirement.name: Per-call overrides use pymongo's native context manager
requirement.requirement: Per-call timeout overrides are performed by the calling code using pymongo's native `with pymongo.timeout(seconds):` context manager. The utility does NOT expose a wrapper API for timeout overrides.

requirement.name: Direct MongoClient instantiation forbidden outside the utility
requirement.requirement: Direct MongoClient(...) instantiation in any ChatHealthy.ai-authored Python file is forbidden except within FrontEndApplicationLib/src/chathealthy_frontend_lib/mongo_utilities.py itself.

requirement.name: Logging is governed by uniform application logging
requirement.requirement: The utility's logging surface is governed by EPIC-008-F-011-S-005 (Uniform application logging).

depends_on.reason: Logging surface is governed by the uniform application logging story.

requirement.name: Explicit per-call batch_size override on library find()
requirement.requirement: The ChatHealthyMongoUtilities Mongo wrapper SHALL expose batch_size as an explicit named keyword parameter on its find() method, with default value None. When batch_size is None the library MUST NOT pass any batch_size to pymongo (pymongo default applies). When the caller sets batch_size to an integer, the library MUST forward that integer to pymongo. The library MUST NOT impose a default batch_size for any caller, MUST NOT cache or persist a batch_size across calls, and MUST NOT infer a batch_size from collection size or call history. Choosing to override batch_size is a per-call caller decision. Compliance test: a pytest configures the canonical logging service to DEBUG, calls find() with batch_size set to a known integer, then reads the configured log destination and asserts the captured mongo.find START line includes the batch_size kwarg verbatim. The same pytest also asserts that omitting batch_size results in a START line that does NOT include batch_size in opts.

feature.name: Manage logging

story.name: Manage logging using Python's logging library

ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's logging module. logging.basicConfig(), logging.getLogger(), and print() MUST NOT appear in ChatHealthy.ai code. Pre-commit Rule-005 MUST enforce this.

requirement.name: logging.basicConfig(), logging.getLogger(), and print() are forbidden in ChatHealthy.ai code

requirement.name: Default log level and destination come from environment variables

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's standard library logging module.

requirement.name: All log messages, including 3rd-party library logs, write to the same log file

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's standard library logging module.

requirement.name: One log file per ChatHealthy component
requirement.requirement: There MUST be one log file per ChatHealthy component (FindCareServer, EvaluateCareServer, SharedServices, etc.). ChatHealthyLoggingService MUST select the file based on the component the process is running.

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's standard library logging module.

requirement.name: Application MUST NOT be disrupted by rotating or deleting the log file
requirement.requirement: The application MUST continue uninterrupted when its log file is archived, renamed, or deleted by an external process. Managing rotation or archival is out of scope. Implementation hint: changing the value of the log-destination environment variable is a valid way to point the application at a new file.

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's standard library logging module.

requirement.name: Logger renders ChatHealthyException with all attributes and both stack traces
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthyLoggingService MUST recognize ChatHealthyException at log time and render every attribute - mode, message, component, server, context - together with a full stack trace of both the wrapped original `exception` (when present) and the ChatHealthyException itself, in a single log entry. The exception argument passed to ChatHealthyLoggingService log methods (exc_info=, or the implicit current exception captured by log.exception() inside an except block) MUST be a ChatHealthyException; passing a non-ChatHealthyException exception is forbidden.

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyException class and contract (Manage Errors story).
Exception rendering policy lives in the Manage Errors design.
ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's standard library logging module.

requirement.name: Per-call debug gate - opt-in conditional emission
requirement.requirement: Every log call to a ChatHealthyLoggingService logger MUST accept an optional parameter (working name `if_not_debug_log` - final name TBD). The parameter's default value MUST be False: when omitted, the call MUST be a no-op unless debug mode is on. When explicitly set to True, the call emits as a normal log call subject to standard level filtering. The flag MUST NOT alter the severity stamped on records that DO emit: logger.info(msg, if_not_debug_log=True) MUST emit at INFO level when debug mode is on, not DEBUG. "Debug mode is on" is defined as: the effective log level of the receiving logger is DEBUG (or lower) - equivalently, the same logger would emit a DEBUG-level record.

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's standard library logging module.

requirement.name: Code that throws ChatHealthyException MUST NOT log; the catcher logs
requirement.requirement: In any ChatHealthy.ai-authored Python function or method whose body contains a `raise ChatHealthyException(...)` statement, no call to ChatHealthyLoggingService log methods (debug, info, warning, error, critical, exception) MUST appear in the same function/method body. The catch site (the function that handles the raised exception) is where the log occurs. Pre-commit Rule-005 MUST enforce this.

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyException class and contract (Manage Errors story).

feature.name: Specialty Filter
feature.description: Filter search results by specialty type, prescriber status, and homeopathic status. The term 'Homeopathic' in this feature refers to a Homeopathic provider â€” it is not a new classification and is not an umbrella label for the broader CAM/holistic/integrative-medicine set. Six-story decomposition: Display Specification, Present Initial Filter, User Manages Filter, User Submits Filter, API Surface and Contracts, Test Coverage.

story.description: How the SpecialtyFilter LOOKS and behaves end-to-end as a panel. Anchors the comprehensive UX description that S-002, S-003, and S-004 reference.

requirement.requirement:
The header uses a light green background. {find actual coded RGB value, or the term the CSS style sheet uses}
It is divided into three rows: a title row, a 'count' row, and a 'controls' row.
The title row says 'Choose Specialties'.
The Count row has 3 values where the label for each value is over the actual value. From left to right, the three values are:
"All possible": composed of the count of all the specialty types that can give care to the user based on the question they asked. This is regardless of whether or not a provider is available within the geographic boundary established by the user's question. In this group a specialty type must have a license but might not be homeopathic, or be able to prescribe.
"All prescribers": the total number of specialty types from 'All possible' that are legally allowed to write prescriptions. This includes, for example, Nurse Practitioners, and is not limited to physicians.
"Your choices": all the specialty types that the user has chosen. They might for example click the uncheck button and then check three specialties; in that case the number would be 3.
Macro Controls
The third row has three controls: a button 'Uncheck all' and two checkboxes 'Prescribers' and 'Homeopathic'. The two checkboxes are stacked vertically whereas the Uncheck button takes up the entire vertical space in this row. The controls in this header row do NOT determine what is submitted when Apply Filter is clicked â€” the only criterion for what gets submitted is the list of checked specialties. The header controls affect that checked-list state, but their purpose is to control which specialties are checked or presented; they are not intended to control what is done when Apply Filter is applied. The behavior of these controls is:
Uncheck All
"Uncheck all": this button unchecks any specialty type that is checked. Each time it is clicked it does this. If there are no specialties checked this button is greyed out, and a tool tip says, 'No specialties are checked'.
Additional requirement
When fewer than 50% of the rows are unchecked, the button's label reads 'Check All'. When it is in this state, the action is to check all specialties.
Prescribers
The list of checked specialists will have a particular state prior to the user clicking the Prescribers checkbox.
For all prescribers, Homeopathic and others, if the checkbox is unchecked it gets checked. If it is checked it remains checked.
For all non-prescribers, Homeopathic and non-Homeopath, if their checkbox is unchecked or checked, after this box is checked, the box becomes unchecked.
Homeopathic
The list of checked specialists will have a particular state prior to the user clicking the 'Homeopathic' checkbox.
For all Homeopathic specialties that treat this disorder specifically, if their checkbox is unchecked it gets checked. If it is checked it remains checked.
For all non-Homeopathic, prescribers or non-prescribers, if their checkbox is unchecked or checked, after this box is checked, the box becomes unchecked.
Additional behavior:
The result set returned to this list upon initialization will have two lists.
List one includes Homeopath specialties that specifically treat the class of problem that the user presented to the engine.
List two includes all homeopathic specialties in this area or generalists that can treat this type of problem. The server will try to eliminate non-logical choices such as midwives to treat erectile dysfunction or gerontologists to treat a child.
From a UX perspective there is only one list.
Scrollbar behavior
If there are more than 10 (configurable) then they are in a scroll bar, but all are available if the user scrolls.
Each specialty has on its right a checkbox. By default, all are checked. A user can check or uncheck any specialty. And they can click the Uncheck all button to remove all from being checked. This is going to be a typical behavior; user unchecks all and then checks some.
"Apply Filter" button: at the bottom of the control is a button labeled 'Apply Filter'. The scope of what gets applied is the specific specialties that are checked from the list of specialties. What is done with the controls in the header is not relevant to what specialties are submitted. Their purpose is to control which are checked or presented. They are not intended to control what is done when Apply Filter is applied. If any changes to the list of checked specialties have been made, then when this button is clicked:
A list of providers (the default list) will be in the center panel. Below that, potentially some providers might have been selected.
The provider list subject to selection but not selected shall be turned 'white' i.e. no records shall show.
A timer identical to the one that accompanied the original search shall be presented.
The selected provider window shall remain as is.
The prompt shall be available to the user.
The timer next to the prompt shall also show.
Middle-screen behavior on Apply Filter (per Skip clarification on the 'default list' / preservation question): the entire middle screen MUST be preserved as is from a business perspective. Specifically: the user's question is repainted; the Available Provider list is repainted; the Selected-for-evaluation panel never went away; the Prompt and 'send' never went away. Fine-grained technical requirements may be crafted from this baseline.
Timers (per Skip clarification): there are two timers. One timer is shown immediately to the LEFT of the user-prompt input box. The second timer is on the main screen. The main-screen timer is correct on Apply Filter except that the user's selected providers panel must be preserved (per the middle-screen-behavior clarification above). The prompt-adjacent timer is correct as is.
If no changes to the filter have been made (changes meaning new checks have been made) then the button will not be hot but greyed out, and if a user clicks the button a non-modal popup with an 'OK' button must say: 'There are no changes to apply, try a new prompt if this is the wrong list. The AI agent will help you craft the right question' and no other action will be taken.
Cache Results on client: in order to enhance performance and in contradiction to the general requirement that all business logic must be done in ChatHealthy's servers in the data center, the list of specialists MUST be cached on the client. Each time a new list of specialists is produced by the FindCare server the entire cache content must be replaced with the new list of specialties.
