requirement.requirement: When the panel is initially populated, every returned specialty's checkbox is in the CHECKED state. The user unchecks from a fully-selected starting point.
requirement.name: Default checkbox state for every returned specialty is CHECKED

requirement.requirement: The specialty list MUST include complementary, alternative, and integrative medicine (CAM) practitioners â€” Acupuncturist, Naturopath, Naprapath, Homeopath, Mechanotherapist, Chiropractor, Massage Therapist, and any other CAM type â€” whenever clinically relevant to the user's request. CAM practitioners MUST NOT be deprioritized, downweighted, or excluded on the basis of being CAM. Per the feature-level clarification, the user-facing 'Homeopathic' checkbox refers to a Homeopathic provider only; it is not an umbrella toggle for the full CAM set and does not introduce a new classification. The master comprehensive UX in EPIC-006-F-002-S-001-REQ-B-001 governs the per-checkbox behavior.
requirement.name: List MUST include licensed CAM practitioners when clinically relevant

requirement.requirement: The specialty list MUST NOT include unlicensed roles such as Homemaker, Driver, Religious Nonmedical Practitioner, Lay Midwife, Doula, Health & Wellness Coach, Health Educator, Lactation Consultant Non-RN, Peer Specialist, Community Health Worker, Case Manager, or Reflexologist. The list MUST NOT include any specialty that is not licensed in at least one US state or Puerto Rico. (Reflexologist exception/inconsistency surfaced as an open issue at the top of this document for Skip to explore.)
requirement.name: List MUST NOT include unlicensed roles or specialties not licensed in any state or Puerto Rico

requirement.requirement: The specialty list MUST NOT include hospitals, laboratories, pharmacies, supplier organizations, transportation services, residential treatment facilities, managed care organizations, agencies, group practices, or any other non-individual entity. Only individual licensed human practitioners belong in the list.
requirement.name: List MUST NOT include institutions, facilities, agencies, or non-individual entries

requirement.requirement: An AI query or queries MUST be made in order to extract the list of specialties from the user's input. This AI query or queries MUST be wrapped in one tool with precise input and output so that the users of the tool are 100% encapsulated from its implementation details. Encapsulation does not constrain how many internal AI calls the tool makes â€” the multi-stage pipeline described in S-002-REQ-T-007 through S-002-REQ-T-012 is implementation detail INSIDE the tool's encapsulated boundary and is not visible at the tool boundary. The Pydantic schema for the tool input and output MUST be approved by a human.
requirement.name: AI tool encapsulates specialty extraction; Pydantic schema human-approved

requirement.requirement: The user's vernacular request is passed to an LLM normalize call using the system prompt registered at prompts.json[_record_id = 'specialty_normalize_system_prompt'].
requirement.name: AI normalize step uses prompts.json record

requirement.requirement: The normalize step's output is embedded using the canonical embedding model declared at EPIC-008-F-011-S-004-REQ-B-001.
requirement.name: Embed normalize output with the canonical embedding model

requirement.requirement: The embedded vector queries SpecialtyMetaData via MongoDB Atlas $vectorSearch with the filter Section='Individual'.
requirement.name: Vector search against SpecialtyMetaData with Section=Individual filter

requirement.requirement: Vector-search results scoring at or above the cosine candidate floor are passed to the AI filter step. The cosine floor value itself is a design choice and is not specified at the requirement level.
requirement.name: Candidate pool above the cosine candidate floor passes to the AI filter step

requirement.requirement: The candidate pool is passed to an LLM filter call using the system prompt registered at prompts.json[_record_id = 'specialty_filter_system_prompt']. The filter call returns the final NUCC code list.
requirement.name: AI filter step uses prompts.json record; returns final NUCC code list

requirement.requirement: The AI flow above runs exactly ONCE per user query. The result list is cached for downstream client-side filtering per the cache REQ-T in S-003.
requirement.name: Pipeline executes once per query; result list cached for downstream use

The Manage slice specifically covers: individual checkbox toggles, category-checkbox behavior, the Uncheck-All / Check-All control, count updates, and panel persistence across service-control transfers.

requirement.requirement: The user can uncheck any individual specialty checkbox to remove that specialty from the active filter selection.

requirement.requirement: The Prescribers checkbox in the panel header behaves exactly as described in the master comprehensive UX in EPIC-006-F-002-S-001-REQ-B-001 (Prescribers section): for all prescribers (Homeopathic and others), if the per-specialty checkbox is unchecked it gets checked; if it is already checked it remains checked. For all non-prescribers (Homeopathic and non-Homeopath), regardless of prior state, the per-specialty checkbox becomes unchecked. The master REQ-B-001 governs in any conflict.
requirement.name: Prescribers checkbox behavior follows the master comprehensive UX

requirement.requirement: The Homeopathic checkbox in the panel header behaves exactly as described in the master comprehensive UX in EPIC-006-F-002-S-001-REQ-B-001 (Homeopathic section): for all Homeopathic specialties that treat the disorder specifically, if the per-specialty checkbox is unchecked it gets checked; if it is already checked it remains checked. For all non-Homeopathic specialties (prescribers or non-prescribers), regardless of prior state, the per-specialty checkbox becomes unchecked. Per the feature-level clarification, 'Homeopathic' here refers to a Homeopathic provider â€” it is not an umbrella label for the broader CAM set and does not introduce a new classification. The master REQ-B-001 governs in any conflict.
requirement.name: Homeopathic checkbox behavior follows the master comprehensive UX

requirement.requirement: All effects of the Prescribers and Homeopathic checkboxes are realized client-side against the cached specialty list. No round-trip to the backend, no DB call, no observable latency.
requirement.name: Toggling Prescribers or Homeopathic MUST NOT trigger a backend query

requirement.requirement: A single button in the panel header checks all currently-visible specialties or unchecks all of them per the rule refined in the master comprehensive UX in EPIC-006-F-002-S-001-REQ-B-001: the button reads 'Uncheck all' by default and switches to 'Check All' when fewer than 50% of the rows are unchecked. (i.e., the label switches to 'Check All' when the number of unchecked rows is strictly less than 50% of all rows; at exactly 50% the label remains 'Uncheck all'.) The master REQ-B-001 governs in any conflict.
requirement.name: Check-all / uncheck-all button (rule per master comprehensive UX)

requirement.requirement: The 'All Possible' count displays the total number of NUCC specialty types the system returned for the current request. This count does not change as the user toggles checkboxes â€” it reflects the size of the original returned set, constant for the lifetime of one query result.
requirement.name: COUNT 'All Possible' â€” total NUCC specialties returned

requirement.requirement: The 'Prescribers' count displays the number of prescriber-flagged specialty types present in the universe of specialty types that was returned to the client for the current request (i.e., the same universe that 'All Possible' counts). It is NOT a count of the universe of all specialists across the system, and it is NOT filtered by current checkbox state. Per Skip's clarification: this is about the universe returned to the client. The master REQ-B-001 governs in any conflict.
requirement.name: COUNT 'Prescribers' â€” count of prescriber-flagged specialty types in the universe returned to the client

requirement.requirement: The 'Your Choices' count displays the number of specialty checkboxes that are currently checked. This is the set that will be sent to Provider Search when the user hits Apply Filter.
requirement.name: COUNT 'Your Choices' â€” count of specialties currently checked

requirement.requirement: The SpecialtyFilter MUST remain on the screen at all times when the wrapper is active, including across every service-control transfer (FindCare â†” EvaluateCare â†” SharedServices). The SpecialtyFilter is FindCare territory â€” it MUST be served by FindCare and no other service can or may serve this panel.
requirement.name: SpecialtyFilter is FindCare territory; persists across every service-control transfer

requirement.requirement: The cached specialty list from S-002 is the operand for all toggle/checkbox changes in this story, including the Prescribers and Homeopathic category checkboxes. No backend round-trip occurs for any interaction. EXPLICIT EXCEPTION: this is an authorized exception to the project-wide rule 'no business logic on the client,' justified by interactivity latency requirements (toggle response must feel instantaneous). The exception is explicit and covers the category-checkbox semantic filtering as well as individual checkbox toggles. Only the final Apply Filter submission traverses to the backend per the Apply-Filter REQ-T in S-004.
requirement.name: Cache + client-side filtering â€” explicit exception to no-biz-logic-on-client

requirement.requirement: The user-visible behavior of the SpecialtyFilter panel when the user commits the current selection by clicking Apply Filter â€” the button's visibility and greyed/hot state, the no-changes non-modal popup, the clearing of the unpicked-providers list, the timer presentation, and the kick-off of a new provider query â€” MUST comply with the comprehensive UX described in EPIC-006-F-002-S-001-REQ-B-001 for the slice that covers Apply-Filter submission. The Submit slice specifically covers: Apply-Filter button visibility/state (greyed-when-no-changes per the master), the non-modal popup on click when no changes have been made, change detection between the current selection and the last submitted selection, clearing of the unpicked provider list, timer placement, and the trigger that kicks off the new provider query.

The selected-providers panel and the prompt area are preserved per the middle-screen-behavior clarification in the master REQ-B-001.

requirement.requirement: When Apply Filter triggers a new provider query, the timer MUST appear in the control frame at the bottom of the screen, in the same location as the initial search timer. Per the master comprehensive UX, two timers are involved (one immediately to the left of the user-prompt input box; one on the main screen); this REQ-T governs the main-screen timer at the bottom control frame.

requirement.requirement: The Apply Filter button is always visible at the bottom of the screen (placement per S-001-REQ-T-017). Its hot/greyed state follows the master comprehensive UX in EPIC-006-F-002-S-001-REQ-B-001: when the user has made changes to the filter selection that have not yet been applied, the button is hot; when no changes have been made (or after a successful Apply Filter clears the change state), the button is greyed out. If the user clicks the greyed button, a non-modal popup with an 'OK' button MUST display the message: 'There are no changes to apply, try a new prompt if this is the wrong list. The AI agent will help you craft the right question' and no other action is taken. The master REQ-B-001 governs in any conflict â€” the previous 'invisible-until-change' behavior is NOT the requirement.

story.name: User Submits Filter to Provider Tab

story.description: The technical contracts that bound the Specialty Filter feature: API visibility model, input contract, hand-off contract to Provider Search, and DOM frame placement.

requirement.requirement:
All Specialty Filter APIs are PRIVATE â€” in-process function calls within the FindCare service. The feature exposes ZERO public HTTP endpoints (no browser-callable routes) and ZERO protected HTTP endpoints (no peer-service-callable routes). All Specialty Filter functionality is reachable only by other code running inside the FindCare process. The folder layout MUST reflect this â€” Specialty Filter modules live under `private/` (or equivalent per the FindCare API folder convention).
Current architecture note (per Skip clarification in v4): at this point of our architecture the cross-component call out is to a JavaScript function in index.html. While that pattern is problematic in many cases, we are NOT taking on a refactor of it at this time; today all calls route through JS functions. When caching covers the path, the JS-function indirection is not the issue.
requirement.name: API visibility â€” all Specialty Filter APIs are PRIVATE to FindCare (today via JS in index.html)

requirement.requirement: The system MUST NOT parse the user's vernacular utterance for geographic terms inside the specialty-matching mechanism; geography never reaches that mechanism. Per Skip clarification in v4, the geographic qualifier will be resolved in the routing AI call (currently not yet wired). All geo references in the user's utterance will be sanitized prior to the client receiving the specialty list, and the AI prompt will account for geography. The Specialty Filter tool will receive a sanitized query. The exact routing-AI prompt and the precise geo-field shape (typed enum, free-form string, or structured object) will be resolved collaboratively as that prompt is finalized â€” these details are NOT a client-side concern and are not required at this requirement's level.
requirement.name: Input contract â€” geographic qualifier is sanitized upstream and never reaches the specialty-matching mechanism

requirement.requirement:
On Apply Filter, the Specialty Filter calls the Provider Search API endpoint with a payload containing: selected_nucc_codes (array of NUCC code strings) and geo (object carrying the user's geographic qualifier; precise shape per S-005-REQ-T-002 resolution). The endpoint name and canonical JSON shape live in the FindCare service-API contract. The Provider Search feature's behavior on receipt is governed by EPIC-006-F-001 and is NOT specified here.
Authoring note: per Skip directive in v4, requirements MUST NOT cite bug ids â€” that is bad requirements management. This REQ pointed at the FindCare service-API contract directly and contains no bug-id references.
requirement.name: Handoff contract â€” Apply Filter calls Provider Search API with {selected_nucc_codes, geo}

requirement.requirement: The SpecialtyFilter MUST be rendered in the parent wrapper's DOM tree, NOT inside any service iframe (FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices). This is the technical mechanism that enables panel persistence across service-control transfers (the persistence REQ-T in S-003).
requirement.name: DOM placement â€” rendered in parent wrapper DOM, NOT inside any service iframe

Test ids follow the convention {full-REQ-id}-TEST-1 (e.g., EPIC-006-F-002-S-001-REQ-B-001-TEST-1). Each REQ in this feature references its corresponding test_id in its own `tests` field.

This story's status remains not_started until each test body is implemented and Skip approves the test plan.

requirement.requirement: A Playwright end-to-end test MUST be written that exercises the Specialty Filter from initial query response through user management of the panel through Apply Filter submission, and asserts that the user-visible BEHAVIOR at every stage matches the comprehensive UX described in EPIC-006-F-002-S-001-REQ-B-001 â€” specifically: counts move correctly, checkboxes toggle correctly, button visibility/hot/greyed transitions correctly, the no-changes popup fires correctly, the unpicked provider list clears correctly, and the timers appear in the right places. Per Skip directive in v4: Playwright scripts are constructed for FUNCTIONALITY. APPEARANCE (pixel-comparison against SpecialtyFilters.jpg) is a UAT function, not a SIT function â€” appearance belongs to human eyes at this point of project maturity. The test serves as the executable verification of the four per-story compliance REQ-Bs (S-001-REQ-B-001, S-002-REQ-B-001, S-003-REQ-B-001, S-004-REQ-B-001) for behavior. Test plan and test body require Skip approval per the approved-test-plan rule for Claude-authored tests.
requirement.name: End-to-end Playwright test proving the per-story compliance REQ-Bs deliver Skip's comprehensive UX (functional only)

feature.name: Provider Detail
feature.description: This feature specifies the detailed user view and capabilities of a provider detail.

story.name: Provider Detail display
story.description: The Provider Detail panel is the user-facing surface the user reaches by clicking a Provider link from wherever it is presented within the ChatHealthy.ai application. It shows identity, credentials, every practice and business address (labeled and ordered), every license, insurance identifiers, the pipeline-derived enrichments (county info, urban marker), and external research links the user can click to verify the provider independently. Every field is read from the provider record in our Mongo; that record is brought to live-NPPES freshness on each click by the data-management story (EPIC-006-F-025-S-002).

requirement.name: Display reads only from the provider record
requirement.requirement: Every Provider Detail render MUST read its fields from the Mongo provider record document for the clicked NPI. The rendering is independent of any maintenance done on the record by EPIC-006-F-025-S-002 â€” the display shows what is currently in the record at render time.

requirement.name: Identity and credential fields
requirement.requirement: The panel MUST display the provider's full name (prefix, first, middle, last), credentials, primary taxonomy (NUCC display name), NPI, status (active/inactive), and enumeration date. Missing fields render as empty placeholders â€” no fallback prose.

requirement.name: All licenses, one row per licenses[] entry
requirement.requirement: The panel MUST display every entry in the record's normalized licenses[] array. Each row shows the licensing state and the license number. When a provider has multiple licenses in the same state, each is shown as its own row. When the licenses[] array is empty the License section is still labeled but shows an empty list â€” no fallback prose.

requirement.name: All addresses, labeled, business at the bottom
requirement.requirement: The panel MUST display every entry in the record's addresses[] array. Each row carries an explicit label ("Practice" for address_type='practice', "Business" for address_type='business'). Display order: all practice addresses first (in the order they appear on the record); all business addresses last. The fields per row are: street (line1 + line2 if present), city, state, ZIP, country, phone, and the enriched county info (see REQ-B-005).

requirement.name: Pipeline-enriched county info shown per address
requirement.requirement: For every address row the panel MUST display the county name (from county.name on the address) and the urban marker (from county.urban). When county.urban is absent on an address (e.g. a just-written-back new address whose urban workbook pass has not yet re-run) the panel renders the county name only, no urban marker. The county.fips and county.source fields are internal â€” not shown to the user.

requirement.name: Insurance section from the normalized insurance[] array
requirement.requirement: The panel MUST display an Insurance section rendering every entry in the record's normalized insurance[] array. Each row shows the insurance_type (human-readable, e.g. 'Medicaid', 'Medicare'), the brand (human-readable issuer with state suffix, e.g. 'State Medicaid Agency â€” AK'), the state, and the raw_value (the original identifier the issuer assigned). When insurance[] is empty the Insurance section is still labeled but shows an empty list â€” no fallback prose. The raw other_identifiers[] array is internal â€” not shown to the user.

requirement.name: External research links always rendered
requirement.requirement: Every render MUST include Healthgrades (search by name + state) and the NPI Registry (lookup by NPI). The panel MUST also render a third link to the appropriate state medical board for the provider's primary practice state, with coverage for every US state and the District of Columbia. For practice addresses in US territories and outlying sovereignties (PR, GU, VI, AS, MP, etc.) the panel MUST render the licensing authority link appropriate to that sovereignty. Each link MUST prefill suitable search criteria (provider name, license number, NPI) where the destination supports it so the user lands already scoped to the right provider. Each link carries a short guidance string explaining what the user will find at the destination.

requirement.name: Page invocation contract
requirement.requirement: The panel MUST be invoked exclusively by the user clicking a Provider link. No utterance, no language-model call. The click payload carries the NPI and the link-as-shown snapshot (name, state, taxonomy) so the backend has the bare minimum to identify the record and run the data-management flow.

requirement.name: Rendering layer separation
requirement.requirement: The panel HTML template lives at Website/index.html (the host page). The FindCare iframe MUST send only structured data via a postMessage event carrying the provider record + the research-sites object. The host page owns the layout; the iframe owns the payload. No prose strings cross the postMessage boundary.

story.name: Provider Detail data management and retrieval
story.description: Every Provider Detail click triggers a four-step data-management cycle: (1) fetch the live NPPES record by NPI; (2) compare every NPPES-sourced field on the live response to the corresponding field on the provider record in our Mongo; (3) when divergence is detected, write the live values back into the provider record while preserving or re-running pipeline enrichments according to the per-enrichment rules below; (4) display proceeds from the current provider record via the display story. Our trust model is unchanged: NPPES is authoritative for NPPES-sourced fields; our pipeline owns the enrichments (county info, urban marker, can_prescribe, is_homeopathic, is_disqualified, active log, normalized licenses[], normalized insurance[], embedding). Insurance is sourced exclusively from NPPES other_identifiers and then normalized; there is no separate insurance feed.

requirement.name: Live NPPES fetch on every click
requirement.requirement: Every Provider Detail request MUST fetch the full NPI record from the NPPES Registry public API at https://npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov/api/?number={npi}&version=2.1 with a 10-second timeout. NPPES is the authoritative source for all NPPES-sourced fields: basic identity, taxonomies, addresses, other_identifiers, status, and enumeration date.

requirement.name: Compare live vs the provider record before writing
requirement.requirement: After the live fetch the backend MUST compare every NPPES-sourced field on the response to the corresponding field on the provider record. The comparison covers name, taxonomies (codes + primary switch), the full addresses array (line1, line2, city, state, ZIP, country, phone, address_type), the raw other_identifiers array, status, enumeration date, and active log. When every field matches, no write occurs and the flow proceeds directly to display.

requirement.name: Write-back on divergence
requirement.requirement: When the comparison detects any divergence the backend MUST overwrite the NPPES-sourced fields on the provider record with the live values, then re-run or preserve pipeline enrichments per the rules in REQ-B-005 through REQ-B-011. The write is a single document update; the display read happens after the write succeeds.

requirement.name: New-address county lookup via Google Maps only
requirement.requirement: When the live NPPES response includes an address NOT present on the provider record (a brand-new street + city + state), the backend MUST resolve the new address's county.fips and county.name by calling the Google Maps geocoding API exclusively. The pipeline's earlier-stage funnel (ZIP crosswalk, Census Geocoder, NPPES API) is NOT used in this path. The county.source on the new address MUST be stamped 'geocoder_pass4_maps' to record the resolution provenance. If Google does not return an authoritative result for the new address, the county object on that address MUST be omitted (the address ships without county info) and a WARNING MUST be logged naming the NPI and the unresolved address.

requirement.name: Urban marker left off on new addresses
requirement.requirement: When a new address is written back, county.urban MUST be left absent on the new address's county object. The urban marker is owned by the pipeline's USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes (RUCC) workbook pass and is re-stamped on the next full pipeline load. Until then the display story renders the new address with county name but no urban marker (per S-001-REQ-B-005).

requirement.name: Preserve county info on unchanged addresses
requirement.requirement: For every address on the live NPPES response that matches an existing address on the provider record, the backend MUST preserve the existing county object verbatim (county.fips, county.name, county.source, county.zip_ratio if present, county.urban if present). The county info is not re-computed; the prior pipeline run already paid the resolution cost and the inputs have not changed.

requirement.name: Re-run prescriber and homeopathic flags on taxonomy change
requirement.requirement: When the live NPPES taxonomies array differs from the provider record (any added, removed, or changed taxonomy code), the backend MUST recompute can_prescribe, is_homeopathic, and is_disqualified by ORing/ANDing across the new taxonomy set against the ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags catalog (the same logic the pipeline's provider_flags_enrichment uses). When taxonomies are unchanged, these top-level flags MUST be preserved as-is.

requirement.name: Re-normalize licenses[] and insurance[] on write-back
requirement.requirement: On every write-back, the backend MUST replace BOTH the raw other_identifiers[] array (the NPPES-sourced data, exactly as the pipeline's normalize_provider_rows produces it) AND the normalized insurance[] array (the pipeline-derived form with insurance_type, brand, state, raw_value that the display consumes). Similarly the normalized licenses[] array MUST be regenerated from the live taxonomies' license fields so display and search consumers see consistent data. There is no enrichment of other_identifiers from any external insurance feed â€” NPPES is the only source.

requirement.name: Update active log if NPPES status changed
requirement.requirement: When the live NPPES basic.status, npi_deactivation_date, or npi_reactivation_date differs from the values represented by the last active[] log entry on the provider record, the backend MUST append a new event entry to active[] carrying the new event type (deactivated/reactivated), the date, the resulting is_active bool, and a source marker (nppes_deactivation_date / nppes_reactivation_date). When the status is unchanged, active[] is preserved verbatim.

requirement.name: Recompute quality flags after write-back
requirement.requirement: After write-back the backend MUST recompute the bad_data and out_of_scope flags from the new record state, using the same rules the pipeline's _mark_quality uses: bad_data {flagged: true, reason: 'no_address'} if addresses[] is empty; out_of_scope {flagged: true, reason: 'foreign_provider'} if the primary practice address country != 'US'; out_of_scope {flagged: true, reason: 'deactivated'} if the last active event is is_active=false. When inputs are unchanged the flags are preserved.

requirement.name: Stamp the provenance object on every successful write-back
requirement.requirement: On every successful write-back, the backend MUST set the provider record's sidecar provenance object as follows: provenance.origin = 'real_time_sync'; provenance.last_touched_at = the ISO timestamp of the write moment; provenance.real_time_sync_count is incremented by 1 if the field exists, otherwise initialized to 1. The four existing batch-ingest identifiers â€” load_id, loaded_at, chunk_id, row_index_in_chunk â€” MUST be preserved unchanged; they continue to identify the record's original pipeline ingest and are NEVER overwritten by a live write-back. The embedding, embedding_model, and embedding_version fields MUST also be preserved here; they are then superseded by REQ-B-014 when re-embedding completes.

requirement.name: Failure modes do not corrupt the record
requirement.requirement: When the NPPES live fetch fails (timeout, non-200, malformed response, zero results) OR the Google Maps geocoding call fails for a new address (covered separately by REQ-B-004), the backend MUST NOT write to the provider record. The display story is served from the existing (possibly stale) record. The failure is logged at WARNING. The user is not told the freshness sync failed â€” they see what we have.

requirement.name: One write per click, atomic, idempotent
requirement.requirement: When divergence is detected, the backend MUST issue exactly one MongoDB update against the provider record containing all the NPPES-sourced field updates plus the recomputed enrichment fields. Concurrent clicks for the same NPI MUST be safe â€” idempotent: the second write sees the same live response and either no-ops (because the first already wrote it) or produces identical fields.

requirement.name: Re-embed using the global embedding model on write-back
requirement.requirement: After a successful write-back, the backend MUST re-embed the record using the canonical global embedding model (per EPIC-008-F-011-S-004 and EPIC-002-F-005-S-012). The new embedding REPLACES the prior embedding, embedding_model, and embedding_version fields on the record. This keeps vector-search surfaces (provider search, specialty filter) consistent with the fresh field state after a live sync. If the embedding call fails, the prior embedding fields MUST be preserved and the write-back is still considered successful (the rest of the record is fresh; vector search will lag by one click until the next embedding attempt succeeds).

feature.name: Find Clinical Trials
feature.description: Find recruiting clinical trials by condition. Decomposed into three stories (data retrieval, display, architecture). Stories and requirements pending operator approval of V5 draft in _oneshots/EPIC-006-F-031_FindClinicalTrials_FeatureDraft_V5.docx.

story.name: Find Clinical Trials data retrieval
story.description: ClinicalTrialsTool data-retrieval contract: CT.gov v2 search parameters, the geographic_scope filter (international or US-only), pagination defaults, demographic filters (age, sex), the canonical search_context echo, and the deterministic /gate op for pagination.

requirement.name: Request totalCount from CT.gov and surface the total to callers
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST send countTotal=true on every CT.gov v2 /studies request and parse payload.totalCount from the response. The total MUST be surfaced on Response.total_count for downstream display. CT.gov returns totalCount as an integer when countTotal=true.

requirement.name: Default page size of 10 records
requirement.requirement: Request.page_size MUST default to 10 (down from 25). The user explicitly paginates with the cursor returned in Response.cursor; the wrapper's pagination control mirrors the providers pagination pattern.

requirement.name: Accept optional participant demographics (age, sex)
requirement.requirement: Request MUST accept two optional participant-demographic fields: age_years (Optional[int]) and sex (Optional[str]). Condition remains the only required field. When age_years is supplied, ClinicalTrialsTool MUST map to CT.gov aggFilters using the canonical buckets: age<18 -> ages:child, 18<=age<65 -> ages:adult, age>=65 -> ages:older. When sex is supplied, ClinicalTrialsTool MUST resolve it to 'm' or 'f' (per S-003-REQ-B-007) and map to CT.gov sex:m or sex:f. Gender is intentionally NOT a parameter on this tool -- sex alone drives the CT.gov filter.

requirement.name: Always emit a 'trials' stream event on every code path
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST emit a {kind:'trials', data:Response} stream event on every code path -- success, empty result set, error. The client relies on the trials event as the canonical end-of-search signal; silent paths previously caused 'no trials event in stream' user-visible failures.

requirement.name: Echo authoritative SearchContext on every Response
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST populate Response.search_context with the exact {condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope} actually used to fetch this page. The client uses search_context to re-issue pagination requests against the same canonical criteria, preventing the raw user utterance from leaking into the CT.gov call on subsequent pages.

requirement.name: Routes API failures must be surfaced (no silent swallow)
requirement.requirement: When the Google Routes API call for a destination fails, the tool MUST log the failure as a Mode 2 ChatHealthyException in one of four named modes: routes_api_key_missing (GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY env var absent), routes_api_non_200 (HTTP response not 200), routes_api_empty (200 with empty routes[]), and routes_api_failed (exception during the call). Distance/duration MAY remain absent on the affected Location; the operator is notified via the log.

requirement.name: Direct deterministic pagination op on /gate
requirement.requirement: SharedServices /gate MUST accept op='clinical_trials_page' with a payload matching ClinicalTrialsTool.Request (condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope, cursor, page_size). UR dispatches to ClinicalTrialsTool with no LLM and no UtteranceManager hop. This is the deterministic path the client uses for More / Back pagination clicks (REQ-B-068).

requirement.name: Geographic scope: international (default) or US-only
requirement.requirement: Request MUST accept an optional geographic_scope field with values 'international' (default) or 'us'. ClinicalTrialsTool MUST honor it as follows: 'international' applies NO geographic filter to CT.gov (all records returned worldwide). 'us' MUST add the CT.gov v2 GEO filter restricting to country=United States. No other per-country scoping is supported in this iteration -- the only choices are international or US.

requirement.name: Unit tests cover every public component of ClinicalTrialsTool
requirement.requirement: Every public method/function of ClinicalTrialsTool -- including but not limited to: CT.gov request builder, response parser, age_years -> aggFilter mapper, sex -> aggFilter mapper, geographic_scope -> GEO filter mapper, brief_summary first-sentence truncator, search_context echo populator, Routes API caller -- MUST have unit tests. Each component's test set MUST include at least ONE positive case (asserting the happy-path output) AND at least ONE anticipated negative case (e.g. missing input, malformed input, upstream failure mode, boundary condition). Tests live in FindCare/ClinicalTrials/tests/ alongside the tool source. No test may share state with another test.

story.name: Find Clinical Trials display
story.description: Front-end display contract: left-panel header band, first-sentence truncation, More/Back pagination, center-panel section anchors, right-panel section-list with smooth-scroll, loading banner content and timer behavior, intent_classified mid-stream banner update, and the pagination error overlay verb context.

requirement.name: Left-panel brief_summary truncated to first sentence with ellipsis
requirement.requirement: In the per-trial card in the left panel, the trial's brief_summary MUST be displayed truncated to its first sentence. When truncation occurs (the first sentence is shorter than the full summary), '...' MUST be appended to signal truncation. The user clicks the trial's NCT id to view the full detail in the main window.

requirement.name: Left-panel header band: canonical query criteria + record range
requirement.requirement: The colored header band at the top of the left panel MUST display the canonical query criteria as echoed by the tool (Response.search_context). Format: 'Clinical trials -- condition: <X>, subject age: <Y>, subject sex: <Z>, <location>, scope: <international|US>'. When the tool returns a total_count, the band MUST also append ' -- showing <start> to <end> of <total>'. When total is unknown the band MUST NOT show a count (it MUST NOT imply a count it does not know).

requirement.name: Left-panel More / Back pagination controls
requirement.requirement: The left panel MUST render a 'more trials' link when Response.cursor is non-null and a 'back' link when prior cursors exist (client-side history). Clicking either MUST round-trip through ClientRouter.makeCall to /gate op='clinical_trials_page' (REQ-B-073) -- NOT through the LLM-routed utterance path. The pagination control mirrors the providers pagination pattern.

requirement.name: Center-panel trial detail: section anchors
requirement.requirement: Every section in the main-window trial detail MUST carry a stable anchor id of the form id="ct-sec-<slug>" where <slug> is a lowercased hyphenated form of the section title. The anchors are the targets for right-panel section-list jump links (REQ-B-070).

requirement.name: Right-panel section-list with smooth-scroll jumps
requirement.requirement: When a trial is displayed in the main window, the right panel MUST render a 'Trial sections' list with one clickable link per section in the current trial (linked to the anchor ids from REQ-B-069). Clicking a link MUST smooth-scroll the main-window center to that section's anchor.

requirement.name: Immediate clear + timer on More / Back click
requirement.requirement: When the user clicks More or Back in the left panel, the system MUST immediately (before the network round-trip): clear the main-window trial detail, clear the right-panel section list, start a one-second-tick timer from zero, and render a loading banner. Then the network fetch is issued. The user must never see stale data while a new page is being fetched.

requirement.name: Loading banner content: canonical criteria + record range
requirement.requirement: The loading banner MUST display the canonical criteria (REQ-B-067 format, INCLUDING the geographic_scope) plus the record range being retrieved, e.g. 'condition: hepatitis B, subject age: 28, subject sex: male, Los Angeles, scope: US -- retrieving records 11-20 of 247'. The banner MUST NOT show only the raw user verb. The timer ticks every second next to or under the banner.

requirement.name: Mid-stream loading-banner update from intent_classified
requirement.requirement: On a fresh utterance flow, when UR has finished classifying the utterance into a findClinicalTrials intent, UR MUST emit a {kind:'intent_classified'} stream event carrying the canonical criteria (action, condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope). The client MUST replace the loading banner's raw utterance text with the canonical criteria as soon as that event arrives, so the user sees what the system actually understood, not the raw utterance.

requirement.name: Pagination error overlay must include verb context
requirement.requirement: When a More / Back pagination fetch fails, the client error overlay MUST prepend a verb-context clause to the underlying error message: 'While trying to load more clinical trials: <err>' (for next) or 'While trying to go back to the previous page of clinical trials: <err>' (for prev). The user must always see what action was in flight when the error occurred.

requirement.name: Standalone Playwright test for the clinical-trials display
requirement.requirement: A NEW Playwright test MUST be created at architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/find_care_clinical_trials_test.py covering every display REQ in Story S-002 -- at minimum: the left-panel header band format, the first-sentence truncation with ellipsis, the More / Back pagination controls and their round-trip through op='clinical_trials_page', the center-panel section anchors, the right-panel section-list with smooth-scroll, the immediate clear+timer on click, the loading-banner content and intent_classified update, and the pagination-error overlay verb context. The test MUST be INDEPENDENT of the smoke Playwright test -- the smoke only confirms the page renders and each iframe shows good content at a high level; this test asserts the fine-grained display contract. The test MUST fetch a real clinical trial from clinicaltrials.gov v2 (a stable, recruiting NCT id with a known section structure) as the reference fixture and assert against its actual data. The test MUST allow parameterized exercise of different search parameters (condition, age, sex, location, scope) and full pagination cycles (More, Back, More, etc.). If an existing Playwright test already covers any of this surface, that test is reused (and extended where it is incomplete) rather than duplicated.

requirement.name: Selected trial highlighted in left panel; click clears center+right immediately, then paints new trial
requirement.requirement: In the left-panel trial list, the trial currently displayed in frame_MainWindow MUST be visually distinguished (highlighted background) so the user always knows which card they are viewing. When the user clicks any trial card, the system MUST IMMEDIATELY blank frame_MainWindow and frame_RightPanel (paint empty content) BEFORE painting the new trial, so the user has an unambiguous visual confirmation that the click registered even when the new trial is fetched from the same in-memory page (no backend hop). The new trial's full detail is then painted into frame_MainWindow and its section-list into frame_RightPanel, and the left-panel highlight moves to the newly-selected card.

story.name: Find Clinical Trials architecture
story.description: Architecture contract between UtteranceManager, Universal Router, and ClinicalTrialsTool. UM prompts for refinements on first turn and extracts on follow-up; LLM (not regex) resolves the sex answer; condition is the only required field; UR thin pass-through for the deterministic pagination op.

requirement.name: UtteranceManager prompts for refinements on first clinical-trial turn
requirement.requirement: On the FIRST turn where the user expresses clinical-trial interest, UM MUST set target_action='closeConnection200' and emit a user_message that names EVERY refinement field not already known. The literal words 'age', 'sex', 'location', and 'scope' (asking international vs US) MUST appear in the user_message for each field that is missing. UM MUST tell the user that condition alone is enough -- they can answer 'skip' for any field. Park a pending_disambiguation with kind='clinical_trial_demographics'. UM MAY skip the ask and dispatch findClinicalTrials directly ONLY when all refinements are already known.

requirement.name: UtteranceManager extracts age_years, sex, user_location, geographic_scope from follow-up
requirement.requirement: On the FOLLOW-UP turn after the prompt, UM MUST extract every refinement supplied. age_years (int) from 'I'm 28' / '28' / '28yo' / 'age 28'. sex (lowercased 'm' or 'f') per REQ-B-007. user_location (free-text) from any location mention. geographic_scope ('international' or 'us') from any 'international'/'worldwide'/'US only'/'United States only' mention. Populate all extracted fields as Arguments on the findClinicalTrials intent. If the user declines ('skip', 'no', 'just show me'), proceed with whatever fields are populated. Always set target_action='findClinicalTrials'.

requirement.name: LLM-driven resolution of the user's sex answer to 'm' or 'f'
requirement.requirement: UM MUST resolve the user's answer to the sex prompt — or any sex signal in a free-text utterance — into the canonical lowercase token 'm' or 'f' via the classifier LLM. The LLM, not regex, MUST be authoritative. The LLM MUST recognize: (a) direct labels — 'Male', 'M', 'man', 'boy', 'masculino' → 'm'; 'Female', 'F', 'woman', 'girl' → 'f'; (b) male family / relationship words referring to the subject — 'son', 'brother', 'father', 'dad', 'uncle', 'nephew', 'grandfather', 'grandpa', 'husband', 'boyfriend', 'fiancé' → 'm'; (c) female family / relationship words — 'daughter', 'sister', 'mother', 'mom', 'aunt', 'niece', 'grandmother', 'grandma', 'wife', 'girlfriend', 'fiancée' → 'f'; (d) third-person pronouns about the subject when no contradicting label is present — 'he', 'his', 'him' → 'm'; 'she', 'her', 'hers' → 'f'. If the answer is ambiguous, non-binary, or mixes signals the LLM cannot reconcile, sex MUST be left None and the search dispatches without a sex filter. Gender is not a parameter in this iteration; we ask sex only. The same rules apply BOTH on the dedicated follow-up prompt AND on the first turn when the user volunteers the information ('clinical trial for my son who is 9' → sex='m', age_years=9).

requirement.name: Condition is the ONLY required field for findClinicalTrials
requirement.requirement: Across the entire clinical-trials flow (UM extraction, UR dispatch, tool execution), condition is the ONLY required field. age_years, sex, user_location, and geographic_scope are ALL optional refinements of equal stature -- none is 'primary', none is 'bonus'. The search MUST dispatch with whatever the user provides, including no refinements at all if the user skips every field. Default scope when omitted is 'international' (REQ-B-074).

requirement.name: Universal Router dispatches /gate op=clinical_trials_page as a thin pass-through
requirement.requirement: When /gate receives op='clinical_trials_page', UR MUST invoke _handle_clinical_trials_page which constructs a clinical_trials_tool.Request from the payload (Pydantic validates) and calls TOOL.run_and_log(deps, request). No biz logic in the handler -- all biz logic lives in ClinicalTrialsTool. UR also emits {kind:'intent_classified'} per REQ-B-073 on the LLM-routed findClinicalTrials dispatch path so the client can update its loading banner.

requirement.name: Unit tests cover UtteranceManager clinical-trial extraction paths
requirement.requirement: Every UM extraction rule in S-003 -- first-turn prompt construction (REQ-B-005), follow-up extraction of age / sex / location / scope (REQ-B-006), LLM-driven sex resolution (REQ-B-007), and the condition-only required-field guarantee (REQ-B-008) -- MUST have unit tests. Each rule's test set MUST include at least ONE positive case (e.g. user supplies all refinements; UM extracts cleanly) AND at least ONE anticipated negative case (e.g. user says 'skip'; ambiguous sex answer the LLM cannot resolve; user supplies an unsupported country for geographic_scope and UM falls back to international). Tests live alongside the UM source.

requirement.requirement: For form factors such as the iPhone and Galaxy, a reactive interface MUST support the phone. The reactive interface MUST use a style guide regarded as an industry standard.
requirement.name: Reactive interface for iPhone and Galaxy MUST use an industry-standard style guide

requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy.ai phones and iPads MUST conform to the Apple Human Interface Guidelines (HIG), published by Apple Inc. at https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines. Baseline rules that MUST be observed in the reactive interface: (a) every interactive control presents a minimum 44x44pt hit target (HIG Inputs); (b) layouts honor safe-area insets via CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) with the document declaring <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"> so content clears the Dynamic Island and home indicator (HIG Layout); (c) text contrast meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large) as cross-referenced by HIG Accessibility; (d) body type sizes use rem so they honor user Dynamic Type / browser zoom settings; (e) primary actions on phone breakpoints (<= 600px) sit within the lower-third thumb zone of the viewport. The version of HIG in force is the current published edition; the citation MUST be re-pinned if Apple issues a major guide revision.
requirement.name: Technical requirement MUST cite the exact best-practice phone/iPad style guide in use

feature.name: Engineering Rule Enforcement
feature.description:
This feature specifies the rules that must be enforced by the chatHealthy.ai dev ops infrastructure utilizing the Anthopic Hooks as event triggers. 
It specifies the concrete DevOps surface that wires Claude Code's hook architecture into ChatHealthy governance. Hosts SessionStart / PostCompact / UserPromptSubmit / Stop enforcement entries declared in engineering_rules.json, the chathealthy_devops_boot program (Rule-002), and the conversation-log persistence path (Rule-001). Owns the operator-visible boot lifecycle: conversation context replay and agile_backlog taxonomy injection on both new-session begin and post-compaction restart.

Move prime rule into governance JSON and add two runtime enforcement points
story.description: The prime engineering rule lives only in CLAUDE.md today and has no hook-driven enforcement. This story moves the rule text verbatim into engineering_rules.json and adds two runtime enforcement entries that execute via the existing hook architecture: prompt_verify_directive (UserPromptSubmit) and response_claim_audit (Stop). Both executors live inside the renamed hook manager AnthropicsClaudeCodeHookManager.py.

requirement.requirement: Above all else: Claude MUST NOT make any misrepresentations. Before stating anything, Claude must conduct sufficient research - reading project files, code, requirements, and external sources as needed - so that Claude can only: state a verified fact, state that it does not know, or ask a clarifying question. This rule takes precedence over all other directives when Claude is interacting with the human operator.
requirement.name: Prime rule: no misrepresentation
Materiality threshold
requirement.requirement: In all non-production environments, a possible consequence to an action a human user asks Claude Code to do - either as an analysis task or as one that will change state in a reversible way - must not be surfaced to the human operator when that possible analytical or factual potential has less than a 2% probability of occurring.

The prime rule MUST be encoded as a Rule entry in brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json with at least two enforcement entries that execute at runtime via the existing hook architecture: (1) prompt_verify_directive fires on UserPromptSubmit and, when the user prompt asks about external-system behavior, injects a hard directive requiring Claude to cite a tool result from this turn or to say 'I don't know - let me verify'; (2) response_claim_audit fires on Stop, scans Claude's just-finished response for definitive claims about external systems, and writes a violation record when no Read/Grep/Bash/WebFetch tool call in the same turn touched that system. Both executors live inside the renamed hook manager (AnthropicsClaudeCodeHookManager.py). The CLAUDE.md preamble is replaced by a one-line pointer to the rule ID.
requirement.name: Prime rule runtime enforcement

story.name: Rules infrastructure: manager, base worker, lock, timeout, telemetry, exit-code aggregation
story.description: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager + EnforcementWorker (abstract base) deliver the framework: read-only rules-registry load, hook-filtered enforcement dispatch, manager-owned mutex coordination, per-worker subprocess timeout, structured violation/telemetry envelopes, and worst-code-wins aggregation. Per V20 Â§4.4. The manager is invoked by every Git and Claude Code hook with a single hook_name argument.

requirement.name: Rules carry enforcement entries
requirement.requirement: Every engineering rule that the team intends to enforce MUST carry at least one programmatic enforcement entry. A rule with an empty enforcement array is documentation, not governance, and SHALL be either populated, retired, or annotated as documentation-only.

requirement.name: Enforcement at hook moment
requirement.requirement: Enforcement runs at the moment a violation can occur â€” the relevant Git or Claude Code hook â€” not on a separate cadence. There is no nightly job that catches yesterday's mistake.

requirement.name: Hook-agnostic framework
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule MUST be able to attach to any of the four Git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push) and any of the six Claude Code hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded). The framework is hook-agnostic; the enforcement entry declares its hook.

requirement.name: Human debuggability
requirement.requirement: The system MUST be debuggable by a human. One file per role. One class per file. One entry point. Per-enforcement, per-worker structured stdout and telemetry, with worst exit code propagated.

requirement.name: Multi-PID concurrency
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST handle multi-PID race conditions correctly. The same hook can fire many times concurrently across different Claude Code PIDs and Git invocations. The manager acquires a lock before dispatching any worker whose enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True; in-process locks are forbidden.

requirement.name: Additive enforcement
requirement.requirement: Adding the next enforcement MUST be a small, additive change. New enforcement entries get a new enforcement_id and â€” if needed â€” a new worker subclass; existing rules and workers are not touched.

requirement.name: Worker inherits base class
requirement.requirement: Every worker MUST inherit from EnforcementWorker. Subclasses implement only their domain-specific check logic. The base class owns scope evaluation, violation shape, exit codes, telemetry, and error handling so every worker behaves the same from the manager's perspective.

requirement.name: Enforcement entry first-class
requirement.requirement: Enforcement entries are first-class records: every entry carries a stable enforcement_id (format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN), a declared hook, an executable_path, a scopes field carrying scope-list rules in the four canonical types (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern), and a requires_lock boolean. They can be cited in audit trails, bug reports, and the backlog like requirements are today.

requirement.name: Filesystem mirrors operating model
requirement.requirement: The architecture MUST be aligned with the EPIC / Feature / Story tree. Filesystem mirrors operating model. The home for this feature is projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/. crossEpicConcerns/ holds shared business artifacts only â€” no code lives there.

requirement.name: V1 demonstrability
requirement.requirement: Once V1 ships, BR-1 through BR-9 are demonstrably satisfied for the worked example (file scanning on pre-commit) and the framework is in place to absorb every other rule on its own schedule.

requirement.name: Four canonical scope-list types
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST support all four scope-list types on every enforcement entry, even when a given worker uses only a subset. The four permitted terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern) are the only vocabulary used anywhere in this system.

requirement.name: Enforcement schema fields
requirement.requirement: engineering_rules.json schema gains the following required fields per enforcement entry: enforcement_id (string, format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN); hook (enum: pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded); executable_path (string â€” repo-relative path to the worker script that implements this enforcement); requires_lock (boolean â€” true if the manager must acquire a lock before dispatching this worker); scopes (array of three-column arrays â€” [function_name: str, scope_list_type: str, list_of_terms: list[str]] â€” carrying this enforcement's per-enforcement scope-list rules; scope_list_type âˆˆ {allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern}; the EngineeringRulesSchema.json validator enforces this row shape; see Â§4.6); timeout (integer, optional â€” seconds; defaults to manager constant DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30 when omitted; the manager passes this value to subprocess.run(..., timeout=N); on timeout the manager kills the worker subprocess and returns EXIT_WORKER_TIMEOUT (4); the worker does not see this field â€” the timeout is enforced by the parent process; see Â§4.3.2). The four scope-list types are carried only by scopes; there are no separate top-level allowed_exact / allowed_pattern / excluded_exact / excluded_pattern fields on the entry.

requirement.name: Manager class and exit codes
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager lives at projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py. Single class. Single main. Constructor signature __init__(hook_name: str). run returns int. The manager module defines the following named exit-code constants and run returns one of them: EXIT_OK = 0 (all matched enforcements passed), EXIT_VIOLATIONS_FOUND = 1 (at least one worker reported violations; commit/push must block), EXIT_MANAGER_ERROR = 2 (manager-level failure: cannot read engineering_rules.json, malformed schema, unknown hook name, or any other pre-dispatch error), EXIT_WORKER_SPAWN_FAILURE = 3 (one or more workers could not be launched: missing executable_path, executable not found, permission denied, OSError on subprocess), EXIT_WORKER_TIMEOUT = 4 (one or more workers exceeded the configured subprocess timeout), EXIT_WORKER_INTERNAL_ERROR = 5 (a worker exited with a non-0 / non-1 status â€” i.e. anything â‰¥ 3 from a worker is treated as an internal worker failure rather than a violation). Aggregation by precedence (highest wins): 2 > 3 > 5 > 4 > 1 > 0. Manager-level errors trump worker errors trump violations trump success, so the caller can immediately tell whether the issue is in the framework or in the user's code. Worker exit codes follow the same convention for the worker's subset: 0 = clean, 1 = violations, 2 = worker error; any worker exit â‰¥ 3 is promoted by the manager to EXIT_WORKER_INTERNAL_ERROR.

requirement.name: Manager load-filter-spawn
requirement.requirement: Manager loads engineering_rules.json read-only, filters enforcement[] by hook, and for each matching enforcement reads executable_path and spawns the worker via subprocess.run([sys.executable, executable_path, enforcement_id], timeout=...). The manager collects each subprocess returncode and aggregates by the TR-2 exit-code precedence.

requirement.name: EnforcementWorker base class
requirement.requirement: EnforcementWorker (abstract base) lives at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/enforcement_worker.py. It owns: __init__(enforcement_id), _load_enforcement, is_in_scope(resource), main (CLI entry that parses enforcement_id, instantiates the subclass, calls run, returns its exit code), violation emission, telemetry emission, and structured error handling. Subclasses implement run and any private helper methods their domain requires.

requirement.name: Violation record shape
requirement.requirement: Violation record shape (emitted by the base class): {enforcement_id, rule_id, resource, message, severity}. severity in {info, warn, error}.

requirement.name: Telemetry envelope
requirement.requirement: Telemetry envelope (emitted by the base class): start record and end record per worker invocation, both carrying enforcement_id, hook, duration_ms, files_scanned, violation_count, exit_code. Format: one JSON object per line to stdout.

requirement.name: Manager-owned mutex
requirement.requirement: When an enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True, the manager MUST acquire a process-safe lock keyed on enforcement_id before invoking subprocess.run, and MUST release the lock after subprocess.run returns (clean, non-zero, or timeout). Default mechanism: advisory file lock. In-process Python locks are forbidden. Workers do not declare a concurrency primitive.

requirement.name: Manager-worker contract
requirement.requirement: Manager and workers MUST NOT import each other's internals. The only contract is enforcement_id (str) in via CLI argv, exit code (int) out via subprocess returncode, and the structured stdout (violation + telemetry) envelope.

requirement.name: Tests location
requirement.requirement: Tests live at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/tests/. The base class ships with its own test suite covering scope evaluation, exit-code semantics, violation shape, telemetry envelope, and the try/except fail-safe. Each new worker ships with at least one happy-path and one violation-path test.

requirement.name: Hook plumbing
requirement.requirement: Hook plumbing..git/hooks/{pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push} each invoke `python <repo-root>/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py --hook <hook>`..claude/settings.json registers the same invocation under SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded with the matching `--hook <hook_name>` flag. A pytest under architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/tests/ MUST verify, for every hook named above: (a) hard assert the wire-up exists when the hook carries at least one enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json; (b) advisory warning when the wire-up is missing and the hook has no enforcement (reserved for future Phase-6 workers). The test runs in the F-002 suite and the hard assertions gate pre-push.

requirement.name: Worker taxonomy
requirement.requirement: Worker taxonomy supported by the framework: file scanning (pre-commit / pre-push), prompt-injection check (UserPromptSubmit â€” returns additionalContext), post-response audit (Stop), log publishing (UserPromptSubmit + Stop -> Kafka), boot orchestration (SessionStart), and mode selection (SessionStart). Each is a concrete subclass of EnforcementWorker, deployed as its own standalone executable.

story.name: Scanning: file enumeration on hooks, SCOPES evaluation, scope precedence
story.description: Per V20 Â§4.5 and Â§4.9. Workers receive resource candidates (staged or about-to-push files for the V1 ScanFilesEnforcementWorker), evaluate each via the base-class is_in_scope walk against the SCOPES rows on the enforcement entry, and dispatch matched check methods. Scope precedence is fixed and lives entirely in the base class.

requirement.name: Scope walk precedence
requirement.requirement: Scope evaluation is fixed-precedence and lives entirely in the base class. For each (resource, function_name) the base class walks the matching rows in self.scopes (filtered by function_name) in this fixed order: excluded_exact, excluded_pattern, allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, then per-check SCOPE_DEFAULT. Subclasses do not override this walk. The default behavior (in scope vs. out of scope when no row matched) is declared per check via the per-method SCOPE_DEFAULT class attribute.

requirement.name: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker
requirement.requirement: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker (worked example, V1) lives at projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/scan_files_enforcement_worker.py. It is a standalone Python script with a main that takes enforcement_id as a CLI argument and exits with a status code. Its run implements two domain checks synchronously, in this order, on every in-scope file: (a) _scan_http(file) â€” the HTTP-vs-HTTPS regex scan ported from preCommitScan.py; (b) _validate_json(file) â€” the JSON schema validation ported from validate_all_json.py. Both run inside the same subprocess. Multi-threading inside run is a documented future enhancement, not V1. requires_lock = false (read-only worker; the manager dispatches without acquiring a lock). ScanFilesEnforcementWorker's scope-list rules live in its enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json under the scopes field (see Â§4.6); the worker inherits the default _load_scopes from EnforcementWorker, which returns self.entry.get("scopes", []). It does NOT override _load_scopes and contributes no SCOPES class attribute (see Â§4.5 for the mechanism, Â§4.9.1 for the per-method spec, and Â§4.9.2 for the worked-example rows).

requirement.name: Scope rows on enforcement entry
requirement.requirement: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker scope rules are expressed as a flat three-column list in its enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json under the scopes field. Each row has the shape [function_name: str, scope_list_type: str, list_of_terms: list[str]] where scope_list_type is one of the four canonical terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern) and function_name is the name of a check method on the worker (e.g. _scan_http, _validate_json). The EnforcementWorker base class loads the list at worker startup through the virtual _load_scopes method, whose default implementation returns self.entry.get("scopes", []); ScanFilesEnforcementWorker inherits that default and does NOT override it. The base class then resolves function_name to a bound method via getattr(self, row[0]) at startup, so a typo in function_name fails loudly rather than silently dropping a rule. The ordered precedence of the four types is fixed in the base class per TR-5 and is described in narrative form in Â§4.5. The SCOPE_DEFAULT class attribute is per-check: False for _scan_http (don't flag a path that no rule matched), True for _validate_json (every governed JSON is in scope unless explicitly excluded). The canonical worked example â€” exactly the rows used by V1 â€” is in Â§4.9.2.

requirement.name: preCommitScan.py JSON retirement
requirement.requirement: preCommitScan.py SHALL drop ".json" from SCAN_EXTENSIONS and \.json$ from HTTP_EXEMPT_PATTERNS once ScanFilesEnforcementWorker is the single source of truth (note: SCAN_EXTENSIONS and HTTP_EXEMPT_PATTERNS are legacy module-level names inside preCommitScan.py â€” the artifact being retired â€” and are not part of the new framework's vocabulary; the new framework uses scopes rows in engineering_rules.json). Once the manager dispatches all enforcement, preCommitScan.py is retired.

requirement.name: Scan must test this content
requirement.requirement: The scan rule Must test for: (a) Font compliance â€” see EPIC-008-F-011-S-003-REQ-B-004 (Scan of all relevant files must test font compliance); (b) JSON Schema validation â€” see EPIC-008-F-002-S-006 (JSON validation: _validate_json check, $schema web-fetch resolver, meta-schema carve-out, in-run cache); (c) HTTPS compliance â€” see EPIC-008-F-002-S-005 (HTTP vs HTTPS: _scan_http check and allowed_pattern URL handling).

story.name: HTTP vs HTTPS: _scan_http check and allowed_pattern URL handling
story.description: Per V20 BR-12, BR-13, TR-11. The _scan_http check on ScanFilesEnforcementWorker enforces that production source code, documentation, and deployment configuration MUST NOT contain http:// URLs unless the URL itself matches an allowed_pattern row on the enforcement entry's scopes (loopback, link-local metadata, w3.org, etc.). Files intended to carry http:// content as legitimate data are listed in allowed_exact / allowed_pattern rows. Other files are exempted via excluded_exact / excluded_pattern.

requirement.name: http: legitimate-content allowance
requirement.requirement: Files that are intended to carry plain text "http:" as legitimate content â€” for example, JSON files whose purpose is to record example URLs, configuration files that list http endpoints by design, fixtures, and similar data files â€” MUST be allowed to contain the term "http:". These files are listed on the enforcement entry's allowed by exact match rows, or matched by the enforcement entry's allowed by pattern rows, and they will not be flagged as a violation.

requirement.name: http: production-source ban
requirement.requirement: Files that are intended to be production source code, documentation, deployment configuration, or any other artifact that should not embed insecure http URLs MUST NOT contain the term "http:" unless the URL itself is on the enforcement entry's allowed by pattern rows (for example, loopback addresses, link-local metadata endpoints, or known public standards URLs). Files of this kind that are deliberately exempt for any reason MUST appear on the enforcement entry's excluded by exact match rows or be matched by the enforcement entry's excluded by pattern rows. Any other file found to contain the term "http:" is a violation and the commit MUST be blocked.

requirement.name: _scan_http scope alignment
requirement.requirement: The set of files allowed to contain "http:" is exactly the union of the enforcement entry's allowed_exact rows and the files matched by the entry's allowed_pattern rows for _scan_http. The set of files exempt from the scan entirely is exactly the union of the entry's excluded_exact rows and the files matched by the entry's excluded_pattern rows for _scan_http. Any file not matched by any of those four scope_list_type rows that contains the term "http:" â€” except where the URL itself matches an allowed_pattern row for _scan_http â€” is a violation.

story.name: JSON validation: _validate_json check, $schema web-fetch resolver, meta-schema carve-out, in-run cache
story.description: Per V20 BR-11/15/16, TR-12/18/19, Â§4.9.3 and Â§4.9.3.1. The _validate_json check on ScanFilesEnforcementWorker validates every governed JSON file under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ against the schema declared in its $schema field, using jsonschema Draft 2020-12. ChatHealthy schemas declared in $schema URLs are resolved via HTTPS GET (5s timeout, per-run cache) per TR-18; the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema is the single carve-out, served from a local copy under Website/schemas/standard/ per TR-19 / BR-16. Files with $schema missing that are not explicitly excluded MUST FAIL LOUD.

requirement.name: Governed JSON validation gate
requirement.requirement: Every file the system treats as governed JSON content MUST validate cleanly against the schema declared in its $schema field. The set of governed JSON files is defined using only the four permitted scope-list terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern). The system MUST NOT trust data from a JSON file that fails schema validation, and the framework MUST treat validation failure as a governance violation. JSON validation is the load-bearing gate that protects the entire governed-data layer from silent drift.

requirement.name: Draft 2020-12, no opt-out
requirement.requirement: Governed JSON content lives under brain/machine_artifacts/content/. Each governed JSON file MUST declare its schema URL in a top-level $schema field. JSON parsing uses Python's standard library json module. Schema validation uses the jsonschema package against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Validation failure produces a violation record per TR-6 and contributes to the worker's exit code (EXIT_VIOLATIONS_FOUND = 1). Files identified by the worker's excluded_exact or excluded_pattern lists are skipped silently; files in scope without a $schema field MUST FAIL LOUD. There is no opt-out, and there is no quiet passing of unschemaed JSON content. The JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema URL is the single resolver carve-out, served from a local copy at Website/schemas/standard/json-schema-2020-12-meta.json. All other $schema URLs are resolved by HTTP GET with a 5-second timeout and per-run cache.

requirement.name: Validation uses $schema URL
requirement.requirement: Validation MUST use the schema referenced by the JSON file's $schema URL.

requirement.name: External standards committed
requirement.requirement: External standards used by the framework MUST be committed to the repository.

requirement.name: $schema HTTPS resolution + cache
requirement.requirement: Aligned to BR-15. ChatHealthy schemas declared in $schema URLs are resolved via HTTPS GET to the URL the JSON file declared, performed at validation time. A per-run cache deduplicates identical URLs within a single worker invocation. Unreachable URL, non-200, timeout, or non-JSON response body produces a per-file ViolationRecord per TR-6.

requirement.name: External-standard carve-out cache
requirement.requirement: Aligned to BR-16. Cached external standards live under Website/schemas/standard/. A standard is eligible for caching when its URL is contractually frozen by the spec maintainer (any change requires a new versioned URL). The framework's runtime serves those URLs from the cached copies. Cached standards remain under the stewardship of their original publisher; the framework's governance applies to content the framework owns.

story.name: SessionStart and PostCompact boot duties dispatched via chathealthy_enforcement_manager
story.description: On every Claude Code SessionStart hook and on every PostCompact hook (context purge), the boot program replays the most recent conversation utterances from MongoDB and injects the agile_backlog taxonomy. Dispatch is performed by chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py per Rule-002 enforcement entries; the boot is no longer wired directly in .claude/settings.json.

requirement.name: Replay 170 most recent utterances from Mongo into SessionStart additionalContext
requirement.requirement: On SessionStart, chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST read the 170 most recent utterance documents from MongoDB ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive, trim each document to {actor, content}, order newest-first, and emit them as part of the hook's additionalContext so Claude resumes with recent conversation context. If the MongoDB read fails (connection, auth, or query error), the boot MUST fail open - log the failure to stderr and continue with remaining SessionStart duties without aborting the session.

requirement.name: Inject agile_backlog taxonomy (epic+feature descriptions, story names) into SessionStart additionalContext
requirement.requirement: On SessionStart, chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST read brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json and emit the business taxonomy as part of the hook's additionalContext: every epic's id, name, and description; every feature's id, name, and description; every story's id and name. Story descriptions, requirements, and tests MUST NOT be emitted. The output is the operator-facing context shape, not a context-resident @-import.

requirement.name: Read hook_event_name from stdin to branch SessionStart and PostCompact dispatch
requirement.requirement: chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST read the Claude Code hook payload JSON from stdin and dispatch on the hook_event_name field. SessionStart and PostCompact MUST each execute the two duties in EPIC-008-F-002-S-007-REQ-T-002 and EPIC-008-F-002-S-007-REQ-T-003 in order. Any other hook_event_name value MUST be a no-op that exits 0. Each branch MUST be wrapped in try/except/finally that calls sys.exit so control always returns to the enforcement manager.

requirement.name: Boot is invoked exclusively through Rule-002 enforcement entries, not direct settings.json wiring
requirement.requirement: chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST NOT appear directly in .claude/settings.json hooks. It is invoked exclusively via Rule-002 enforcement entries (Rule-002-ENF-001 on SessionStart, Rule-002-ENF-002 on PostCompact) dispatched by chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py. .claude/settings.json registers only the enforcement manager (one entry per hook); the manager loads engineering_rules.json and spawns the matching enforcement workers.

feature.name: Brain Consistency
feature.description: Ensures all brain JSON data is internally consistent, cross-referenced, and free of orphaned records. Enforcement mechanisms run deterministically on boot and at check-in.

story.description: On the first user prompt, Claude Code MUST boot the governance singleton and ask the user to select an operating mode (1 = Unattended, 2 = Normal, 3 = Idiot). There MUST be no SessionStart hook. Known bug: BUG-AUTH-001.

requirement.requirement: CLAUDE.md MUST state only that the boot class governs the session.
requirement.name: CLAUDE.md states only that boot class governs the session

requirement.requirement: Each Claude Code session MUST complete a deterministic, non-circumventable boot sequence before any other work. The sequence is: (1) load the governance brain and run compliance checks; (2) at the end of boot, ask the user exactly two questions in order and block all other assistant output until both are answered â€” Q1: mode selection per REQ-010; Q2: orphan triage per REQ-011. The sequence MUST NOT be skippable, paraphrasable, summarizable, or deferrable by Claude Code. Implementation MAY use any hook topology (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop-hook validator, blocking-reply pattern) so long as the user-observable behavior holds: every new session begins with those two questions presented verbatim, in order, with no other assistant output preceding them.
requirement.name: Enforce deterministic boot: governance + 2 mandatory verbatim questions before I

requirement.requirement: After boot completes, Claude Code MUST ask the user to select an operating mode: 1 = Unattended, 2 = Normal, 3 = Idiot. Claude Code MUST NOT proceed until the user has made a selection.

requirement.requirement: Orphan triage is the second of the two boot questions. After the user answers REQ-010, Claude Code MUST ask a single yes/no question: 'Triage orphan bugs?' If the user answers no, boot completes and normal work begins. If the user answers yes, Claude Code MUST present the orphan bug table and the user chooses how many to triage this boot â€” one, several, or all. Triaging an orphan means assigning it a req_id or closing it. There is no per-orphan defer option and no obligation to triage every orphan; the single yes/no gate governs whether the list is shown at all, and within 'yes' the user drives how many get worked.

requirement.requirement: Every action taken within this project MUST be governed by any applicable rule found in brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json. requirement.requirement: The user MUST NOT be forced to login twice during the boot sequence.
