The deployer MUST navigate the collection's target-keyed shape (filter records by `target_kind`; read the entry in `environments[]` whose `env_binding` matches the target environment â€” `dev`, `qa`, or `prod` â€” for the addressable node; iterate `files[]` for source-file composition) rather than any flat lookup. The deployer MUST NOT carry any hardcoded ports dict, container dict, or path constant in source. All facts necessary to build, deploy assets to, or describe a server in the ChatHealthy digital portfolio must reside only in the local .env file or the single source of truth for these facts. Any constant previously embedded in source that drives deploy behavior MUST move into the appropriate TargetRecord verbatim. After migration, no port number, container name, or file-system path that drives deployed-env deploy behavior MAY appear as a literal in any resource other than the Brain file, 'deployment_architecture.json'. If it is necessary to construct YAML, DOCKER, or other files in order to accomplish a build or deployment to a server, those assets MUST be built during the primary script's execution and deleted as soon as possible after being transmitted to the nodes that need them.

requirement.name: Promote chain pairs are invariant; only (localâ†’dev), (devâ†’qa), (qaâ†’prod) are valid
requirement.requirement: The promote chain is invariant. The ONLY valid (source, destination) pairs the promote workflow MUST accept are exactly three: (local, dev), (dev, qa), (qa, prod). Any other pair â€” including (local, qa), (local, prod), (dev, prod), (qa, dev), (prod, qa), (dev, local), or any self-pair â€” MUST be rejected at the input layer before any git, build, or filesystem action runs. The rejection MUST fail loud with a message naming the invalid pair and citing this requirement.

requirement.name: Promote destination becomes byte-identical to source; merge semantics forbidden
requirement.requirement: For every promote step, the destination branch MUST become byte-identical to the source branch tip at the moment promote runs. The promote workflow MUST achieve this via 'git reset --hard origin/<source>' + 'git push --force-with-lease origin <target>'. The promote workflow MUST NOT use 'git merge', 'git merge --ff-only', 'git rebase', 'git cherry-pick', or any other operation whose post-condition leaves the destination's tree differing from source by even one byte. Any commit, docstring, comment, or related artifact that describes promote as a 'merge' or 'fast-forward merge' is forbidden and MUST be corrected.

story.name: Prod-only behaviors
story.description: The only differences between prod and the dev/qa environments, aside from their different addresses, are: (1) the chrome banner with versions and navigation between the servers does not appear in prod, and (2) the security GUI widget does not appear in prod.

requirement.name: Version & framework ID assignment
requirement.requirement: When environment=prod, after human UAT sign-off, the deploy script accepts human-supplied values for a new version ID (and potentially a new framework ID) and writes them to the version document (per S-001-REQ-T-002). Dev and qa deploys never change these fields. No automation, ever, sets version or framework.

requirement.name: Display chrome OFF
requirement.requirement: In prod, the non-prod display chrome (S-005) MUST NOT render: no environment banner, no security token panel, no service-switching buttons. The smoke test (S-006) skips display-chrome checks when env=prod via its macro-variance dimension.

story.name: Non-prod display chrome
story.description: Display chrome visible in local, dev, and qa; absent in prod (see S-004-REQ-B-002). Owns the environment banner, the security-token panel, and the three service-switching buttons. Banner reads /health from whichever service currently owns the page (FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices).

requirement.name: Banner contents
requirement.requirement: The environment banner displays environment label (LOCAL/DEV/QA), version, framework, and build, fetched from the /health endpoint of whichever service currently owns the page. All values render on one line with sufficient spacing for human readability. The banner displays the active service name in brackets (e.g., [evaluatecare]).

requirement.name: Banner re-fetches on ownership transfer
requirement.requirement: When page ownership transfers between services, the banner re-fetches /health from the new owner and updates inline.

requirement.name: Service buttons + active is cold
requirement.requirement: Three service-switching buttons (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) appear in the banner. The currently-active service's button is cold (greyed, disabled); on click it shows tooltip 'You are here already'. The other two buttons are hot (clickable, styled). Clicking a hot button transfers page ownership to that service, which then controls the entire frame. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

requirement.name: Unimplemented placeholder
requirement.requirement: The center panel displays the service name and 'is still unimplemented.' when SharedServices or EvaluateCare has control, until those services have real implementations. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

requirement.name: Security token panel
requirement.requirement: Each service displays a security token panel rendered per the mock at {projectRoot}/brain/machine_artifacts/diagramsAndImages/GUIImagesAndMockUps/NonProdSecuriytToken.jpg. Right panel and lower regions display the security information defined by EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-007. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

story.name: Smoke test
story.description: One master Playwright pytest (`Code/deploy/localSmokeTestPyTest.py`) runs against any environment. The script varies along three dimensions: (1) environment â€” localhost / dev / qa / prod; (2) macro variance â€” display chrome (banner, token, service buttons) is exercised in non-prod and skipped in prod per S-004-REQ-B-002; (3) micro variance â€” PKI certificates differ across environments and the cert-verification step asserts the env-appropriate cert is in use. The actual script is the source of truth: where these requirements differ from the script's behavior, the script wins and these requirements MUST be reverse-engineered to match. Per-step requirements below (REQ-B-002 through REQ-B-037) capture each test class in the script.

requirement.name: Master smoke-test contract
requirement.requirement: `localSmokeTestPyTest.py` is the single master smoke test. It accepts the target environment as a parameter and exercises every step below in declared order. Every step MUST pass for the smoke test to PASS overall.

requirement.name: Step 00 â€” Build gate: local and dev report identical build
requirement.requirement: Smoke test fetches /health from local FindCare and dev FindCare and asserts the `build` field matches across the two envs. Two environments on the same build MUST be running identical code and configuration; mismatched builds halt the smoke test before any further steps.

requirement.name: Step 01 â€” HTTPâ†’HTTPS redirect
requirement.requirement: Browser navigation to http://{domain} MUST 301-redirect to https://{domain}. The smoke test deliberately probes the insecure scheme (constructed at runtime) and asserts the final URL is https://.

requirement.name: Step 02 â€” Banner shows env label, version, framework, build
requirement.requirement: The environment banner element (`#envBanner`) MUST be visible and contain the env label (LOCAL/DEV/QA), and the literal strings `Version: <v>`, `Framework: <f>`, `Build: <b>` whose values match the response from the active service's /health.

requirement.name: Step 03 â€” SharedServices button is a banner button
requirement.requirement: A `<button>` with `data-service='sharedservices'` MUST exist inside `#envBanner` (not in any header nav), MUST be visible, and its label MUST be `SharedServices` (PascalCase, no space).

requirement.name: Step 04 â€” Splash renders welcome words
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe loads. The first 10 words of the canonical welcome message (per `_get_welcome_words`) MUST appear in the iframe body text.

requirement.name: Step 05 â€” Chat input enabled and focused on click
requirement.requirement: The chat input element (`input[placeholder*='Type a message']` or textarea) MUST be visible, MUST NOT carry a `disabled` attribute, and MUST become focused when clicked.

requirement.name: Step 06 â€” Search returns providers
requirement.requirement: Submitting `Find me a bone doctor in Delaware` MUST yield results containing NPI strings (`NPI[:\s]+\d{10}`) in the iframe body within the chat timeout. The smoke test captures the originating session token for downstream nonce comparisons.

requirement.name: Step 07 â€” Specialty checkboxes appear in left panel
requirement.requirement: After a search, `#leftPanel` MUST contain at least one `input[type='checkbox']` representing a specialty.

requirement.name: Step 08 â€” Left panel cell layout and scroll cap
requirement.requirement: The left panel MUST contain exactly four `[data-cell]` cells (1..4) with reactive percentage heights 18/40/20/22 (declared via `flex:0 0 N%` or `height:N%` â€” pixel heights are forbidden). An Uncheck All / Check All toggle MUST live inside cell 1 (the green header). With more than 12 prescribers present, no more than 12 specialty checkboxes may be visible in cell 2 without scrolling.

requirement.name: Step 09 â€” Provider NPIs in center frame
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe body MUST contain provider NPI strings (`NPI[:\s]+\d{10}`) after the search resolves.

requirement.name: Step 10 â€” Bottom panel zero before selection
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe body MUST contain `0 / 5` (or `0/5`) reflecting an empty Selected for Evaluation panel before any provider is selected.

requirement.name: Step 11 â€” Select up to three providers
requirement.requirement: Up to three provider Select-for-Evaluation buttons MUST be clickable; the smoke test clicks min(count, 3) of them.

requirement.name: Step 12 â€” Selected providers appear in bottom panel
requirement.requirement: After selection, the iframe body MUST include the words `SELECTED` and `EVALUATION` and the count must read 1..5 / 5 (no longer 0).

requirement.name: Step 13 â€” Evaluate button click
requirement.requirement: An Evaluate button (`#guiEvalBtn` or text-matched `Evaluate`) MUST be present and clickable; the smoke test clicks it to trigger handoff to EvaluateCare.

requirement.name: Step 14 â€” EvaluateCare has frame control
requirement.requirement: After the Evaluate click, the chat iframe (`#coreChatFrame`) MUST be hidden and `#evalcareSplash` MUST be visible â€” EvaluateCare owns the frame.

requirement.name: Step 15 â€” mTLS to EvaluateCare TLS 1.2+
requirement.requirement: An mTLS handshake from the smoke test (using FindCare's client cert + key against the CA cert) to localhost:EVALCARE_PORT MUST succeed with TLS version 1.2 or higher. Failure of the handshake (SSLError) is a hard failure.

requirement.name: Step 16 â€” Right panel shows EvaluateCare + provider NPIs
requirement.requirement: `#rightPanel` text MUST contain `EVALUATECARE` (case-insensitive substring) and at least one 10-digit NPI string after the EvaluateCare handoff.

requirement.name: Step 17 â€” Token same sent/received; positioned below specialties
requirement.requirement: The handoff FindCareâ†’EvaluateCare MUST yield a fresh nonce; the session GUID MUST remain identical. The session token element (`#guiSessionCell` or `#guiSessionId`) MUST be positioned below the specialty list (its bounding-box `y` must be greater than the bottom of the scroll container), not beside it.

requirement.name: Step 18 â€” Token components in distinct colors in both panels
requirement.requirement: Both right panel and left panel MUST show signed-token components in distinct colors: signed token in indigo (`#6366f1`), nonce in amber (`#d97706`), GUID in teal (`#0b7a75`). Right and left panels MUST present the same color treatment.

requirement.name: Step 19 â€” Nonce changed after EvaluateCare handoff; GUID preserved
requirement.requirement: After the FindCareâ†’EvaluateCare handoff, the EvaluateCare-side nonce MUST differ from the original FindCare nonce; the EvaluateCare-side GUID MUST equal the original GUID.

requirement.name: Step 20 â€” EvaluateCare splash text
requirement.requirement: `#evalcareSplash` MUST be visible and contain the literal strings `EvaluateCare` and `is still unimplemented`.

requirement.name: Step 21 â€” Filter toggle change
requirement.requirement: Clicking the first specialty `[data-gui-action='filter-toggle']` checkbox MUST register and trigger the gui:reset path on apply. The toggle clicked MUST be a specialty filter-toggle (not a filter-provider-type) so that the return to FindCare proceeds via gui:reset.

requirement.name: Step 22 â€” Apply filter returns control to FindCare
requirement.requirement: Clicking `[data-gui-action='filter-apply']` MUST: (1) restore visibility of `#coreChatFrame`; (2) hide both `#evalcareSplash` and `#sharedSplash`; (3) cause the FindCare welcome message to repaint (â‰¥20 of the first 25 welcome words present in the iframe body within ~15 seconds).

requirement.name: Step 23 â€” Chat input visible and focused after return
requirement.requirement: After return to FindCare, the chat input element MUST be visible and focused within the polling window (15 retries / 1s).

requirement.name: Step 24 â€” Nonce changed on EvaluateCareâ†’FindCare return
requirement.requirement: The handoff EvaluateCareâ†’FindCare MUST yield a fresh nonce different from both the original FindCare nonce and the EvaluateCare nonce; the GUID MUST remain unchanged.

requirement.name: Step 25 â€” SharedServices button push: direct, not proxied
requirement.requirement: Clicking the SharedServices banner button MUST result in: (1) `#rightPanel` showing `Shared Services`; (2) at least one POST to `<SHARED_URL>/verify-token` directly (not proxied through FindCare's `/shared/verify-token`); (3) `#rightPanel` text containing `Server, serving security token: SharedServices` (self-identifying responding service, not the token signer).

requirement.name: Step 26 â€” SharedServices has frame control
requirement.requirement: After the SharedServices push, `#coreChatFrame` MUST be hidden and `#sharedSplash` MUST be visible.

requirement.name: Step 27 â€” mTLS to SharedServices TLS 1.2+
requirement.requirement: An mTLS handshake from the smoke test (using FindCare's client cert + key against the CA cert) to localhost:SHARED_PORT MUST succeed with TLS version 1.2 or higher.

requirement.name: Step 28 â€” SharedServices splash renders the live User Object
requirement.requirement: After the user clicks the SharedServices banner button, the center panel `#sharedSplash` MUST be visible and MUST render the User Object as follows: (1) Header containing the literal 'Shared Services â€” User Object'. (2) An 'Identity' subsection that lists, on labeled rows: `user_type` with the literal value `Guest` (the universal pre-registration identity), `guid` as a 32-character lowercase hex string, `origin` with the literal value `SharedServices`, `server_env`, `created_at`, and `expires_at`. (3) A 'Session Conversation History' subsection. If the underlying admin.Sessions doc carries no `ux_events` and no `utterances` yet, the subsection MUST display the literal 'No UX events or utterances yet.'; otherwise it MUST render the conversation as four parallel scroll-bar threads with the following exact taxonomy: a thread labeled 'Person' carrying ONLY typed utterances (never UX clicks); a thread labeled 'Person â†’ System' carrying UX-control / nav-button clicks; a thread labeled 'Machine' carrying pedantic responses to UX events plus tool results returned via the utterance bridge; and a thread labeled 'LLM â†’ System' carrying every LLM emission (clarifications directed at the person and tool invocations directed at the machine, collapsed into one stream). Each thread MUST be in its own scrollable container; small (â‰¤11px) body font. The splash content is computed server-side by the SharedServices splash op invoked through the universal front door (POST /gate). The FindCare page renders the returned HTML verbatim.

requirement.name: Step 29 â€” SharedServices token auth: GUID preserved, nonce fresh
requirement.requirement: `#rightPanel` header MUST read `SHARED SERVICES` (case-insensitive). The handoff FindCareâ†’SharedServices MUST yield a fresh nonce; GUID MUST equal the original.

requirement.name: Step 30 â€” SharedServices nonce/GUID stored and verified
requirement.requirement: The SharedServices-side nonce and GUID captured in step 29 MUST be present in test state; the GUID MUST equal the original FindCare GUID.

requirement.name: Step 31 â€” Handoff 4: SharedServicesâ†’FindCare via filter
requirement.requirement: Clicking a specialty checkbox and Apply Filter MUST return control to FindCare (`#coreChatFrame` visible). The handoff MUST yield a fresh nonce.

requirement.name: Step 32 â€” Handoff 5: EvaluateCareâ†’SharedServices direct
requirement.requirement: After re-selecting a provider and clicking Evaluate, then clicking the SharedServices banner button from the EvaluateCare context, `#rightPanel` MUST show `Shared Services`. The handoff MUST yield a fresh nonce.

requirement.name: Step 33 â€” Handoff 6: SharedServicesâ†’EvaluateCare via re-evaluate
requirement.requirement: Returning to FindCare via filter, then re-selecting and clicking Evaluate, MUST hand control to EvaluateCare directly from the SharedServicesâ†’FindCare path. The handoff MUST yield a fresh nonce.

requirement.name: Step 34 â€” All four services respond on HTTPS with expected JSON
requirement.requirement: Final assertion: `GET https://<BASE_URL>/` returns HTTP 200; `GET <FINDCARE_URL>/health` returns JSON with `status=="ok"`; `GET <EVALCARE_URL>/health` returns JSON with `service=="evaluate_care"`; `GET <SHARED_URL>/health` returns JSON with `service=="shared_services"`.

requirement.name: Step 35 â€” Comprehensive PKI certificate verification (NEW)
requirement.requirement: The smoke test MUST hold the public certs of every server participating in mTLS (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) and assert: (a) every cert file in {projectRoot}/Code/Shared/ops/certs/ parses as a valid PKI X.509 certificate, is signed by the project's CA cert (ca.crt), and is not expired; (b) for each ordered server pair (FindCareâ†”EvaluateCare, FindCareâ†”SharedServices, EvaluateCareâ†”SharedServices), an mTLS handshake succeeds in BOTH directions using the appropriate client cert against the CA. The point of the step is to assert real mutual-PKI rather than any subset (Steps 15 and 27 cover only FindCareâ†’EvaluateCare and FindCareâ†’SharedServices; this step fills the gap and adds explicit cert-validity checks).

requirement.name: Test Provider Detail
requirement.requirement: After clicking on a 'provider detail' link in a list of providers in the center panel, the smoke test shall assert if all requirements of EPIC-006-F-025-S-001 â€” 'Provider Detail display.' have been satisfied.

story.name: Step notices and human-instructed bell
story.description: On-screen notices at significant deploy steps (the mechanism for S-001-REQ-B-005). The bell is HUMAN-INSTRUCTED ONLY: it never rings as default behavior. Default deploy behavior is silent except for the on-screen notices.

requirement.name: Step notices
requirement.requirement: At each significant deploy step the script MUST display an on-screen notice. Significant steps are: (1) deploy started for {environment}; (2) old environment torn down and ready to receive new; (3) new environment built; (4) smoke test started; (5) smoke test ended, with ratio (passed/total) of assertions and list of any failures.

requirement.name: Bell rings only on explicit human instruction
requirement.requirement: The bell MUST NOT ring by default. The human operator may instruct Claude (via IDE prompt, command-line flag, or other explicit invocation) to ring the bell at specific times, in specific patterns. The operator chooses both WHEN and HOW. There is no requirement for unattended-deploy bell behavior; all deploys are human-supervised (per S-001-REQ-B-006).

story.name: React serving migration (opportunistic architectural evolution, one-time)
story.description: ONE-TIME architectural evolution included opportunistically in this deploy-management feature. Moves the React frontend serving responsibility from FindCare (port 7860) to SharedServices (port 8002). After this story ships, it is permanently done â€” it does NOT belong to the enduring deploy facts and never re-fires.

requirement.name: React serving moves to SharedServices
requirement.requirement: After this story ships, SharedServices (port 8002 per S-001-REQ-T-001) serves the React frontend in addition to its backend. FindCare (port 7860) serves only the FindCare backend. No other behavioral change.

requirement.name: Build URLs updated
requirement.requirement: S-001-REQ-T-008 (the universal React build req) builds the React frontend with the SharedServices URL baked in. Pre-migration FindCare URL is removed from all build paths.

requirement.name: Smoke test passes post-migration
requirement.requirement: The master smoke test (S-006) passes against an environment where SharedServices serves the React frontend, with no regression in any of the current step set (Step00..Step34 plus the cert-verification step in S-006-REQ-T-003 â€” currently 36 steps total).

story.name: Local Development File System & local Code Repository Management
story.description: This story specifies how the local file system will materialize on the disk and in the Cursor IDE. It will also specify the file system's relationship to the local Git, which is an exact mirror, when pushed, of the same repository on GitHub. Due 2026-05-22.

requirement.name: Physical and IDE file system mirror agile_backlog hierarchy at root, free of deployment details and technical clutter
requirement.requirement: The physical file system, as well as the file system displayed in the project view of the IDE, MUST reflect the hierarchy defined by agile_backlog.json. It MUST do so at the root. It MUST NOT reflect any deployment details or be burdened with unnecessary technical clutter.

requirement.name: No code file spans more than one feature
requirement.requirement: No code file CAN span more than one feature. Each source file belongs to exactly one feature in the agile_backlog hierarchy.

requirement.name: Python packaging artifacts live in the deployment feature, not in business-model paths
requirement.requirement: Files such as `__init__.py` MUST reside in a deployment-feature path and MUST NOT reside on a business-model â†’ file system path. Other examples of such files are `pyproject.toml`, `__pycache__/`, and other Python packaging or runtime-tooling artifacts.

requirement.name: IDE view = physical file system = agile_backlog hierarchy down to Feature level
requirement.requirement: All directories as reflected by the IDE MUST be a one-to-one reflection of the physical file system, which MUST be a mirror of the hierarchy of the agile_backlog to the level of the Features.

requirement.name: Downstream artifacts on disk are never authored by hand; Extractor is the sole writer
requirement.requirement: Every downstream on-disk artifact that corresponds to a `files[]` row in any TargetRecord (workflow YAMLs, Dockerfiles, shell scripts, bat scripts, certs, keys, static assets, and any other `handler_type` in the V18 enum) MUST be authored only by Extractor's `materialize` writing `embedded_content` byte-for-byte to `source_location`. Hand-authoring or hand-editing of any such file MUST be detected at the commit boundary as `file_drift` (REQ-T-031) and MUST be rejected with the bare reject form.

requirement.name: Local Code Repository Management retires Code/deploy/ in favor of architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/code/
requirement.requirement: After migration to V18, the `Code/deploy/` directory MUST NOT contain any deploy chain implementation module. Every file previously living under `Code/deploy/` that is a deploy chain implementation module (Builder, Extractor, Crosswalk, RecordLoader, RecordWriter, DeploymentCollection, SecretsResolver, PreCommitHook, local deployer, CLI bootstrap) MUST be moved to `architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/code/` and the corresponding `files[i].source_location` in every affected TargetRecord MUST be updated to the new repo-relative path. The crosswalk validator's coverage check MUST be re-run after the move; any stale path MUST cause REJECT.

requirement.name: File-system level rename or move of a managed file requires a deliberate Builder.build_record invocation
requirement.requirement: When the operator renames or moves a file that is referenced by `files[i].source_location` in any TargetRecord, the affected TargetRecord(s) MUST be refreshed by a deliberate `Builder.build_record(target_id, repo_root)` invocation per-target. No watcher, no IDE save event, and no auto-extractor side effect MAY refresh a TargetRecord in response to a filesystem event. If the operator commits without running Builder, Crosswalk's `check_file_drift` (REQ-T-031) MUST detect the divergence at the commit boundary and PreCommitHook MUST return `1` with the bare-reject form (REQ-T-028).
