feature.name: Conversation-log Pipeline (Claude Code hooks -> Kafka -> MongoDB)
feature.description: DevOps feature that owns the end-to-end pipeline by which every Claude Code and Claude utterance is recorded. Each UserPromptSubmit and Stop hook events are persisted to long-term storage in the Mongo Db. The pipeline has three runtime components: (a) a hook-driven publisher worker that POSTs the raw hook payload to a local producer sidecar, (b) the producer sidecar HTTP service on 127.0.0.1:8100 that forwards to the conversation_log Kafka topic, and (c) a consumer that drains the topic and persists each message to MongoDB ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive. Rule-001 in engineering_rules.json is the runtime enforcement vehicle for the publisher leg of this feature.

story.name: Publisher leg - hook-driven POST to local sidecar with browser-popup failure signaling
story.description: Per-hook-event publication of the raw payload from Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks to the local producer sidecar at http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce. On sidecar unreachability the publisher MUST signal the operator visibly via a fullscreen browser warning page so the operator is never silently disconnected from the archive. This story is the implementation home for the three Rule-001 statements; Rule-001 itself is the engineering-rules vehicle that wires the worker into the hook framework.

requirement.name: UserPromptSubmit hook publishes raw payload to local producer sidecar
requirement.requirement: On every Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook event, the conversation-log publisher worker MUST read the raw hook payload from stdin and POST the unmodified JSON body to http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce with Content-Type: application/json and a request header X-Hook-Event identifying the hook event name. The POST MUST complete within the hook's configured timeout (15 seconds per Rule-001-ENF-001). A 2xx response from the sidecar is the success criterion; the worker MUST exit 0 on success.

requirement.name: Stop hook publishes raw payload to local producer sidecar
requirement.requirement: On every Claude Code Stop hook event, the conversation-log publisher worker MUST read the raw hook payload from stdin and POST the unmodified JSON body to http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce with Content-Type: application/json and X-Hook-Event identifying the hook event name. The POST MUST complete within the hook's configured timeout (15 seconds per Rule-001-ENF-002). A 2xx response is the success criterion; the worker MUST exit 0 on success.

requirement.name: Sidecar-unreachable failure shows fullscreen browser warning page to the operator
requirement.requirement: If the POST to http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce fails for any reason (connection refused, timeout, non-2xx response, OSError), the worker MUST write a viewport-filling HTML failure page to a temp-directory file and launch the operator's default browser pointed at that file. The page MUST state in unmistakable language that the conversation-log pipeline is DOWN, that Claude Code interactions are NOT being persisted, and that the operator must restart the producer sidecar. The worker MUST exit non-zero on this path so the failure surfaces in the hook's telemetry.

requirement.name: Publisher worker is wired via engineering_rules.json (Rule-001), not directly in settings.json
requirement.requirement: The conversation_log_publisher_worker.py worker MUST be invoked via the V19 engineering-rules enforcement architecture: Rule-001 declares two enforcement entries (Rule-001-ENF-001 for UserPromptSubmit, Rule-001-ENF-002 for Stop) whose executable_path points at the worker. .claude/settings.json registers the UserPromptSubmit and Stop hook commands as chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py --hook <hook> only. The settings.json file MUST NOT call the worker directly, and the worker MUST NOT be invoked by any legacy dispatch path (governance_matrix.json or chathealthy_devops_boot.py's removed conversation_log_worker class).

story.name: Producer sidecar - local HTTP service on 127.0.0.1:8100 forwarding to Kafka topic
story.description: The local producer sidecar is an HTTP service bound to 127.0.0.1:8100 that accepts POST /produce, treats the request body as an opaque JSON payload, and forwards it to the conversation_log Kafka topic. The sidecar isolates the publisher worker from Kafka client configuration, transport credentials, and broker addressing - the worker speaks plain HTTP and the sidecar speaks Kafka. Implementation lives at Code/Shared/ops/ChatHealthyLogService/.

requirement.name: Sidecar binds only to loopback at 127.0.0.1:8100 and accepts POST /produce
requirement.requirement: The producer sidecar MUST bind only to 127.0.0.1 (loopback) on TCP port 8100 and MUST NOT bind to any externally-routable interface. It MUST accept HTTP POST on path /produce with Content-Type: application/json, treating the request body as an opaque JSON payload to be forwarded unchanged to the conversation_log Kafka topic. It MUST respond with HTTP 2xx on successful produce and HTTP 5xx (or connection refusal) on any failure to forward.

requirement.name: Sidecar forwards the request body unchanged to the conversation_log Kafka topic
requirement.requirement: The producer sidecar MUST publish the request body to the Kafka topic named 'conversation_log' without modification. The sidecar MUST NOT add, remove, reorder, or otherwise mutate any fields of the JSON payload. The hook event identifier carried in the X-Hook-Event request header MAY be propagated as a Kafka message header but MUST NOT be merged into the payload body.

story.name: Consumer leg - drain conversation_log topic to MongoDB ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive
story.description: The conversation_log consumer drains the conversation_log Kafka topic and persists each message as one document to MongoDB cluster ClaudeCodeLog, collection conversation_log_archive. The consumer is the durability boundary for the pipeline - once a message is committed to the archive collection, it is considered persisted for forensic and operator-review purposes.

requirement.name: Consumer persists each Kafka message as one document in conversation_log_archive
requirement.requirement: The conversation_log consumer MUST consume the conversation_log Kafka topic and insert each message as exactly one document into MongoDB collection ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive. The consumer MUST NOT drop, merge, or batch-rewrite messages. It MUST acknowledge each Kafka offset only after the MongoDB insert returns success so an at-least-once delivery property holds across consumer restarts.

requirement.name: Consumer transforms malformed Kafka messages so every utterance lands in conversation_log_archive
requirement.requirement: The conversation_log consumer MUST treat every Kafka message as durable and MUST NOT reject or discard a message because the payload is malformed. For each message consumed from the conversation_log topic, the consumer MUST produce exactly one document in MongoDB collection ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive. When the payload is not valid JSON, when required fields (for example actor or content) are missing, when bytes are not valid UTF-8, or when content is not a string, the consumer MUST wrap, coerce, or annotate the record so that an insert_many call against the archive collection succeeds. The transformed document MUST carry a cleanup-description field that names the transformation applied (for example raw-bytes-wrapped, json-parse-failed, actor-defaulted, content-coerced-to-string). Legibility of the utterance MUST be degraded as little as possible by the transformation; loss of the utterance is forbidden. When a record fails to be written for any reason an operational response is demanded. And Rule-002 statement #5 brings this failure to the attention of a human operator.

requirement.name: Consumer redacts credentials with model-based redaction; retries on failure; stores unredacted on final failure with a pointer to the error file
requirement.requirement: Before inserting a record into ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive, the conversation_log consumer MUST submit the content field to a model-based credentials-redaction step (not regex). The redaction step MUST replace API keys, passwords, connection strings, tokens, secrets, and credentials with the literal marker [Sensitive content redacted] and MUST leave all other text exactly as-is. The redaction engine MUST be an LLM call (currently gpt-4.1-mini). The LLM system prompt MUST include the project's Code/.env file as a non-exhaustive reference (the sensitive term might not be in .env). The LLM user prompt MUST include the last 5 utterances prior to the current utterance, queried from ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive by descending timestamp_utc, so the model can contextualize what a secret might be. The consumer MUST retry the LLM call up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1s, 2s). After 3 attempts have all failed, the consumer MUST store the ORIGINAL unredacted content (durability of REQ-T-001 takes precedence over redaction success). On final failure, the consumer MUST append one JSONL line of the form {"timestamp_utc": "...", "mongo_id": "<inserted_id>", "error": "<terse cause>"} to the consumer error file at %TEMP%/chathealthy_consumer_errors.log, capturing the ObjectId returned by the Mongo insert so the failed record can be located operationally.

requirement.name: Consumer redacts profanity in content via model-based redaction with fail-open fallback
requirement.requirement: Before inserting a record into ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive, the conversation_log consumer MUST submit the content field to a model-based profanity-redaction step (not regex). The redaction step MUST replace profanity and vulgar language with the literal marker [expletive deleted] and MUST leave all other text exactly as-is. The redaction engine MUST be an LLM call (currently gpt-4.1-mini). The redaction MUST be a single attempt with no retries. If the redaction call fails or returns an error, the consumer MUST fall back to storing the unredacted content rather than dropping the message; the durability obligation of REQ-T-001 takes precedence over redaction success. Profanity redaction MUST run AFTER credentials redaction, so that if credentials redaction substituted any markers, profanity redaction operates on the already-credentials-handled content.

epic.name: Pipelines
epic.description: This epic defines all the requirements for ChatHealthy's data pipelines, which do data ETL and data quality management, and data enrichment. All of the code lives and executes in Azure and writes to the ChatHealthyDataPipelines cluster.

feature.name: DB Infrastructure Management
feature.description: Operational management of the MongoDB Atlas cluster, the Azure resources hosting the pipeline data, and the data pipeline processing tier. Covers pausing/resuming the cluster around active pipeline work, maintaining the cluster tier at the smallest practical size between runs, and orchestrating the Azure Functions worker scale for the pipeline app itself, plus storage account management.

story.name: Manage Pipeline Cluster Pauses
story.description: This story specifies the requirements for pausing the pipeline cluster when no live work is using it, resuming + warming it up when a Pipeline job starts and it is paused, and using reservations to ensure the cluster will not be paused while work is taking place. Pauses are reservation-driven: while reservations exist the cluster stays up; when reservations[] is empty the cluster is paused. Both orchestrators and human operators can hold reservations. A separate reaper safety process catches reservations that are not removed (e.g. job ab-end before its release) and pauses the cluster anyway.

requirement.name: Reservations
requirement.requirement: The pipeline cluster's pause/resume lifecycle is driven by a reservations table. While at least one live reservation exists the cluster stays unpaused; when reservations[] is empty and cluster_state==IDLE the cluster gets paused.

requirement.name: Orchestration Make Reservation
requirement.requirement: Every pipeline orchestrator MUST register a reservation at the start of its run (cluster_name, job_id, requester, expected_duration_minutes, reservation_class='automated') and MUST wait for cluster IDLE, the signal that the cluster is ready to transact, before doing work.

requirement.name: Orchestration Delete Reservation
requirement.requirement: Every pipeline orchestrator MUST delete its reservation when it completes â€” both on the happy path AND on failure paths (via try/finally or equivalent guarantee). Orphaned reservations from crashes are caught by the lifecycle reaper as a backstop, not as the primary mechanism.

requirement.name: Externally Cluster Uptime
requirement.requirement: An external operator MUST be able to hold the cluster up for a bounded human window by registering a reservation with reservation_class='human'. Human-class reservations are never auto-reaped by the reservation reaper.

requirement.name: Warm-up
requirement.requirement: On resume from pause, the cluster lifecycle layer MUST poll Atlas until cluster_state==IDLE before any reservation reports back ready. No work is dispatched against a non-IDLE cluster.

requirement.name: Parent orchestrator reserves Mongo pipeline cluster in wakeup phase
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§5.1 (Wakeup): the parent orchestrator (one instance per run) MUST call ClusterLifecycleManager.register_reservation_activity as the first step of the run, before any throttle configure and before any source-gather work is dispatched. Per v9 Â§11.0 (business rules preserved): the cluster reservation contract is unchanged from the legacy pipeline.

requirement.name: Parent orchestrator releases cluster reservation in finally block
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§8.6 (streaming_pipeline_orchestrator_fn) and Â§13.1 (failed Mongo bulk_write): the parent orchestrator MUST call release_cluster_activity inside a finally block so that the reservation is released on both happy-path and failure-path exit. Per v9 Â§13.1: 'the cluster reservation is released in the parent's finally block. The pipeline run is marked failed.'

story.name: Manage Pipeline Cluster Scale
story.description: Control of the Atlas cluster tier (M10/M20/M30/etc.). Atlas preserves whatever tier was set across pauses, so deliberate downsizing belongs here, not as a side effect of pause/resume.

requirement.name: Maintain Cluster Tier at Smallest Practical Size
requirement.requirement: Between active pipeline runs the cluster MUST be held at the smallest tier that still serves any standing queries against pipeline collections. Pipeline orchestrators are responsible for scaling UP to JOB_TIER (with lock_tier=True) at the start of a run and scaling DOWN to the baseline tier at the end.

story.name: Manage Azure Scale
story.description: Pre-warm and cool down the Azure Functions Flex Consumption always_ready instance count around a pipeline fan-out. Prevents the two-wave cold-start pattern that causes OOM (exit code 137) when activities crowd onto too few workers.

requirement.name: Warm Instances
requirement.requirement: Before fan-out, the pipeline orchestrator MUST PATCH always_ready = num_workers via the Azure Management API (Managed Identity or Service Principal) and wait for the propagation latency to elapse before dispatching activities.

requirement.name: Cool Instances
requirement.requirement: After the pipeline completes, the orchestrator MUST PATCH always_ready = 0 so the function app is not billed for idle workers between runs.

requirement.name: warm_instances_activity call in infrastructure setup phase
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§5.4 (Infrastructure setup): the parent orchestrator MUST call warm_instances_activity with the operator-configured num_workers value. The activity body is the existing ARM PATCH on scaleAndConcurrency.alwaysReady. The parent MUST wait for the warm-propagation period to elapse before pool spawn (Â§5.5).

requirement.name: cool_instances_activity invocation in parent orchestrator
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§8.6 (streaming_pipeline_orchestrator_fn): after the pool task_all returns, the parent orchestrator MUST call cool_instances_activity before release_cluster_activity. The cool call PATCHes always_ready back down so the FA is not billed for idle workers between runs.

story.name: Hosting Substrate Selection
story.description: Governs which Azure hosting substrate runs the Pipeline Function App and which Durable Functions storage provider backs it. Per v9 Â§10, the recommended substrate is Azure Container Apps (1 replica minimum, 1 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, scale-to-zero) running Netherite as the Durable Functions storage provider; adoption is conditional on Container Apps run cost remaining at or below the current Flex Consumption baseline (phase-1 dry-run quantifies the actual cost). This story owns the substrate choice, the deploy_architecture target_kind that realizes it, and the cost-parity audit that validates continued use.

requirement.name: Substrate selection is conditional on cost parity
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§10 and Â§14 (open risks): the Pipeline Function App MUST run on the substrate that delivers Netherite throughput per Burckhardt Â§5.1 equation (1) at a total run cost at or below the current Flex Consumption baseline. Adoption of the v9 Â§10 Option C recommendation (Azure Container Apps, 1 replica minimum, scale-to-zero, Netherite) is conditional on cost parity established by the phase-1 dry-run; if parity is not met the substrate decision is revisited.

requirement.name: Adopt Container Apps with Netherite per v9 Â§10 Option C
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§10 Option C: the Pipeline Function App MUST run as a containerized Durable Functions worker on Azure Container Apps with a minimum of 1 replica (1 vCPU, 4 GB RAM) and scale-to-zero when idle. host.json MUST set storageProvider type=Netherite and partitionCount=32. The constant-footprint design fits one replica; Netherite owns all 32 partitions on that single host.

requirement.name: deployment_architecture.json carries a Container Apps target_kind
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§10 and Â§11.0 Phase-1 step: brain/machine_artifacts/content/deployment_architecture.json MUST add a new target_kind for Azure Container Apps and migrate the pipeline deploy target from azure_function_app to the new ACA target_kind. The existing deploy scripts (local_deploy.py, remote_deploy.py) MUST gain a parallel ACA path.

requirement.name: Phase-1 dry-run records minute-billed compute cost
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§10 cost math and Â§16.3: the phase-1 Missouri-spike dry-run MUST record actual minute-billed compute (vCPU-sec, GiB-sec) on Azure Container Apps to the persistent monitoring surface defined by F-102-S-001 Â§16.3. The recorded value is the input to the cost-parity decision in REQ-B-001.

story.name: Data version management
story.description: Any collection in any cluster used by the code might have different versions. The ChatHealthy code must be capable of abstracting the name of a collection so that without changing code different collections with different schemas can be used by the code, as per specific business requirements on a per collection basis.

requirement.name: Provider collection must support versioning
requirement.requirement: The provider collection must be capable of having different versions.

requirement.name: SpecialtyMetaData collection must support versioning
requirement.requirement: The SpecialtyMetaData collection must be capable of having different versions.

requirement.name: All version configurations live in one MongoDB collection, hand-maintained by Claude as SA under human supervision
requirement.requirement: All configurations must be hosted in one MongoDB collection, which must be maintained by hand by Claude as SA and a human actor to supervise.

requirement.name: Gateway is the facade; ChatHealthyJobManager spawns the propagation job
requirement.requirement: The pipeline function ChatHealthyDataPipelinesGatewayFunctionApp must be used as the facade from whence this story is realized. The ChatHealthyJobManager must be the place that spawns the job to propagate the changes configured in the DB.

feature.name: Common Pipeline Orchestration Requirements
feature.description: Shared scaffolding used by every individual pipeline: the orchestration framework and activity contract, base worker classes, common data-source fetching, source-file archive management, source-vs-DB reconciliation, the shared embedding worker, and the pipeline-independence story.

story.name: Durable Orchestration Framework + Activity Contract
story.description: Durable Functions orchestrator + activity contract that every pipeline uses for fan-out, fan-in, status surfacing, and resumability.

requirement.name: Durable Orchestration Framework + Activity Contract
requirement.requirement: Pipelines use Azure Durable Functions; orchestrators and activities follow a single shared contract for invocation, status, and resumability.

requirement.name: Adopt the Netherite four-primitive Durable Functions model
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§1 (Frame of reference: the Netherite white paper): all pipeline orchestrators and entities MUST be expressed in terms of the four Durable Functions primitives the Burckhardt et al. Netherite paper formalizes â€” stateful instances (orchestrations and entities), stateless tasks (activities), work items (orchestrator, entity, activity, timer), and partition-keyed routing. No other concurrency or actor model may be introduced alongside Durable Functions for pipeline work.

requirement.name: Boundary principle: Netherite vs Mongo vs ChatHealthy code
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.6 (Boundary principle): the runtime owns message management (at-least-once delivery, serializable commit, worker dispatch, activity timeouts, instance lifecycle); partitions (durable entities) own in-process state under the runtime's serialization contract; Mongo owns the durable provider record's lifecycle keyed by NPI under UpdateOne($set, upsert=True); ChatHealthy code owns idempotent transit through the runtime, throttle and worker definitions, the straight-through enrichment chain, schema-compliant document emission, and the staging blob write/delete cycle. No responsibility crosses these boundaries.

requirement.name: No application-side retry, claim, release, or in-flight registry
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.7: the design relies on Durable Functions' at-least-once delivery and serializable commit (Burckhardt Â§4.4) for message-level idempotency, and on Mongo UpdateOne($set, upsert=True) keyed on NPI for record-level change management. The pipeline MUST NOT add any application-side retry layer, claim/release protocol, or in-flight record registry on top of these primitives.

requirement.name: No fallbacks, no exception catching, discrepancy report is the failure surface
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.10: per-record failures (normalize rejection, schema violation, external-API failure, bulk_write rejection) MUST be reported via work_manager.report_discrepancy and persisted to PublicHealthData.pipeline_discrepancy_reports plus published to the admin notification channel. No fallback paths and no local exception catching are permitted. A configurable failure threshold (--discrepancy-abort-threshold) drives abnormal termination of the entire workflow when discrepancy_count exceeds the threshold.

requirement.name: Constant runtime footprint is a precondition, not a consequence
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§1 (Burckhardt Â§4.3 'State management' warning) and Â§2 (ten constraints with constant-footprint footnotes): the design MUST keep partition state O(1) per partition, throttle state O(1) per throttle, work-manager state O(pool_size + source_count), and per-worker memory bounded by batch_size Ã— per-record shape. No state shape that grows with the input record count is permitted. The constant-footprint requirement is the precondition for Netherite's group-commit throughput claim (T = B / L) â€” without it, equation (1) does not hold.

requirement.name: REQ 16.1 â€” message-infrastructure cost MUST be instrumented per run
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§16.1: the pipeline MUST emit, per run, the actual count of (a) entity-signal operations the runtime executed, (b) control-queue / partition-message ops driven by the storage provider, and (c) Mongo write ops issued by the worker pool. The expected operating band is the one quoted in Â§12 (legacy ~10,000â€“20,000 HTTP requests against the design's group-committed ~1,000â€“2,000 effective writes). Drift outside that band MUST raise an alert and a follow-up review of the Â§12 amelioration claim.

requirement.name: REQ 16.2 â€” per-record staging blob I/O MUST be instrumented per run
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§16.2: the pipeline MUST emit, per run, the actual storage operation count per processed record on the staging blob path â€” PUT on stage-write, GET on read-back, LIST on assignment-close enumeration, DELETE on post-commit cleanup. The expected operating band is approximately four storage operations per record. Drift above that band MUST raise an alert and a follow-up review of the staging design (the batched-staging-collection alternative becomes viable if per-record ops rise materially).

requirement.name: REQ 16.3 â€” metrics MUST be published to a persistent monitoring surface
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§16.3: REQ 16.1 and REQ 16.2 MUST be backed by a concrete monitoring surface â€” an instrumented metric stream (e.g., Application Insights custom metrics, Log Analytics workspace, or equivalent Azure-native observability sink) that (a) records every run's values, (b) retains them for trend analysis across at least the prior twelve runs, and (c) emits an alert to the operator notification channel when a value crosses the configured threshold. Without this surface Â§16.1 and Â§16.2 cannot be evaluated and the design's cost claims cannot be verified.

story.name: Base Worker Classes
story.description: Shared Python base classes for pipeline workers (load workers, enrichment workers, etc.).

requirement.name: Base Worker Classes
requirement.requirement: All pipeline workers extend a shared base class that handles MongoDB connection, batching, logging, and error reporting.

requirement.name: Workers are end-to-end straight-through; no per-stage fan-out
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.3: one record-processing worker takes one assignment (one Mongo bulk_write batch's worth of records) through every stage in a single pass. Throttles serialize external-API access via async callbacks: the worker requests permission, waits for the callback, makes the call. No per-stage fan-out, no sharded per-stage inboxes, no chained activities per stage.

requirement.name: Workers never die mid-assignment; lifecycle owned by work manager
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.8: workers ask the work manager for the next assignment; the work manager either hands one over or refuses; on refusal the worker returns (dies). Replacement spawn is the work manager's responsibility. Workers age out at approximately 110 minutes â€” the 2-hour Durable activity ceiling minus a 10-minute safety margin. Workers MUST NEVER die mid-assignment.

requirement.name: Record is the message content; record is NOT the message
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.9: records are durable Mongo documents identified by NPI with their own change-management lifecycle. Messages are ephemeral payloads that carry record content between components. The two MUST NOT be conflated. The pipeline_message dataclass that conflates the two in the legacy code is removed per Â§15 (Delete).

story.name: Data-Source Fetching
story.description: In each pipeline, it is likely that new data must be fetched on the internet. It is required that a common HTTP/SFTP/etc. fetch layer with retry, content-hash checking, error management, and content-version tracking be used. Auto-discovery of the source URL is per-source and lives next to the source's fetcher.

requirement.name: Data-Source Fetching
requirement.requirement: All pipelines fetch external source data through a single shared module that handles retries, content-hash checks, and version tracking.

requirement.name: Manage data source freshness
requirement.requirement: Because each data source might be published on different frequencies, it is required that for the pipeline, an array of staleness facts be argued at the user level. This array must include a data source name, and a value of how many days to wait before looking for new data, even if data exists in ChatHealthy.ai's repository. If 0 is the value then one must look for data each time the function is invoked. If any number of days are argued then if the number of days (exactly as per file's time stamp) is exceeded, the file must be gathered again. If a file that should be gathered is not gathered: (1) the old file must be deleted, and (2) the program must abend.

requirement.name: Source-gather workers are short-lived activities, one per source
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.3: source-gather workers are short-lived activities. Each is allocated to gather one source of data; on completion the worker terminates and is garbage-collected by the runtime. The work manager observes the absence on the next stats poll and either spawns a new gather worker for remaining source work or moves the pipeline to seeding the record-processing queue.

requirement.name: Gather activity inventory: nppes_zip, pl_pfile, zip_crosswalk, rucc, specialty_catalog, icd10
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.3: the gather activities for the Provider Pipeline are gather_nppes_zip_activity (fetches NPPES monthly dissemination ZIP into Blob Storage; idempotent on version), gather_pl_pfile_activity (extracts pl_pfile_*.csv from the ZIP and drop-and-recreate-style loads into pipeline_sources_pl_pfile keyed by NPI), gather_zip_crosswalk_activity (loads the HUD ZIP/county crosswalk into pipeline_sources_zip_county_crosswalk), gather_rucc_activity (fetches the USDA RUCC XLSX from the AI-discovered URL into pipeline_sources_rucc), gather_specialty_catalog_activity (copies ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags into pipeline_sources_specialty_catalog), and gather_icd10_activity (existing icd10_loader.py shape preserved).

requirement.name: source-gather concurrency bounded by token_bucket/source_gather throttle
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.2 and Â§5.2: the source-gather sub-orchestrator calls gather_*_activity for each source in parallel up to token_bucket/source_gather's capacity, and returns when the last gather activity completes. The throttle entity carries refill_rate, capacity, tokens, last_refill_at and is the only concurrency knob over the source-gather phase.

requirement.name: AI agent discovers source URLs for NPPES and USDA RUCC
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.3 (gather_rucc_activity 'AI-discovered URL') and the existing F-102-S-003-REQ-T-006 addendum: sources whose canonical URL changes between releases (NPPES NPI dissemination, USDA RUCC XLSX, NUCC taxonomy CSV) MUST identify the correct file by calling an AI agent (Claude Haiku via the Anthropic SDK), not by regex or HTML scraping heuristics in code. There is no fallback URL constant; the fetcher raises and the run fails loudly on agent error per v9 Â§2.10.

requirement.name: Pool spawn is gated on source-gather completion
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.4: the work manager seeds the record-processing queue and spawns record-processing workers ONLY AFTER every source-gather worker has persisted its source into the data partition. pool_size = total âˆ’ 1 work manager âˆ’ N throttles. Source loading is bounded and MUST NOT race with record processing for the same memory budget.

story.name: Source File Storage Management
story.description: Durable storage of every external source file the pipeline has ingested, with version + content-hash, so a pipeline run can be re-played against a specific historical source.

requirement.name: Source File Storage Management
requirement.requirement: Every external source file consumed by any pipeline MUST be archived in Azure Blob Storage with version and content-hash so a load can be replayed against a specific historical source.

requirement.name: Two-places persistence: source-file blob and Mongo provider document
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.6 and Â§3.4: records are persisted in exactly two places by design â€” the canonical source file (NPPES dissemination CSV ingested as a JSON-in-blob representation in Azure Blob Storage, in the provider-data container) and the durable Mongo provider document. No other durable persistence of in-flight record state is permitted. Pre-indexed cross-reference data (pl_pfile, RUCC, ZIP crosswalk, specialty catalog) lives in Mongo collections on the pipeline cluster because random-access lookups by NPI are the dominant read pattern there.

requirement.name: Data partition collections inventory and ownership
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.4: the data partition consists of (a) the NPPES dissemination ZIP and its canonical post-import JSON-in-blob in the provider-data Azure Blob Storage container, (b) {env}_PublicHealthData.pipeline_sources_zip_county_crosswalk, (c) {env}_PublicHealthData.pipeline_sources_pl_pfile, (d) {env}_PublicHealthData.pipeline_sources_rucc, (e) {env}_PublicHealthData.pipeline_sources_specialty_catalog. Each is written once per run by its corresponding source-gather activity. The specialty catalog is read from ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags into a run-local collection for predictability.

requirement.name: Source CSV is byte-offset indexed before any record processing
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§0024 (pre-processing requirement): before any record-processing worker starts, the NPPES dissemination CSV MUST be indexed once so that every record's byte-offset within the file is paired with its NPI. The pre-processing step computes file_size, header_end, and chunk_size and these are the inputs to work_manager.seed() per Â§3.1 state. The work manager holds the assignment queue implicitly (arithmetic, not materialized) and per-record workers receive byte-range assignments (start_byte, end_byte) that align on row boundaries.

requirement.name: Pre-indexing pairs every secondary-source row with its NPI key
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§0025: the same pre-processing pairs each secondary-source row with its NPI key where applicable (pl_pfile, NPPES public-API responses), so every cross-source join at enrichment time is a single Mongo find by NPI on a pre-built index.

story.name: Sourceâ†”DB Reconciliation
story.description: Post-load comparison of the ingested source vs the destination DB collection. Detects missed rows, drift, and (for full-source loads) rows in the DB that are no longer in source.

requirement.name: Sourceâ†”DB Reconciliation
requirement.requirement: After every load, the pipeline MUST reconcile the destination collection against the source file: report rows in source-not-in-DB, rows in DB-not-in-source (when source is a full file: delete), and rows whose field values diverge.

requirement.name: Discrepancy reporter persists per-record failures and publishes notifications
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.8 and Â§13: every component that fails a record (normalize failure, schema validation, bulk_write rejection, external-API failure) MUST signal work_manager.report_discrepancy with the record key (NPI when known, byte offset otherwise) and a controlled reason. The work manager appends one document per call to PublicHealthData.pipeline_discrepancy_reports and publishes one notification per call to the admin notification channel.

requirement.name: Discrepancy threshold drives loud workflow abort
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§13.6: when discrepancy_count exceeds discrepancy_threshold (set per run via --discrepancy-abort-threshold), work_manager.next_assignment MUST begin returning None to every caller. Workers drain naturally; the parent orchestrator's task_all completes with all sub-orchestrations returning {'reason':'drained_or_aged_out'}; the parent surfaces the abort via an explicit 'discrepancy_threshold_exceeded' return value and a final notification.

requirement.name: pipeline_discrepancy_reports indexed on (load_id, reported_at)
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§11.0 Phase-1 provisioning step: {env}_PublicHealthData.pipeline_discrepancy_reports MUST be provisioned with an index on (load_id, reported_at) so that post-run remediation queries scan only the run of interest. The collection is durable and survives the run; operators query it post-run to drive remediation per Â§13.6.

requirement.name: Failed bulk_write at assignment close surfaces and reports
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§13.1: a failed Mongo bulk_write at assignment close MUST propagate out of process_assignment_activity unwrapped. Durable Functions marks the activity invocation failed; the record_worker_orchestrator's call_activity raises; the parent task_all fails; the parent's finally block releases the cluster. Before the parent fails, the worker MUST signal work_manager.report_discrepancy with assignment-id and reason='bulk_write_error'. The previously committed batches are durably in Mongo; a re-run is the only retry.

story.name: Embedding Worker
story.description: Shared embedding-generation worker used by both Provider and Specialty pipelines. Calls OpenAI text-embedding-3-large and writes the embedding vector back to the record.

requirement.name: Embedding Worker
requirement.requirement: A single shared embedding worker generates vector embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-3-large) for any pipeline that needs vector search.

requirement.name: Embedding rate is one token_bucket/openai throttle entity
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.2 (throttle inventory) and Â§6 (embed step): the embedding-generation rate to OpenAI text-embedding-3-large is owned by exactly one throttle entity, token_bucket/openai, whose state is {refill_rate, capacity, tokens, last_refill_at, waiters[]}. The record-processing worker calls _embed via the callback path: request_permission, wait_for_external_event, call OpenAI.

requirement.name: should_embed gating: bad_data and out_of_scope skip embed
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§11.0 (business rules preserved) and Â§6 (per-record flow): the embed step is gated on should_embed(doc). Records with bad_data flagged or out_of_scope flagged MUST skip the embed call. The text passed to OpenAI is render(project(doc)); on success the worker stamps embedding (3072-d vector), embedding_version, embedding_model on the document.

requirement.name: Embedding throttle ceiling is the long pole for national runs
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§12 (throughput model) and Â§14 (open risks): the token_bucket/openai refill_rate is the dominant throughput constraint on full national runs. At 100 tokens/sec and one embed per record, an 8.8M-record run requires approximately 22 hours of embed work. The operator-configurable refill_rate MUST be widened for national-scale runs (paid tier supports several thousand req/sec); separating embedding into its own phase is the alternative path. Pipeline configuration MUST expose --openai-refill-rate so the rate is set per run.

requirement.name: Throttle waiters list capped at pool_size
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§14 (throttle-waiters list growth) and Â§3.2: when pool_size workers park on token_bucket/openai at the same time, the entity carries pool_size waiter entries. The throttle entity MUST cap waiters at pool_size and reject overflow loud (no silent drop). This bounds per-operation serialization cost on the throttle entity.

story.name: Pipelines must be independent of one another
story.description: Every individual pipeline orchestration is 100% independent of every other except that they share BasePipelineOrchestrator. All pipelines enter through a single authenticated URL; each pipeline has a name (the ChatHealthyTask value) and its payload is dispatched accordingly.

requirement.name: Single authenticated entrance URL
requirement.requirement: One client-facing URL with authentication MUST be the only entrance for invoking any pipeline. As implemented, this is the HTTP POST route 'Router' on the function app (DevPipelineManagementService), authenticated via auth.require_auth.

requirement.name: Pipeline named via first positional argument
requirement.requirement: Each pipeline MUST have a name. The pipeline name (the JSON body field 'ChatHealthyTask') MUST be the request's first positional argument and MUST NOT have a default. All other arguments live in the 'payload' object and MUST have defaults â€” depending on the pipeline name the payload shape may vary.

requirement.name: Per-pipeline 100% independence except shared base
requirement.requirement: Each orchestration MUST be 100% independent of each other except that they share a base class. The only legitimate cross-pipeline coupling is BasePipelineOrchestrator (reservation + IDLE wait + try/release). No pipeline orchestrator may yield activities or sub-orchestrators belonging to another pipeline.

requirement.name: Every pipeline shares exactly the v9 Â§2 core pattern
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2 (the core pattern, non-negotiable): every pipeline MUST realize the same ten design constraints â€” partition vs message split (Â§2.1), throttle-entity-only scaling (Â§2.2), straight-through workers (Â§2.3), source-gather-before-pool (Â§2.4), staging-out-on-completion (Â§2.5), the boundary principle (Â§2.6), no application-side retry (Â§2.7), work-manager-owned lifecycle (Â§2.8), record-is-not-message (Â§2.9), no fallbacks and discrepancy as the failure surface (Â§2.10). Per-pipeline independence (REQ-B-003) is realized by each pipeline owning its own parent orchestrator, its own work-manager entity instance, and its own gather activity set â€” but every pipeline shares the Â§2 contract and the shared Durable substrate.

feature.name: Provider Pipeline
feature.description: End-to-end load of the provider record consumed by FindCare. Produces {env}_PublicHealthData.providers on the front-end cluster.

story.name: Manage Provider Pipeline Orchestration Flow
story.description: The end-to-end orchestration that drives the Provider Pipeline: reservation -> health -> load (sub-orchestrator) -> attach_practice_locations -> Pass1 -> Pass2 -> Pass3 -> Pass4 -> Pass6 -> urban_flag -> embeddings + vector index -> reconciliation -> release. Owns the order, the dependency edges, and the failure handling. All orchestration steps are gated by start_step so a resumed run begins at the requested step. Implementation: ProviderPipelineOrchestrator._pipeline_steps in provider_load_manager.py.

requirement.name: Manage Provider Pipeline Orchestration Flow
requirement.requirement: A single durable orchestrator drives the Provider Pipeline through reservation, source fetches, base load, enrichments, embedding generation, reconciliation, and release â€” in that order, with try/finally guarantees on the reservation release.

requirement.name: Provider Pipeline parent orchestrator is streaming_pipeline_orchestrator_fn
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§8.6: the Provider Pipeline parent orchestrator MUST execute the following sequence: call_activity('reserve_cluster_activity'); for each throttle in cfg, call_entity(throttle/<name>, 'configure', params); call_sub_orchestrator('source_gather_orchestrator'); call_activity('get_csv_metadata_activity'); call_entity(work_manager/<load_id>, 'seed', {**meta, **cfg}); call_activity('warm_instances_activity', {'num_workers': cfg['pool_size']}); build pool = [call_sub_orchestrator('record_worker_orchestrator', {**cfg, 'worker_id': wid, 'load_id': load_id}) for wid in range(1, cfg['pool_size']+1)]; task_all(pool); call_activity('cool_instances_activity'); call_activity('release_cluster_activity') in a finally block. Returns {'load_id': load_id}.

requirement.name: Work manager entity state shape and operations
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.1 and Â§8.1: the work manager is a single durable entity instance keyed 'default' or per-load-id. Its state is { config{file_size, header_end, chunk_size, total_chunks, batch_size, discrepancy_threshold}, next_chunk_id, next_worker_id, workers{worker_id: {kind, spawned_at, age_limit_seconds}}, done, discrepancy_count }. worker_id is a monotonically increasing integer the work manager issues at spawn time; the counter starts at 1 and never re-uses a value. Operations: seed(file_meta), next_assignment(worker_id) â†’ assignment|None, ack(chunk_id), spawn_pool(pool_size), spawn_source_gather(sources[]), respawn(worker_id), report_discrepancy(record_key, reason), stats().

requirement.name: Work manager queue is arithmetically derived, not materialized
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.1 (footprint) and Â§8.1 (next_assignment): the work manager MUST NOT materialize the assignment queue. next_assignment computes start=header_end + cid * chunk_size_bytes, end=min(start+chunk_size_bytes, file_size) from the seeded config; total_chunks is (file_size - header_end + chunk_size_bytes - 1) // chunk_size_bytes. The queue footprint is O(1); only the worker roster grows with pool_size.

requirement.name: record_worker_orchestrator_fn loop body
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§8.3: the per-pool-slot sub-orchestration MUST loop: yield context.call_entity(wm, 'next_assignment', {'worker_id': wid}); if the result is None, break; yield context.call_activity('process_assignment_activity', {**cfg, 'assignment': assignment, 'orchestration_instance_id': context.instance_id}); yield context.call_entity(wm, 'ack', {'worker_id': wid}); if context.elapsed_seconds() > cfg['age_limit_seconds'], yield context.call_entity(wm, 'respawn', {'worker_id': wid}) and break. Return {'worker_id': wid, 'reason': 'drained_or_aged_out'}.

requirement.name: process_assignment_activity body â€” straight-through chain
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§8.4: process_assignment_activity MUST execute the full straight-through chain per row in the assigned byte range: stream via _iter_csv_partition; state-filter via _raw_row_matches_state; normalize via normalize_raw_record; _pass1_zip; _pass2_census; _pass3_billing; _pass4_maps; _pass6_nppes; _stamp_urban; _stamp_flags; _mark_quality; if should_embed(doc), _embed; then write one JSON blob per record at pipeline-staging/{load_id}/{assignment_id}/{worker_id}/{npi}.json. On no row does the activity catch or retry locally.

requirement.name: process_assignment_activity commit phase
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§8.4 (commit phase) and Â§3.7: at assignment close, the activity MUST list blobs under its prefix pipeline-staging/{load_id}/{assignment_id}/{worker_id}/, fetch each, parse JSON, build [UpdateOne({'npi': doc['npi']}, {'$set': doc}, upsert=True) for doc in batch], call coll.bulk_write(ops, ordered=False), and delete the staging blobs on success. Failure of bulk_write surfaces loud per v9 Â§13.1 and increments work_manager.discrepancy_count.

requirement.name: Mongo writer is NOT a separate throttle
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.6 and Â§4 (Throttle inventory): Mongo bulk_write batch_size is intentionally NOT a separate throttle entity. batch_size lives on the assignment object the work manager hands out and is a runtime knob on work-manager config (doubleable via code or configuration without redesign). Atlas is the horizontally scalable, idempotent sink under the $set upsert contract; a throttle in front of it would add latency without protecting the service.

requirement.name: Records staged out, never carried in worker memory across batch
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.5: when a record completes its straight-through pass, the worker MUST write it to the staging partition (one JSON blob in Azure Blob Storage), not retain it in in-process memory. When the assignment's batch_size records have all been staged, the worker reads them out of staging, performs ONE Mongo bulk_write of UpdateOne($set, upsert=True) ops, then deletes those records from staging. Staging holds at most pool_size Ã— batch_size records at any moment.

requirement.name: Staging container path layout
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§7: staging is implemented in the provider-staging Azure Blob Storage container on the same storage account that hosts the provider-data container. The blob path MUST be pipeline-staging/{load_id}/{assignment_id}/{worker_id}/{npi}.json where the file contents are the schema-conformant provider document JSON. Blob metadata stamped on write: load_id, assignment_id, worker_id, npi, staged_at (ISO8601). The path is the authoritative key; metadata is informational only.

requirement.name: Staging write/read/delete contract
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§7: workers Put-Blob once per processed record (last-write-wins on the path; staging is not durable). At assignment close, list-blobs under pipeline-staging/{load_id}/{assignment_id}/{worker_id}/ and fetch each. After the providers bulk_write succeeds, delete-blob for each enumerated path (idempotent). The listing returns at most batch_size blobs in steady state.

requirement.name: Staging orphan-safety lifecycle policy
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§7 and Phase-1 provisioning step in Â§11.0: the provider-staging Azure Blob Storage container MUST have a lifecycle-management policy that moves any blob older than 6 hours to deleted state. This is the orphan-safety net for a failed run that leaves staging blobs behind. Operators MAY also issue a bulk delete by previous load_id prefix at the start of a re-run.

requirement.name: Pool size and batch size cap staging footprint
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.5 and Â§7: peak blob count at steady state is pool_size Ã— batch_size. With pool_size=100 and batch_size=5,000 (the design starting point, doubleable at runtime), peak is 500,000 blobs at ~1 KB per record â‰ˆ 500 MB across the cluster â€” a constant, not a function of source size. The lifecycle policy expiry is the safety margin against an orphaned assignment.

requirement.name: Storage Queue is the throttle-callback substrate
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§8.4 (throttle-callback hook) and Â§15 (Create file pipeline/Code/throttle_callback.py): the throttle-callback path MUST use a dedicated Storage Queue listener inside process_assignment_activity to receive grant events from the throttle entities. The orchestrator-mediated alternative is rejected because it inflates orchestration history by one entry per record per throttled call.

requirement.name: Throttle-callback Storage Queue poll cadence
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§14 (open risks â€” throttle-callback shape): the Storage Queue listener inside process_assignment_activity MUST poll at a 200 ms cadence as the design starting cadence. Calibration is permitted; the cadence is the substrate's single knob for trading latency against storage transactions.

requirement.name: Age-out at 110 minutes; respawn issues next monotonic worker_id
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.8, Â§5.7, and Â§8.3: the age limit MUST be 110 minutes (the 2-hour Durable activity ceiling minus a 10-minute safety margin). On age-out the worker signals respawn and returns; the work manager spawns a new sub-orchestration with next_worker_id (a monotonic counter that never re-uses a value) and removes the retired worker from its roster. Pool size stays at the configured invariant.

requirement.name: Configurable CLI flags: --pool-size, --batch-size, --discrepancy-abort-threshold
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§11.0 Phase-1 step on pipeline/run_streaming_pipeline.py: the run_streaming_pipeline entry point MUST accept --pool-size, --batch-size, and --discrepancy-abort-threshold flags as first-class CLI arguments. The throttle parameter contract remains; the legacy --num-workers flag is retained as an alias to --pool-size for one cycle, then removed.

requirement.name: Discrepancy threshold default at the configuration layer
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.10 and Â§8.1 (seed defaulting): the work manager MUST default discrepancy_threshold to a sensible value at seed time when the CLI does not pass one (the Â§8.1 skeleton shows 1000). The default is established at the configuration layer, not hard-coded inside next_assignment.

story.name: NPPES NPI Registry
story.description: Base provider data: the NPPES NPI dissemination file (Type 1 individuals + Type 2 organizations).

requirement.name: NPPES NPI Registry
requirement.requirement: The base provider records come from the NPPES NPI dissemination file (CMS, monthly full + weekly diffs). All other provider data is enrichment on top of this.

requirement.name: NPPES dissemination CSV is the system-of-record blob ingested as JSON-in-blob
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§0014, Â§0024, Â§3.4, Â§11.0: the NPPES monthly dissemination ZIP is the Tier-1 system of record (~8.8M rows per monthly file). Records are keyed by the 10-digit NPI issued by CMS. After gather_nppes_zip_activity ingests the ZIP into Azure Blob Storage, the canonical post-import JSON-in-blob representation is the first of the two persistence places for every record (Mongo being the second).

requirement.name: State filter applies to raw rows before normalization
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (state filter) and Â§11.0: per-record processing MUST drop rows whose NPPES state field does not match the run's states list via _raw_row_matches_state, BEFORE normalize_raw_record runs. This guards normalization cost on out-of-scope rows.

requirement.name: normalize_raw_record mutates raw NPPES into schema-shape
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (Normalize) and Â§9.1: normalize_raw_record MUST mutate the raw NPPES dict into addresses[], licenses[], taxonomies[], other_identifiers[], active[], and the identity fields. The result MUST validate against the shape of ChatHealthyProvidersSchema.json (the schema is the authoritative business-rule artifact per Â§9.1).

requirement.name: Mongo upsert keyed on the 10-digit NPI
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.6, Â§6 (Commit step), Â§11.0 (Mongo upsert key), and Â§8.4: every provider record MUST be written to Mongo as UpdateOne({'npi': doc['npi']}, {'$set': doc}, upsert=True). The NPI is the canonical key for the entire record domain. Mongo absorbs the write idempotently â€” re-runs with updated NPPES data mutate existing documents in place.

story.name: Multi-Address File
story.description: NPPES Practice Locations file (pl_pfile_*.csv). Provides the secondary practice locations for providers who operate at more than one address. Joined into each provider record.

requirement.name: Multi-Address File
requirement.requirement: Provider records MUST include every practice location from the NPPES Practice Locations file (pl_pfile_*.csv), not only the primary address. Consumer queries against practice_address.* MUST match across all locations.

requirement.name: gather_pl_pfile_activity pre-loads pl_pfile keyed by NPI
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.3, Â§0016, and Â§11.0 (Practice-location attach): gather_pl_pfile_activity MUST extract pl_pfile_*.csv from the NPPES ZIP, parse every row into {npi, addresses:[...]}, and drop-and-recreate-style load into {env}_PublicHealthData.pipeline_sources_pl_pfile. The collection is pre-indexed at gather time so per-record lookups during enrichment are O(1).

requirement.name: Per-record worker attaches secondary addresses inline
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§11.0 (Practice-location attach) and Â§14 (open risks): the per-record worker MUST read pipeline_sources_pl_pfile by NPI at normalize time and merge the secondary addresses into addresses[]. The legacy attach_practice_locations Phase B ($merge-based concatenation) is dropped per Â§14; the per-record lookup adds Mongo reads but applies only to the ~5% of providers with secondary addresses.

story.name: County Enrichment
story.description: ZIP-to-county lookup enrichment is performed by a sequence of complementary algorithms; each is tried in turn against the residue of the previous pass until the cumulative match rate clears the 98% SLA. Stamps county.fips, county.name, and county.source onto every practice_address element (and the top-level county back-compat surface from the primary).

requirement.name: County Enrichment
requirement.requirement: Each practice_address element MUST be enriched with county.fips and county.name. The pipeline applies a sequence of complementary algorithms until the cumulative match rate clears 98%, then writes a reconcile report.

requirement.name: Pass 1 â€” HUD ZIP/county crosswalk bulk enrichment
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (Pass 1 ZIP crosswalk), Â§11.0, and Â§0017: for each address, if pipeline_sources_zip_county_crosswalk has a row with res_ratio â‰¥ 0.98 the worker MUST set county = {fips, name, source: 'crosswalk_pass1', zip_ratio}. The HUD USPS ZIP-to-County Crosswalk is the Tier-2 authoritative reference and drives ~77% of addresses on first try.

requirement.name: Pass 2 â€” US Census Geocoder via token_bucket/census
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6, Â§3.2, and Â§11.0: for each address still missing county.fips, the worker MUST call _pass2_census via the token_bucket/census throttle (Census Geocoder API has a documented ~10 requests/sec ceiling). On success set county.source='geocoder_pass2_batch'; on miss set 'geocoder_failed'.

requirement.name: Pass 3 â€” Census billing-address fallback via token_bucket/census
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 and Â§11.0: if the primary practice address is 'geocoder_failed', the worker MUST call _pass3_billing via token_bucket/census against the business address line. On success set county.source='geocoder_pass3_billing'.

requirement.name: Pass 4 â€” Google Maps Geocoding via token_bucket/google_maps
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6, Â§3.2, and Â§11.0: if still failed and Google Maps is enabled, the worker MUST call _pass4_maps via token_bucket/google_maps. Resolve returned county name to FIPS via the crosswalk-derived lookup. Set 'geocoder_pass4_maps' on success or 'geocoder_pass5_maps_billing' on billing-address resolution. Google Maps is paid; the throttle is a cost knob.

requirement.name: Pass 6 â€” NPPES public API via token_bucket/nppes
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6, Â§3.2, and Â§11.0: last resort, the worker MUST call _pass6_nppes via token_bucket/nppes (~5 requests/sec per IP per CMS documentation). Fetch the canonical address by NPI from the CMS registry and retry the ZIP crosswalk against that address. Set county.source='geocoder_pass6_nppes' on success.

requirement.name: ZIP/state mismatch repair from license data
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§11.0 (ZIP/state-mismatch repair from license data): single license match repairs the address; multiple licenses sets bad_data.reason='zip_state_mismatch_multiple_licenses'; no license sets 'zip_state_mismatch_no_license'; license doesn't resolve sets 'zip_state_mismatch'.

requirement.name: Bad-data and out-of-scope flag values
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (_mark_quality) and Â§11.0: the worker MUST set bad_data = {flagged: true, reason: 'no_address'} or {flagged: true, reason: 'zip_state_mismatch'}; and out_of_scope = {flagged: true, reason: 'foreign_provider'} or {flagged: true, reason: 'deactivated'} per the legacy rules. These flags drive should_embed() and search exclusion downstream.

story.name: Urban Classification
story.description: Urban/rural classification stamped onto provider county data using the Census 2020_UA_COUNTY workbook (percent-urban-population thresholding).

requirement.name: Urban Classification
requirement.requirement: Each enriched practice_address county MUST be flagged urban=true/false based on the Census Bureau urbanization percentage for that county.

requirement.name: Urban flag stamped via pipeline_sources_rucc by FIPS
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (Urban flag), Â§3.4, and Â§11.0: for each address with county.fips set and state matching the run scope, the worker MUST look up pipeline_sources_rucc by FIPS and set addresses[i].county.urban = bool. The source is the USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes (RUCC) XLSX, ingested once per run by gather_rucc_activity into pipeline_sources_rucc as FIPS â†’ {urban: bool}.

story.name: Provider Embeddings
story.description: Vector embeddings of provider records (text-embedding-3-large) for similarity search.

requirement.name: Provider Embeddings
requirement.requirement: Each provider record MUST carry an OpenAI text-embedding-3-large vector embedding and the embedding_model + embedding_version fields for re-embed gating.

requirement.name: Embedding stamped via OpenAI text-embedding-3-large
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (Embed) and Â§11.0 (Embedding): provider records that pass should_embed MUST be stamped with embedding (3072-d vector), embedding_version, and embedding_model fields. The text passed to OpenAI is text = render(project(doc)). The call MUST go through token_bucket/openai per F-102-S-006.

story.name: Provider Proprietary Flag Enrichment
story.description: Stamps the proprietary flags can_prescribe and is_homeopathic on every provider record, derived from the F-105 single-source-of-truth catalog using the provider's primary taxonomy code. Source-of-truth for the catalog is feature EPIC-010-F-105 (the JSON file in findcarestorage/chathealthy-public-data/enrichment_content/specialty_classification_gpt41.json).

requirement.name: Provider can_prescribe flag from F-105 catalog
requirement.requirement: Every provider record MUST carry can_prescribe (boolean) derived from the F-105 catalog using the provider's primary taxonomy code (or first taxonomy if no primary). Organizations (entity_type_code='2') MUST be stamped can_prescribe=false regardless of taxonomy. Catalog source: EPIC-010-F-105.

requirement.name: Provider is_homeopathic flag from F-105 catalog
requirement.requirement: Every provider record MUST carry is_homeopathic (boolean) derived from the F-105 catalog using the provider's primary taxonomy code (or first taxonomy if no primary). Organizations (entity_type_code='2') MUST be stamped is_homeopathic=false. Catalog source: EPIC-010-F-105.

requirement.name: _stamp_flags reads pipeline_sources_specialty_catalog by primary taxonomy code
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (Provider flags) and Â§11.0 (Provider flags): the worker MUST call _stamp_flags which reads pipeline_sources_specialty_catalog by the record's primary taxonomy code and stamps can_prescribe, is_homeopathic, and is_disqualified on the document. The catalog itself lives in ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags per Â§3.4.

requirement.name: entity_type_code='2' short-circuits all three provider flags to false
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§11.0 (Entity-type short-circuit): if entity_type_code == '2' (organization), the worker MUST force can_prescribe=false, is_homeopathic=false, and is_disqualified=false regardless of what the catalog returns. Organizations are never prescribers, never homeopathic, and never disqualified by taxonomy.

story.name: Provider Normative Schema
story.description: Provider records produced by this pipeline conform to a normative JSON Schema published at chathealthy.ai/schemas/. This is a documentary contract â€” the pipeline does NOT validate records against it at runtime. Consumers of the providers collection rely on the schema as the source of truth for the record shape.

requirement.name: Provider normative schema URL
requirement.requirement: Provider records MUST conform to the normative schema published at https://chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyProvidersSchema.json (filesystem source Website/schemas/ChatHealthyProvidersSchema.json). The pipeline does not validate against this schema at runtime; the schema is the contract between the pipeline and any downstream consumer.

requirement.name: ChatHealthyProvidersSchema.json is the authoritative business-rule artifact
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§9.1: ChatHealthyProvidersSchema.json is the single authoritative business-rule artifact for the provider record. Stakeholder review of the business rules preserved by the migration is a review of this schema, which is self-documented through the non-normative description on every field. The canonical published location is https://{env}.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyProvidersSchema.json (filesystem source Website/schemas/ChatHealthyProvidersSchema.json). The schema is referenced, not duplicated, in technical design so it remains the single source of truth and cannot drift.

requirement.name: Every emitted provider document MUST validate against the schema
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.6 (boundary principle) and Â§11.0 (Schema compliance): every document emitted at the staging-write boundary MUST validate against ChatHealthyProvidersSchema.json. Mongo $jsonSchema rejection at bulk_write is the enforcement boundary; a rejection becomes a discrepancy per Â§13.1.

feature.name: Specialty Pipeline
feature.description: End-to-end load of the specialty record consumed by FindCare. Produces {env}_PublicHealthData.SpecialtyMetaData on the front-end cluster.

story.name: Manage Specialty Pipeline Orchestration Flow
story.description: The end-to-end orchestration that drives the Specialty Pipeline: reservation -> health -> load_specialty_data (sync sub-step internally fetches NUCC, stores blob, loads MongoDB, generates embeddings, enriches flags) -> release. Implementation: SpecialtyPipelineOrchestrator._pipeline_steps in load_specialty_data.py.

requirement.name: Manage Specialty Pipeline Orchestration Flow
requirement.requirement: A single durable orchestrator drives the Specialty Pipeline through reservation, source fetch, base load, embedding generation, flag enrichment, and release â€” in that order, with try/finally on the release.

requirement.name: Specialty Pipeline parent orchestrator shares the v9 Â§2 core pattern
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2 (the core pattern applies to every pipeline) and Â§8.6: the Specialty Pipeline parent orchestrator MUST realize the same wakeup â†’ throttle-configure â†’ source-gather â†’ seed â†’ warm â†’ pool â†’ cool â†’ release sequence as the Provider Pipeline, with its own work-manager entity instance and its own gather activity set. The orchestrator MUST own a finally block that calls release_cluster_activity per v9 Â§13.1.

story.name: NUCC Provider Taxonomy CSV
story.description: Base specialty data: the NUCC Provider Taxonomy CSV (Code + Display Name + Classification + Grouping + Specialization + Definition + Notes + Section).

requirement.name: NUCC Provider Taxonomy CSV
requirement.requirement: The base specialty records come from the NUCC Provider Taxonomy CSV. All other specialty fields are enrichment on top of this.

requirement.name: gather_nucc_activity follows the source-gather contract
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.3 and Â§2.4: the NUCC Provider Taxonomy CSV gather MUST be implemented as a short-lived activity in the source-gather phase, following the same contract as the Provider Pipeline gather activities (idempotent on version, drop-and-recreate-style load into its source collection, throttled by token_bucket/source_gather). The activity MUST discover the canonical URL via the AI-agent path per F-102-S-003-REQ-T-AI.

story.name: Specialty Embeddings
story.description: Vector embeddings of specialty records (text-embedding-3-large) for similarity search.

requirement.name: Specialty Embeddings
requirement.requirement: Each specialty record MUST carry an OpenAI text-embedding-3-large vector embedding and the embedding_model + embedding_version fields.

requirement.name: Specialty embeddings share the F-102-S-006 throttle and gating
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§2.2 (one throttle per scale parameter) and Â§3.2: specialty embeddings MUST use the same token_bucket/openai throttle entity instance as provider embeddings â€” there is ONE OpenAI rate budget per environment, not one per pipeline. The embedding text projection differs per record class but the throttle, model, and version constants are shared.

story.name: Specialty Proprietary Flag Enrichment
story.description: Stamps the proprietary flags can_prescribe and is_homeopathic on every SpecialtyMetaData record using the same F-105 single-source-of-truth catalog the provider pipeline uses. Source-of-truth: feature EPIC-010-F-105.

requirement.name: Specialty can_prescribe flag from F-105 catalog
requirement.requirement: Every SpecialtyMetaData record MUST carry can_prescribe (boolean) from the F-105 catalog keyed on the record's Code. Catalog source: EPIC-010-F-105.

requirement.name: Specialty is_homeopathic flag from F-105 catalog
requirement.requirement: Every SpecialtyMetaData record MUST carry is_homeopathic (boolean) from the F-105 catalog keyed on the record's Code. Catalog source: EPIC-010-F-105.

requirement.name: enrich_specialty_flags reads the shared catalog
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§3.4 (specialty catalog) and Â§11.0 (Provider flags, shared catalog): specialty-side flag enrichment MUST read from the same pipeline_sources_specialty_catalog the provider _stamp_flags reads. The catalog is populated once per run by gather_specialty_catalog_activity from ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags. Hard-coded taxonomy classifications in pipeline code are forbidden per F-105-S-001-REQ-B-001.

story.name: Specialty Normative Schema
story.description: SpecialtyMetaData records produced by this pipeline conform to a normative JSON Schema published at chathealthy.ai/schemas/. This is a documentary contract â€” the pipeline does NOT validate records against it at runtime.

requirement.name: Specialty normative schema URL
requirement.requirement: SpecialtyMetaData records MUST conform to the normative schema published at https://chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthySpecialtyMetaDataSchema.json. As of 2026-05-22 this schema file does NOT exist at Website/schemas/ â€” operator decision needed: either (a) author and publish Website/schemas/ChatHealthySpecialtyMetaDataSchema.json so the URL resolves, or (b) point this requirement at a different filename and update this REQ-B to match. The pipeline does not validate against this schema at runtime.

feature.name: Proprietary Provider and Specialty Flags
feature.description: ChatHealthy-maintained classification flags applied to both provider records and specialty records. The catalog is a single JSON file in Azure Blob Storage at findcarestorage/chathealthy-public-data/enrichment_content/specialty_classification_gpt41.json that maps each NUCC code to two booleans. Both the Provider Pipeline (F-103-S-007) and the Specialty Pipeline (F-104-S-004) consume this catalog.

story.name: Maintain One Source of Truth
story.description: The classification catalog lives in exactly one blob (findcarestorage/chathealthy-public-data/enrichment_content/specialty_classification_gpt41.json). Both pipelines load from this one blob. No code-baked prefix tables.

requirement.name: Maintain One Source of Truth
requirement.requirement: The can_prescribe and is_homeopathic NUCC-code classifications MUST be sourced from a single MongoDB collection consumed by both pipelines. Hardcoded taxonomy classifications in pipeline code are forbidden.

requirement.name: Catalog lives in ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§0019 and Â§3.4: the proprietary NUCC code â†’ {can_prescribe, is_homeopathic, is_disqualified} catalog lives in ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags. It is a curated allow/deny list (see BUG-005). At run time the pipeline copies the catalog into the run-local collection pipeline_sources_specialty_catalog for predictability; the ProprietaryData collection itself is the source of truth.

requirement.name: Catalog read shape: NUCC taxonomy code â†’ three booleans
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§0019: the catalog read shape MUST be a lookup keyed on the NUCC taxonomy code returning the three booleans {can_prescribe, is_homeopathic, is_disqualified}. is_disqualified is a third flag introduced by v9 alongside the existing can_prescribe and is_homeopathic; F-105 stories S-002 and S-003 cover the first two, and the catalog must carry all three regardless.

story.name: can_prescribe
story.description: Per-NUCC-code can_prescribe boolean. Applied to specialty records AND denormalized onto provider records based on the provider's primary taxonomy code.

requirement.name: can_prescribe
requirement.requirement: Each specialty record MUST carry can_prescribe (boolean) from the catalog. Each provider record MUST carry can_prescribe derived from its primary taxonomy code via the same catalog.

requirement.name: can_prescribe is stamped by _stamp_flags via the catalog
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (Provider flags) and Â§11.0: can_prescribe is stamped on every provider record by _stamp_flags inside process_assignment_activity, using the primary taxonomy code as the catalog key. entity_type_code='2' short-circuits to false per F-103-S-007-REQ-T-entity_type.

story.name: is_homeopathic
story.description: Per-NUCC-code is_homeopathic boolean. Applied to specialty records AND denormalized onto provider records based on the provider's primary taxonomy code.

requirement.name: is_homeopathic
requirement.requirement: Each specialty record MUST carry is_homeopathic (boolean) from the catalog. Each provider record MUST carry is_homeopathic derived from its primary taxonomy code via the same catalog.

requirement.name: is_homeopathic is stamped by _stamp_flags via the catalog
requirement.requirement: Per v9 Â§6 (Provider flags) and Â§11.0: is_homeopathic is stamped on every provider record by _stamp_flags inside process_assignment_activity, using the primary taxonomy code as the catalog key. entity_type_code='2' short-circuits to false.
